knowledge_statements.scope_note: Only the unambiguous Fréchet-differentiability formula is retained. The stated strong two-point limit is not promoted because it lets only \(\|u-v\|\to0\) and does not specify that both points approach \(x\); read literally, it is not the standard local definition of strong Fréchet differentiability at \(x\).
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(D\subseteq\mathbb{R}^n\), \(F:D\to\mathbb{R}^m\), and \(x\in D\). The mapping \(F\) is Fréchet differentiable at \(x\) with derivative \(F'(x)\) when
\[
F(x+d)-F(x)=F'(x)d+o(\|d\|)
\]
as \(d\to0\) through increments satisfying \(x+d\in D\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A mapping is Fréchet differentiable at x when its increment equals a linear derivative applied to the increment plus an error negligible relative to the increment norm. The extract's strong two-point clause is omitted because its limiting localization at x is missing.

children.title: Bouligand Differential Models
children.top_down_role: Limiting derivative models based on nearby differentiability points.

knowledge_statements.title: Bouligand Differential Models
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite-dimensional limiting-Jacobian definition for locally Lipschitz mappings on open domains.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(U\subset\mathbb R^n\) be open, let \(F:U\to\mathbb R^m\) be locally Lipschitz near \(x\in U\), and let \(D_F\subset U\) be the set where \(F\) is Fréchet differentiable. The Bouligand differential of \(F\) at \(x\) is
\[\partial_BF(x):=\left\{A\in\mathbb R^{m\times n}:\exists\,x_k\in D_F,\ x_k\to x,\ F'(x_k)\to A\right\}.\]
Rademacher's theorem ensures that differentiability points occur almost everywhere near \(x\). The displayed set contains precisely the attainable limiting Jacobians and need not be convex.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The Bouligand differential consists of all matrices obtained as limits of ordinary Jacobians at differentiability points approaching the point of interest.
assumptions_latex: \(U\subset\mathbb R^n\) is open, \(x\in U\), and \(F:U\to\mathbb R^m\) is locally Lipschitz near \(x\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\partial_BF(x)\) is the collection of all limiting classical Jacobians along differentiability points approaching \(x\).

notation.meaning: set of points at which F is Fréchet differentiable
Bouligand differential of F at x

children.title: Clarke Generalized-Jacobian Models
children.top_down_role: Convexified generalized-Jacobian models for locally Lipschitz mappings.

knowledge_statements.title: Clarke Generalized-Jacobian Models
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite-dimensional convexified generalized Jacobian for a locally Lipschitz mapping on an open domain.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(U\subset\mathbb R^n\) be open and let \(F:U\to\mathbb R^m\) be locally Lipschitz near \(x\in U\). The Clarke generalized Jacobian of \(F\) at \(x\) is
\[\partial_CF(x):=\operatorname{co}\bigl(\partial_BF(x)\bigr).\]
Equivalently, it is the convex hull of all limits \(A=\lim_{k\to\infty}F'(x_k)\) obtained from differentiability points \(x_k\to x\). In finite dimensions, \(\partial_CF(x)\) is nonempty, compact, and convex.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The Clarke generalized Jacobian is the convex hull of all limiting Jacobians in the Bouligand differential; in finite dimensions it is nonempty, compact, and convex.
assumptions_latex: \(U\subset\mathbb R^n\) is open, \(x\in U\), and \(F:U\to\mathbb R^m\) is locally Lipschitz near \(x\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\partial_CF(x)=\operatorname{co}(\partial_BF(x))\) is a nonempty compact convex set of generalized Jacobians.

notation.meaning: Bouligand differential of F at x
Clarke generalized Jacobian of F at x

children.title: Newton-Derivative Models
children.top_down_role: Newton-facing derivative representations for nonsmooth operator equations.

assumptions_latex: \(X,Y\) are Banach spaces, \(U\subset X\) is open, and \(F:U\to Y\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(G\) is a Newton derivative of \(F\) at \(x\) exactly when its shifted linearization has residual \(o(\lVert h\rVert_X)\).

notation.meaning: bounded linear operators from X to Y

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Shifted-evaluation convention for Newton derivatives on Banach spaces.

source_refs.source_title: Finite-Dimensional Variational Inequalities and Complementarity Problems, Vol. II

knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
A mapping \(G:U\to\mathcal L(X,Y)\) is a Newton derivative of \(F\) at \(x\in U\) if
\[\lim_{\substack{h\to0\\h\ne0}}\frac{\lVert F(x+h)-F(x)-G(x+h)h\rVert_Y}{\lVert h\rVert_X}=0.\]
The operator used for the increment \(h\) is evaluated at the trial point \(x+h\), and neither uniqueness nor continuity of \(G\) is included in the definition.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A Newton derivative is an operator-valued model, evaluated at the trial point, whose linearization error is little-o of the step norm.
knowledge_statements.title: Newton-Derivative Models

source_witnesses.source_title: Finite-Dimensional Variational Inequalities and Complementarity Problems, Vol. II

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The shifted-residual definition is mathematically coherent and fits the leaf, but the cited finite-dimensional source has not been shown to support this Banach-space formulation or this exact convention for the term Newton derivative.

children.title: Slant-Derivative Models
children.top_down_role: Slant-based local models used in nonsmooth Newton analysis.

assumptions_latex: \(X,Y\) are Banach spaces, \(U\subset X\) is open, and \(F:U\to Y\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(S\) is a slanting function at \(x\) when \(F(x+h)-F(x)-S(x+h)h=o(\lVert h\rVert_X)\).

notation.meaning: bounded linear operators from X to Y

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Pointwise slant differentiability under the shifted-operator convention.

source_refs.source_title: Finite-Dimensional Variational Inequalities and Complementarity Problems, Vol. II

knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
A mapping \(S:U\to\mathcal L(X,Y)\) is a slanting function for \(F\) at \(x\in U\), and \(F\) is slantly differentiable there, if
\[F(x+h)-F(x)-S(x+h)h=o(\lVert h\rVert_X)\quad\text{as }h\to0.\]
Equivalently, the norm of the displayed residual divided by \(\lVert h\rVert_X\) tends to zero. The model need not be a classical derivative or be uniquely determined.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A slant derivative supplies shifted linear operators whose approximation residual is negligible relative to the step norm.
knowledge_statements.title: Slant-Derivative Models

source_witnesses.source_title: Finite-Dimensional Variational Inequalities and Complementarity Problems, Vol. II

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: Slant differentiability has author-dependent boundedness and neighborhood requirements. The cited source has not been inspected sufficiently to validate the stated Banach-space, pointwise shifted-operator convention.

children.title: Derivative-Model Correspondence
children.top_down_role: Structural correspondences between Newton-derivative and slant-derivative viewpoints.

assumptions_latex: The Newton and slant models use the same shifted-evaluation convention on Banach spaces.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: A mapping \(G\) is a Newton derivative at \(x\) if and only if it is a slanting function at \(x\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Equivalence is asserted only for the displayed shifted-operator definitions.

source_refs.source_title: Finite-Dimensional Variational Inequalities and Complementarity Problems, Vol. II

knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Under the convention that both models are mappings \(G:U\to\mathcal L(X,Y)\) evaluated at \(x+h\), the Newton-derivative and slant-derivative predicates coincide:
\[G\text{ is a Newton derivative of }F\text{ at }x\quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad G\text{ is a slanting function for }F\text{ at }x,\]
because each predicate is precisely
\[\lVert F(x+h)-F(x)-G(x+h)h\rVert_Y=o(\lVert h\rVert_X).\]
Terminologies imposing additional boundedness or neighborhood-uniformity conditions require those conditions separately.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: With identical shifted-evaluation conventions, Newton derivatives and slant derivatives are the same first-order approximation model.
knowledge_statements.title: Derivative-Model Correspondence

source_witnesses.source_title: Finite-Dimensional Variational Inequalities and Complementarity Problems, Vol. II

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The equivalence is tautologically correct for the two displayed residual definitions, and property is the proper content kind, but source evidence is required that the named Newton and slant notions use exactly those conventions without additional hypotheses.

children.title: Operator-Equation Regimes
children.top_down_role: Finite-dimensional and function-space settings where these models organize Newton systems.

assumptions_latex: \(X,Y\) are Banach spaces, \(F:U\subset X\to Y\), and \(G:U\to\mathcal L(X,Y)\) is a chosen Newton derivative.
Each selected \(G(x_k)\) is continuously invertible whenever an update is taken.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The iteration outputs an approximate solution of the operator equation \(F(x)=0\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Undamped Newton iteration for Banach-space operator equations.

source_refs.source_title: Finite-Dimensional Variational Inequalities and Complementarity Problems, Vol. II

knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Given \(x_0\in U\) and a tolerance \(\varepsilon\ge0\), for \(k=0,1,\ldots\), stop and output \(x_k\) when \(\lVert F(x_k)\rVert_Y\le\varepsilon\). Otherwise solve the bounded linear operator equation
\[G(x_k)s_k=-F(x_k)\]
for \(s_k\in X\), and set
\[x_{k+1}=x_k+s_k.\]
If the linear equation is insoluble, the selected operator is noninvertible, or \(x_k+s_k\notin U\), the undamped scheme declares failure unless a separate globalization or regularization rule is supplied.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: At each step, solve the Newton-derivative linear equation and add its solution until the operator residual meets tolerance.
knowledge_statements.title: Operator-Equation Regimes

source_witnesses.source_title: Finite-Dimensional Variational Inequalities and Complementarity Problems, Vol. II

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The algorithm fits an operator-equation leaf, but a finite-dimensional citation does not establish the Banach-space formulation. Moreover, invertibility should mean bounded invertibility, and the conclusion incorrectly suggests that the undamped iteration necessarily outputs an approximate solution despite possible failure, divergence, or nontermination.

children.title: Linear Newton Approximation Schemes
children.top_down_role: Abstract local approximation families broader than a single generalized differential.

assumptions_latex: \(F:U\subset\mathbb R^n\to\mathbb R^m\), and \(\mathcal A(z)\subset\mathbb R^{m\times n}\) is nonempty near \(x\in U\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\mathcal A\) is a linear Newton approximation at \(x\) when its worst shifted linearization residual is \(o(\lVert h\rVert)\).

notation.meaning: family of admissible linear approximation matrices at z

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite-dimensional, set-valued shifted linear approximation model.

source_refs.source_title: Finite-Dimensional Variational Inequalities and Complementarity Problems, Vol. II

knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Define
\[r_x(h):=\sup_{A\in\mathcal A(x+h)}\lVert F(x+h)-F(x)-Ah\rVert.\]
The family \(\mathcal A\) is a linear Newton approximation scheme for \(F\) at \(x\) if \(r_x(h)=o(\lVert h\rVert)\) as \(h\to0\), with \(x+h\in U\). Thus every matrix admitted at the shifted point supplies a first-order model; a single-valued Newton derivative is recovered when each \(\mathcal A(z)\) is a singleton.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A linear Newton approximation is a matrix family whose worst admissible shifted linearization error is little-o of the step.
knowledge_statements.title: Linear Newton Approximation Schemes

source_witnesses.source_title: Finite-Dimensional Variational Inequalities and Complementarity Problems, Vol. II

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The exact definition of a linear Newton approximation scheme may require compact-valuedness, local boundedness, or semicontinuity in addition to the residual condition. Full-text inspection is needed before determining whether the supplied worst-case formulation and hypotheses match the cited source.

children.title: Semismooth Mapping Classes
children.top_down_role: Mapping classes that distinguish the principal local convergence regimes.

children.title: Semismooth Maps
children.top_down_role: The basic finite-dimensional semismooth mapping class.

assumptions_latex: \(F:U\subset\mathbb R^n\to\mathbb R^m\) is locally Lipschitz near \(x\in U\) and directionally differentiable at \(x\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(F\) is semismooth at \(x\) when every nearby Clarke-Jacobian linearization has residual \(o(\lVert h\rVert)\).

notation.meaning: directional derivative of F at x in direction h

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Standard finite-dimensional Clarke-Jacobian characterization.

source_refs.source_title: Finite-Dimensional Variational Inequalities and Complementarity Problems, Vol. II

knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
The mapping \(F\) is semismooth at \(x\) if it is directionally differentiable there and, for every sequence \(h_k\to0\) with \(x+h_k\in U\) and every choice \(V_k\in\partial_CF(x+h_k)\),
\[F(x+h_k)-F(x)-V_kh_k=o(\lVert h_k\rVert).\]
Equivalently,
\[\sup_{V\in\partial_CF(x+h)}\lVert F(x+h)-F(x)-Vh\rVert=o(\lVert h\rVert).\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A locally Lipschitz directional map is semismooth when all nearby Clarke-Jacobian models have first-order negligible residual.
knowledge_statements.title: Semismooth Maps

source_witnesses.source_title: Finite-Dimensional Variational Inequalities and Complementarity Problems, Vol. II

children.title: Strongly Semismooth Maps
children.top_down_role: The stronger approximation class associated with quadratic local behavior.

assumptions_latex: \(F:U\subset\mathbb R^n\to\mathbb R^m\) is locally Lipschitz near \(x\in U\) and directionally differentiable at \(x\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(F\) is strongly semismooth at \(x\) when the generalized-Jacobian residual is \(O(\lVert h\rVert^2)\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite-dimensional quadratic-residual definition.

source_refs.source_title: Finite-Dimensional Variational Inequalities and Complementarity Problems, Vol. II

knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
The mapping \(F\) is strongly semismooth at \(x\) if it is directionally differentiable there and there exist \(C,\delta>0\) such that, whenever \(0<\lVert h\rVert<\delta\), \(x+h\in U\), and \(V\in\partial_CF(x+h)\),
\[\lVert F(x+h)-F(x)-Vh\rVert\le C\lVert h\rVert^2.\]
Thus strong semismoothness strengthens the little-order residual required by ordinary semismoothness to a uniform quadratic bound.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Strong semismoothness requires every nearby generalized-Jacobian model to have a uniformly quadratic residual.
knowledge_statements.title: Strongly Semismooth Maps

source_witnesses.source_title: Finite-Dimensional Variational Inequalities and Complementarity Problems, Vol. II

children.title: Higher-Order Semismoothness
children.top_down_role: Semismoothness classes indexed by refined approximation orders.

assumptions_latex: \(F:U\subset\mathbb R^n\to\mathbb R^m\) is locally Lipschitz near \(x\in U\) and directionally differentiable at \(x\).
The order parameter satisfies \(0<\alpha\le1\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Order-\(\alpha\) semismoothness means the generalized-Jacobian residual is \(O(\lVert h\rVert^{1+\alpha})\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Hölder-order refinement with \(0<\alpha\le1\).

source_refs.source_title: Finite-Dimensional Variational Inequalities and Complementarity Problems, Vol. II

knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
The mapping \(F\) is semismooth of order \(\alpha\) at \(x\) if there exist \(C,\delta>0\) such that, for every \(h\) satisfying \(0<\lVert h\rVert<\delta\) and \(x+h\in U\), and every \(V\in\partial_CF(x+h)\),
\[\lVert F(x+h)-F(x)-Vh\rVert\le C\lVert h\rVert^{1+\alpha}.\]
The endpoint \(\alpha=1\) is strong semismoothness; any \(\alpha>0\) implies ordinary semismoothness.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Order-alpha semismoothness bounds generalized-Jacobian approximation errors by the step norm raised to one plus alpha.
knowledge_statements.title: Higher-Order Semismoothness

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Strong Fréchet differentiability and order-p semismoothness
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Two local regularity conditions implying semismoothness, including the refined order-p class.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
The Fréchet derivative F'(x) is strong if
\[
\lim_{\substack{y\to x,\ z\to x\\y\ne z}}
\frac{F(z)-F(y)-F'(x)(z-y)}{\|z-y\|}=0.
\]
For 0<p\le 1, F is p-order semismooth at x if, uniformly for V\in\partial F(x+h) as h\to0,
\[
Vh-F'(x;h)=O(\|h\|^{1+p}).
\]
Strong Fréchet differentiability implies semismoothness, and p-order semismoothness implies semismoothness.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A strong Fréchet derivative supplies a uniform two-point first-order approximation near the base point. Order-p semismoothness requires every nearby generalized-Jacobian linearization to approximate the directional derivative with error of order 1+p. Each condition implies ordinary semismoothness.
assumptions_latex: F\text{ is Fréchet differentiable at }x\text{ for the strong-derivative definition}
F\text{ is locally Lipschitz and directionally differentiable at }x\text{ for }p\text{-order semismoothness}
0<p\le1
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: F'(x)\text{ strong}\Rightarrow F\text{ is semismooth at }x,\qquad F\text{ p-order semismooth at }x\Rightarrow F\text{ is semismooth at }x.

children.title: SC1 Maps
children.top_down_role: SC1 mapping structures relevant to semismooth Newton models.

assumptions_latex: \(F:U\subset\mathbb R^n\to\mathbb R^m\) is continuously differentiable on an open set \(U\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(F\) is an \(SC^1\) map when its Jacobian mapping \(F'\) is semismooth.

notation.meaning: Jacobian mapping from U into matrices

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Provisional semismooth-Jacobian interpretation of \(SC^1\).
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Under the semismooth-Jacobian convention, a mapping \(F:U\to\mathbb R^m\) is of class \(SC^1\) if \(F\) is continuously differentiable and the Jacobian mapping
\[F':U\to\mathbb R^{m\times n}\]
is semismooth, with the matrix space equipped with any fixed norm. Equivalently, \(F'\) is locally Lipschitz, directionally differentiable, and satisfies the semismooth generalized-Jacobian residual condition at each point under consideration.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Under one standard convention, an SC1 map is continuously differentiable and has a semismooth Jacobian mapping.
knowledge_statements.title: SC1 Maps

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: No citation is supplied, and the meaning of SC1 is author-dependent. A source is required to establish that this leaf intends continuously differentiable mappings with semismooth Jacobian mappings and to verify any local Lipschitz or directional-differentiability requirements.

children.title: Piecewise-Smooth Maps
children.top_down_role: Maps assembled from locally smooth selections.

knowledge_statements.title: Piecewise-Smooth Maps
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite-selection local definition of continuous piecewise-C1 mappings.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(U\subset\mathbb R^n\) be open and let \(F:U\to\mathbb R^m\). The mapping \(F\) is locally piecewise \(C^1\) at \(x\in U\) if there exist a neighborhood \(V\subset U\) of \(x\) and finitely many \(C^1\) mappings \(F_i:V\to\mathbb R^m\), indexed by \(i=1,\ldots,q\), such that \(F\) is continuous on \(V\) and
\[F(z)\in\{F_1(z),\ldots,F_q(z)\}\quad\text{for every }z\in V.\]
The active selection set is
\[I(z):=\{i\in\{1,\ldots,q\}:F(z)=F_i(z)\},\]
and it is nonempty for every \(z\in V\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A locally piecewise-smooth map is continuous and locally equals one of finitely many continuously differentiable selection functions at every point.
assumptions_latex: \(U\subset\mathbb R^n\) is open, \(F:U\to\mathbb R^m\), and \(x\in U\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(F\) is locally piecewise \(C^1\) at \(x\) when it is continuous near \(x\) and finitely many local \(C^1\) selection functions cover its values there.

notation.meaning: finite family of local continuously differentiable selection functions

children.title: Selection-Function Geometry
children.top_down_role: Geometry induced by competing smooth selections.

knowledge_statements.title: Selection-Function Geometry
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Local finite-selection representation of a piecewise-smooth mapping and its generalized Jacobians.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(U\subseteq\mathbb{R}^n\) be open, let \(F:U\to\mathbb{R}^m\) be locally Lipschitz, and let \(V\subseteq U\) be an open neighborhood on which there are finitely many continuously differentiable selections \(F_i:V\to\mathbb{R}^m\). Define \(\Omega_i=\{y\in V:F(y)=F_i(y)\}\), and assume \(V=\bigcup_i\operatorname{cl}_V(\operatorname{int}_V\Omega_i)\). For each \(x\in V\), define \(I_e(x)=\{i:x\in\operatorname{cl}_V(\operatorname{int}_V\Omega_i)\}\). Then \[\partial_BF(x)\subseteq\{DF_i(x):i\in I_e(x)\},\qquad \partial_CF(x)=\operatorname{co}\partial_BF(x).\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Under a regular finite smooth-selection representation, every limiting Jacobian comes from an essentially active selection, and the Clarke generalized Jacobian is the convex hull of the limiting Jacobians.
assumptions_latex: \(U\subseteq\mathbb{R}^n\) and \(V\subseteq U\) are open.
\(F:U\to\mathbb{R}^m\) is locally Lipschitz.
The finite selections \(F_i:V\to\mathbb{R}^m\) are continuously differentiable.
\(V=\bigcup_i\operatorname{cl}_V(\operatorname{int}_V\Omega_i)\), where \(\Omega_i=\{y\in V:F(y)=F_i(y)\}\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: For every \(x\in V\), \(\partial_BF(x)\subseteq\{DF_i(x):i\in I_e(x)\}\) and \(\partial_CF(x)=\operatorname{co}\partial_BF(x)\).

notation.meaning: region on which the ith selection represents F
essentially active selection indices at x

knowledge_statements.title: Transition-Surface Structure
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Regular switching boundaries between smooth selection regions.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let two scalar-valued selections \(f_i,f_j:U\subseteq\mathbb{R}^n	o\mathbb{R}\) be continuously differentiable, and put \(g_{ij}=f_i-f_j\). Their transition set is \(S_{ij}=\{x\in U:g_{ij}(x)=0\}\). If \(
abla g_{ij}( ar x)
eq0\), then near \( ar x\), the set \(S_{ij}\) is a continuously differentiable hypersurface with normal \(
abla g_{ij}( ar x)\). The two strict regions \(g_{ij}>0\) and \(g_{ij}<0\) lie locally on opposite sides; hence a max- or min-selection can change between \(i\) and \(j\) only across this surface.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A regular equality between two smooth scalar selections forms a smooth switching hypersurface separating their strict selection regions.

\(f_i(\bar x)=f_j(\bar x)\) and \(\nabla(f_i-f_j)(\bar x)\neq0\).

children.title: Piecewise-Differentiable Constructions
children.top_down_role: Finite selection structures for explicit local Newton models.

knowledge_statements.title: Piecewise-Differentiable Constructions
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite smooth selections give explicit semismooth local Newton models.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(F:U\subseteq\mathbb{R}^n\to\mathbb{R}^m\) be locally Lipschitz and locally representable by finitely many continuously differentiable selections \(F_i\). Then \(F\) is semismooth: for every \(h\to0\) and every \(V_h\in\partial_CF(x+h)\),
\[F(x+h)-F(x)-V_hh=o(\lVert h\rVert).\]
If every active selection has locally Lipschitz derivative, then the remainder is \(O(\lVert h\rVert^2)\), so \(F\) is strongly semismooth. Thus finite compositions of smooth functions with max, min, or absolute value inherit explicit selection-based Newton matrices.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Finite continuously differentiable selections yield semismooth maps; Lipschitz selection Jacobians yield strong semismoothness and quadratic local models.
assumptions_latex: \(F\) is locally Lipschitz and locally has finitely many \(C^1\) selections.
For strong semismoothness, each active selection derivative is locally Lipschitz.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(F(x+h)-F(x)-V_hh=o(\lVert h\rVert)\), or \(O(\lVert h\rVert^2)\) under the stronger assumption.

notation.meaning: a Clarke generalized Jacobian selected at the perturbed point

children.title: Composite-Map Constructions
children.top_down_role: Composition structures used to transfer semismoothness and generalized derivatives.

knowledge_statements.title: Composite-Map Constructions
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite-dimensional semismooth chain rule for locally Lipschitz compositions.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(F:U\subseteq\mathbb{R}^n\to\mathbb{R}^p\) be semismooth at \(x\), and let \(G:V\subseteq\mathbb{R}^p\to\mathbb{R}^m\) be semismooth at \(F(x)\), where both maps are locally Lipschitz and \(F(U)\subseteq V\). Then \(H=G\circ F\) is semismooth at \(x\). Its Clarke generalized Jacobian satisfies
\[\partial_CH(x)\subseteq\operatorname{co}\{AB:A\in\partial_CG(F(x)),\ B\in\partial_CF(x)\}.\]
If both constituent maps are strongly semismooth, then their composition is strongly semismooth.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Locally Lipschitz semismooth maps remain semismooth under composition, with generalized Jacobians contained in the convex hull of Jacobian products.
assumptions_latex: \(F\) and \(G\) are locally Lipschitz and semismooth at the relevant points.
\(F(U)\subseteq V\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(G\circ F\) is semismooth and obeys the displayed generalized-Jacobian chain inclusion.

notation.meaning: composite map G composed with F

children.title: Projection Constructions

knowledge_statements.title: Projection Constructions
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Polyhedral Euclidean projections as strongly semismooth Newton primitives.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
For a nonempty closed convex polyhedron \(C\subseteq\mathbb{R}^n\), define
\[P_C(x)=\operatorname*{argmin}_{z\in C}\tfrac12\lVert z-x\rVert^2.\]
The minimizer is unique, and \(P_C\) is firmly nonexpansive. Moreover, \(P_C\) is piecewise affine with finitely many local affine selections; consequently it is strongly semismooth. On any region where the active constraints are fixed and linearly independent, its classical Jacobian is the orthogonal projector onto the tangent subspace of the corresponding face. Limiting such projectors supply admissible generalized Newton matrices at transition points.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Projection onto a closed convex polyhedron is uniquely defined, firmly nonexpansive, piecewise affine, and strongly semismooth.
assumptions_latex: \(C\) is a nonempty closed convex polyhedron in \(\mathbb{R}^n\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(P_C\) is piecewise affine and strongly semismooth, with generalized Jacobians generated by neighboring face projectors.

children.title: Proximal Constructions
children.top_down_role: Newton-facing mappings generated by proximal operators.

knowledge_statements.title: Proximal Constructions
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Convex proximal mappings as resolvents and semismooth primitives.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(g:\mathbb{R}^n\to(-\infty,+\infty]\) be proper, lower semicontinuous, and convex, and let \(\lambda>0\). Its proximal mapping is
\[\operatorname{prox}_{\lambda g}(x)=\operatorname*{argmin}_{z\in\mathbb{R}^n}\left\{g(z)+\frac{1}{2\lambda}\lVert z-x\rVert^2\right\}=(I+\lambda\partial g)^{-1}(x).\]
It is single-valued and firmly nonexpansive. If \(g\) is convex piecewise linear-quadratic, then the proximal mapping is piecewise affine and therefore strongly semismooth, providing explicit generalized Newton matrices from its neighboring affine pieces.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A convex proximal map is a firmly nonexpansive subdifferential resolvent; piecewise linear-quadratic functions give piecewise-affine, strongly semismooth proximal maps.
assumptions_latex: \(g\) is proper, lower semicontinuous, and convex.
\(\lambda>0\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\operatorname{prox}_{\lambda g}=(I+\lambda\partial g)^{-1}\); for convex piecewise linear-quadratic \(g\), it is strongly semismooth.

children.title: Resolvent-Based Interfaces
children.top_down_role: Operator interfaces linking proximal mappings to resolvent structures.

knowledge_statements.title: Resolvent-Based Interfaces
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Resolvent residuals convert monotone inclusions into semismooth equations.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(T:\mathbb{R}^n\rightrightarrows\mathbb{R}^n\) be maximal monotone and \(\lambda>0\). Define its resolvent and residual by
\[J_{\lambda T}=(I+\lambda T)^{-1},\qquad R_{\lambda T}=I-J_{\lambda T}.\]
The resolvent is everywhere defined, single-valued, and firmly nonexpansive, and
\[0\in T(x)\quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad x=J_{\lambda T}(x)\quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad R_{\lambda T}(x)=0.\]
Thus any semismoothness of \(J_{\lambda T}\) transfers directly to \(R_{\lambda T}\), with generalized Newton matrices of the form \(I-V\), where \(V\in\partial_CJ_{\lambda T}(x)\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The resolvent converts a maximal-monotone inclusion into a fixed-point or residual equation, preserving semismoothness through subtraction from the identity.
assumptions_latex: \(T\) is maximal monotone on \(\mathbb{R}^n\).
\(\lambda>0\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(0\in T(x)\) if and only if \(R_{\lambda T}(x)=0\), and resolvent semismoothness transfers to the residual.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The maximal-monotone resolvent and residual claims are mathematically standard and fit the container, but the record supplies no citation or inspectable locator.

children.title: Semismoothness Transfer Conditions
children.top_down_role: Regularity settings supporting semismoothness of projection-based or proximal constructions.

knowledge_statements.title: Semismoothness Transfer Conditions
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Sufficient conditions for projection-proximal residuals to inherit semismoothness.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(S:\mathbb{R}^p\to\mathbb{R}^q\) be locally Lipschitz and semismooth at \(y=G(x)\), and let \(G:\mathbb{R}^n\to\mathbb{R}^p\) and \(H:\mathbb{R}^n\to\mathbb{R}^m\) be continuously differentiable near \(x\). If \(A:\mathbb{R}^q\to\mathbb{R}^m\) is linear, then
\[R(z)=H(z)+AS(G(z))\]
is semismooth at \(x\). It is strongly semismooth when \(S\) is strongly semismooth and \(DG,DH\) are locally Lipschitz. This applies when \(S\) is a polyhedral projection, a piecewise-affine proximal map, or a semismooth resolvent.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Smooth outer and inner transformations preserve semismoothness of projection, proximal, or resolvent residuals; Lipschitz derivatives preserve strong semismoothness.
assumptions_latex: \(S\) is locally Lipschitz and semismooth at \(G(x)\).
\(G\) and \(H\) are \(C^1\) near \(x\), and \(A\) is linear.
For strong semismoothness, \(S\) is strongly semismooth and \(DG,DH\) are locally Lipschitz.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(R=H+A\circ S\circ G\) is semismooth at \(x\), and strongly semismooth under the stronger assumptions.

children.title: Maximum-Function Constructions
children.top_down_role: Semismooth constructions formed from finite maximum operations.

knowledge_statements.title: Maximum-Function Constructions
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Scalar maximum as a piecewise-smooth strongly semismooth primitive.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
For \(a,b\in\mathbb{R}\),
\[\max\{a,b\}=\frac{a+b+|a-b|}{2}.\]
This function is piecewise affine and strongly semismooth. Its Clarke generalized gradient is
\[\partial_C\max(a,b)=\begin{cases}\{(1,0)\},&a>b,\\\{(0,1)\},&a<b,\\\{(\theta,1-\theta):\theta\in[0,1]\},&a=b.\end{cases}\]
Consequently, if \(f,g:\mathbb{R}^n\to\mathbb{R}\) are smooth, the mapping \(x\mapsto\max\{f(x),g(x)\}\) is semismooth, with Newton rows selected from the active gradients or their convex combinations at ties.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The scalar maximum is piecewise affine and strongly semismooth; its generalized gradient selects either argument or a convex combination at equality.
assumptions_latex: \(a,b\in\mathbb{R}\).
For the composite claim, \(f\) and \(g\) are continuously differentiable.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The displayed maximum formula is strongly semismooth with the stated Clarke generalized gradient.

children.title: Minimum-Function Constructions
children.top_down_role: Semismooth constructions formed from finite minimum operations.

knowledge_statements.title: Minimum-Function Constructions
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Minimum-function encoding of scalar and componentwise complementarity.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For \(a,b\in\mathbb{R}\), define \(m(a,b)=\min\{a,b\}\). Then \[m(a,b)=\frac{a+b-|a-b|}{2},\qquad m(a,b)=0\ \Longleftrightarrow\ a\geq0,\ b\geq0,\ ab=0.\] The mapping \(m:\mathbb{R}^2\to\mathbb{R}\) is piecewise affine and strongly semismooth, with \[\partial_Cm(a,b)=\begin{cases}\{(1,0)\},&a<b,\\\{(0,1)\},&a>b,\\\{(\theta,1-\theta):\theta\in[0,1]\},&a=b.\end{cases}\] For any mapping \(F:\mathbb{R}^n\to\mathbb{R}^n\), define \(M_F(x)\in\mathbb{R}^n\) componentwise by \((M_F(x))_k=m(x_k,F_k(x))\). Then \(M_F(x)=0\) if and only if \(x\geq0\), \(F(x)\geq0\), and \(x_kF_k(x)=0\) for every \(k\in\{1,\ldots,n\}\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The minimum function is piecewise affine and strongly semismooth. Applied componentwise to a vector and a same-dimensional mapping, its zero equation exactly represents nonnegative complementarity.
assumptions_latex: \(a,b\in\mathbb{R}\).
For the componentwise construction, \(n\) is a positive integer and \(F:\mathbb{R}^n\to\mathbb{R}^n\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(m(a,b)=0\) exactly characterizes scalar nonnegative complementarity, and \(M_F(x)=0\) exactly characterizes componentwise nonnegative complementarity between \(x\) and \(F(x)\).

knowledge_statements.title: Norm-Based Constructions
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Euclidean norm as a strongly semismooth complementarity building block.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
The Euclidean norm \(r(z)=\lVert z\rVert_2\) on \(\mathbb{R}^p\) is globally Lipschitz and strongly semismooth. Its Clarke generalized gradient is
\[\partial_Cr(z)=\begin{cases}\{z^{\mathsf T}/\lVert z\rVert_2\},&z\neq0,\\\{v^{\mathsf T}:\lVert v\rVert_2\leq1\},&z=0.\end{cases}\]
Accordingly, any mapping formed by composing \(r\) with a smooth finite-dimensional map and adding smooth terms is semismooth; it is strongly semismooth when the smooth constituent derivatives are locally Lipschitz. This supplies Newton models for norm-based complementarity functions.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The Euclidean norm is globally Lipschitz and strongly semismooth, with the unit ball as its generalized gradient at zero.
assumptions_latex: \(p\) is a positive integer and \(z\in\mathbb{R}^p\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(r(z)=\lVert z\rVert_2\) is strongly semismooth with the displayed Clarke generalized gradient.

notation.meaning: Clarke generalized gradient of the norm

children.title: Fischer-Burmeister Constructions
children.top_down_role: Complementarity equation constructions based on the Fischer-Burmeister mapping.

knowledge_statements.title: Fischer-Burmeister Constructions
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Fischer-Burmeister equation representation of scalar and componentwise complementarity.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Define the Fischer-Burmeister function by
\[\phi_{FB}(a,b)=\sqrt{a^2+b^2}-a-b.\]
For all \(a,b\in\mathbb{R}\),
\[\phi_{FB}(a,b)=0\quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad a\geq0,\ b\geq0,\ ab=0.\]
The function is globally Lipschitz and strongly semismooth. Away from \((0,0)\), its gradient is
\[\nabla\phi_{FB}(a,b)=\left(\frac{a}{\sqrt{a^2+b^2}}-1,\frac{b}{\sqrt{a^2+b^2}}-1\right),\]
while at the origin its Clarke generalized gradient is \(\{(u-1,v-1):u^2+v^2\leq1\}\). Componentwise application converts a complementarity system into a semismooth equation.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The Fischer-Burmeister function vanishes exactly at complementary nonnegative pairs and is strongly semismooth, enabling equation-based Newton methods.
assumptions_latex: \(a,b\in\mathbb{R}\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\phi_{FB}(a,b)=0\) exactly characterizes nonnegative complementarity, and \(\phi_{FB}\) is strongly semismooth.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Basic generalized-Jacobian Newton iteration and semismooth remainder estimates
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Basic nonsmooth Newton step for square locally Lipschitz equations, preceded by the local approximation estimates supplied in the extract.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
If F is semismooth at x, then
\[
F(x+h)-F(x)-F'(x;h)=o(\|h\|)\quad(h\to0).
\]
If F is p-order semismooth at x, then
\[
F(x+h)-F(x)-F'(x;h)=O(\|h\|^{1+p})\quad(h\to0).
\]
For a locally Lipschitz map F:\mathbb{R}^n\to\mathbb{R}^n, the basic generalized-Jacobian Newton iteration for F(x)=0 selects an invertible V_k\in\partial F(x_k) and sets
\[
x_{k+1}=x_k-V_k^{-1}F(x_k).
\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Semismoothness gives a little-o first-order remainder, while order-p semismoothness gives an order 1+p remainder. The basic nonsmooth Newton method for a square locally Lipschitz equation chooses an invertible generalized Jacobian at the current iterate and applies its Newton correction.
assumptions_latex: F\text{ is semismooth at }x\text{ for the }o(\|h\|)\text{ estimate}
F\text{ is }p\text{-order semismooth at }x,\ 0<p\le1,\text{ for the }O(\|h\|^{1+p})\text{ estimate}
F:\mathbb{R}^n\to\mathbb{R}^n\text{ is locally Lipschitz, }V_k\in\partial F(x_k),\text{ and }V_k\text{ is invertible for the iteration}

children.title: B-Differential Newton Methods
children.top_down_role: Newton families organized by Bouligand differential selections.

knowledge_statements.title: B-Differential Newton Methods
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite-dimensional Newton iteration using Bouligand limiting Jacobians.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(F:\mathbb{R}^n\to\mathbb{R}^n\) be locally Lipschitz, and choose \(x_0\in\mathbb{R}^n\). At iteration \(k\), select \(V_k\in\partial_BF(x_k)\), where
\[\partial_BF(x):=\left\{\lim_{j\to\infty}F'(x_j):x_j\to x,\ F\text{ is differentiable at }x_j\right\}.\]
If \(F(x_k)=0\), return \(x_k\). Otherwise solve \(V_kd_k=-F(x_k)\); if \(V_k\) is singular or the system is unsolvable, report failure. Set \(x_{k+1}=x_k+d_k\), and repeat until the prescribed residual or step tolerance is met.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Select a limiting classical Jacobian, solve the corresponding Newton equation exactly, and update by the computed step; terminate at a root or the chosen tolerance.
assumptions_latex: \(F:\mathbb{R}^n\to\mathbb{R}^n\) is locally Lipschitz.
\(\partial_BF(x_k)\neq\varnothing\) at every computed iterate.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(x_{k+1}=x_k-V_k^{-1}F(x_k)\) whenever the selected \(V_k\) is nonsingular.

notation.meaning: Bouligand differential, consisting of limiting Jacobians at nearby differentiability points.

knowledge_statements.title: Generalized-Jacobian Newton Methods
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite-dimensional Newton iteration based on Clarke generalized-Jacobian selections.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(F:\mathbb{R}^n\to\mathbb{R}^n\) be locally Lipschitz, choose \(x_0\in\mathbb{R}^n\), and define
\[\partial_CF(x):=\operatorname{co}\partial_BF(x).\]
At iteration \(k\), return \(x_k\) if \(F(x_k)=0\). Otherwise select \(V_k\in\partial_CF(x_k)\), solve \(V_kd_k=-F(x_k)\), and set \(x_{k+1}=x_k+d_k\). If the selected system has no unique solution, report selection failure or choose another admissible matrix. Stop when the prescribed residual or step tolerance is satisfied.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: At each iterate, select a Clarke generalized Jacobian matrix, solve its Newton system, and take the resulting step.
assumptions_latex: \(F:\mathbb{R}^n\to\mathbb{R}^n\) is locally Lipschitz.
\(\partial_CF(x_k)\neq\varnothing\) at every computed iterate.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(x_{k+1}=x_k-V_k^{-1}F(x_k)\) for each nonsingular selection \(V_k\in\partial_CF(x_k)\).

notation.meaning: Clarke generalized Jacobian of the locally Lipschitz mapping.

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(U\subseteq\mathbb{R}^n\) be open, let \(I\) be finite, and let \(F:U\to\mathbb{R}^n\) be continuous. Suppose there are continuously differentiable mappings \(f_i:U\to\mathbb{R}^n\), \(i\in I\), such that \(F(x)\in\{f_i(x):i\in I\}\) for every \(x\in U\). Define \(I(x):=\{i\in I:F(x)=f_i(x)\}\). Given \(x_0\in U\), at iteration \(k\) choose \(i_k\in I(x_k)\) and solve \(f'_{i_k}(x_k)d_k=-F(x_k)\). If the system has a unique solution and \(x_k+d_k\in U\), set \(x_{k+1}=x_k+d_k\). Return a root or stop at the prescribed tolerance; report local-model failure if no active selection has an invertible Jacobian or if the computed update leaves \(U\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Choose a smooth piece representing the continuous piecewise-smooth mapping at the current point, solve the corresponding Newton equation, and accept the update while it remains in the local model domain.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Clarke-generalized-Jacobian definition for a finite-dimensional locally Lipschitz map.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
A map F:\mathbb{R}^n\to\mathbb{R}^m is semismooth at x if it is locally Lipschitz at x and, for every h\in\mathbb{R}^n, the limit
\[
\lim_{\substack{h'\to h,\ t\downarrow0\\V\in\partial F(x+th')}}Vh'
\]
exists. In that case the directional derivative exists and satisfies
\[
F'(x;h)=\lim_{\substack{h'\to h,\ t\downarrow0}}\frac{F(x+th')-F(x)}{t}=\lim_{\substack{h'\to h,\ t\downarrow0\\V\in\partial F(x+th')}}Vh'.
\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A locally Lipschitz map is semismooth at a point when all nearby generalized-Jacobian products have a common directional limit for every direction. That limit equals the map's directional derivative.
assumptions_latex: F:\mathbb{R}^n\to\mathbb{R}^m\text{ is locally Lipschitz at }x
h\in\mathbb{R}^n
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \forall h,\ \lim_{h'\to h,\,t\downarrow0,\,V\in\partial F(x+th')}Vh'\text{ exists and equals }F'(x;h).

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Invariant-Ball Convergence of the Semismooth Newton Iteration
knowledge_statements.scope_note: A ball-wise convergence and uniqueness theorem with an a posteriori step-based error estimate.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let S=\{x\in\mathbb R^n:\|x-x_0\|\le r\}. Suppose F is locally Lipschitzian and semismooth on S. For every x,y\in S and every V\in\partial F(x), assume V is nonsingular, \|V^{-1}\|\le\beta, \|V(y-x)-F'(x;y-x)\|\le\gamma\|y-x\|, and \|F(y)-F(x)-F'(x;y-x)\|\le\delta\|y-x\|. If \alpha=\beta(\gamma+\delta)<1 and \beta\|F(x_0)\|\le r(1-\alpha), then the nonsmooth Newton iterates remain in S and converge to the unique solution x^*\in S of F(x)=0. Moreover, for every k\ge1, \|x_k-x^*\|\le\frac{\alpha}{1-\alpha}\|x_k-x_{k-1}\|.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: On the ball centered at the initial point, assume uniform invertibility of all generalized Newton matrices and the stated uniform directional-derivative approximation bounds. If the resulting contraction factor is below one and the initial residual satisfies the radius condition, the iterates stay in the ball and converge to its unique root. The error is bounded by alpha divided by one minus alpha times the latest step length.
assumptions_latex: S=\{x\in\mathbb R^n:\|x-x_0\|\le r\}
F\text{ is locally Lipschitzian and semismooth on }S
\forall x,y\in S\;\forall V\in\partial F(x):\quad V\text{ is nonsingular and }\|V^{-1}\|\le\beta
\forall x,y\in S\;\forall V\in\partial F(x):\quad \|V(y-x)-F'(x;y-x)\|\le\gamma\|y-x\|
\forall x,y\in S:\quad \|F(y)-F(x)-F'(x;y-x)\|\le\delta\|y-x\|
\alpha=\beta(\gamma+\delta)<1
\beta\|F(x_0)\|\le r(1-\alpha)
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: x_k\in S\ \forall k,\qquad x_k\to x^*,\qquad F(x^*)=0,\quad x^*\text{ is unique in }S,\qquad \|x_k-x^*\|\le\frac{\alpha}{1-\alpha}\|x_k-x_{k-1}\|\ \forall k\ge1.

children.title: Pointwise BD-Regularity

knowledge_statements.title: Pointwise BD-Regularity
knowledge_statements.scope_note: BD-regularity of a square locally Lipschitz mapping at one point.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(F:\mathbb{R}^n\to\mathbb{R}^n\) be locally Lipschitz near \(\bar x\). The mapping \(F\) is BD-regular at \(\bar x\) if every Bouligand limiting Jacobian at that point is nonsingular:
\[\det V\neq0\qquad\text{for every }V\in\partial_BF(\bar x).\]
Equivalently in finite dimensions, every \(V\in\partial_BF(\bar x)\) has an inverse. The condition is pointwise: it imposes no separate nonsingularity requirement on Bouligand matrices at nearby points.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A square locally Lipschitz mapping is BD-regular at a point when every limiting Jacobian at that point is invertible.
assumptions_latex: \(F:\mathbb{R}^n\to\mathbb{R}^n\) is locally Lipschitz near \(\bar x\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(F\text{ is BD-regular at }\bar x\iff(\forall V\in\partial_BF(\bar x))\ \det V\neq0.\)

knowledge_statements.title: Neighborhood BD-Regularity
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Uniform BD-regularity throughout a neighborhood of the reference point.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(F:\mathbb{R}^n\to\mathbb{R}^n\) be locally Lipschitz near \(\bar x\). The mapping is neighborhood BD-regular at \(\bar x\) if there exist \(r>0\) and \(M<\infty\) such that every \(V\in\partial_BF(x)\) is nonsingular and
\[\|V^{-1}\|\le M\qquad\text{for all }x\in B_r(\bar x).\]
Thus the selected Bouligand Newton models remain invertible with a common inverse bound throughout the specified neighborhood.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: All Bouligand matrices at nearby points must be invertible, with their inverse norms bounded by one neighborhood-wide constant.
assumptions_latex: \(F:\mathbb{R}^n\to\mathbb{R}^n\) is locally Lipschitz near \(\bar x\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\exists r>0\ \exists M<\infty\ \forall x\in B_r(\bar x)\ \forall V\in\partial_BF(x):\ V^{-1}\text{ exists and }\|V^{-1}\|\le M.\)

notation.meaning: Open ball of radius r centered at the reference point.

knowledge_statements.title: All-Element Nonsingularity
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Nonsingularity of every matrix in a generalized-Jacobian set.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(F:\mathbb{R}^n\to\mathbb{R}^n\) be locally Lipschitz near \(\bar x\), and let \(\mathcal{J}F(\bar x)\) be the generalized-Jacobian family used by the Newton method. The all-element nonsingularity condition at \(\bar x\) is
\[\det V\neq0\qquad\text{for every }V\in\mathcal{J}F(\bar x).\]
It guarantees that every admissible matrix at the reference point defines a unique Newton direction for every right-hand side, independently of the selection rule.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Every matrix in the chosen generalized-Jacobian family at the reference point must be invertible.
assumptions_latex: \(F:\mathbb{R}^n\to\mathbb{R}^n\) is locally Lipschitz near \(\bar x\).
\(\varnothing\neq\mathcal{J}F(\bar x)\subseteq\mathbb{R}^{n\times n}\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \((\forall V\in\mathcal{J}F(\bar x))\ \det V\neq0.\)

knowledge_statements.title: Selection-Dependent Nonsingularity
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Invertibility required only for matrices admitted by a specified selection rule.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(F:\mathbb{R}^n\to\mathbb{R}^n\), let \(U\) be a neighborhood of \(\bar x\), and let \(S(x)\subseteq\mathcal{J}F(x)\) be the nonempty matrix set permitted by a Newton selection rule. Selection-dependent nonsingularity on \(U\) means
\[\det V\neq0\qquad\text{for every }x\in U\text{ and every }V\in S(x).\]
Matrices belonging to \(\mathcal{J}F(x)\setminus S(x)\) need not be nonsingular. Hence invertibility is guaranteed for every permitted selection, but not for arbitrary elements of the larger generalized Jacobian.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Only matrices allowed by the specified Newton selection rule must be invertible; excluded generalized derivatives may be singular.
assumptions_latex: \(\varnothing\neq S(x)\subseteq\mathcal{J}F(x)\subseteq\mathbb{R}^{n\times n}\) for every \(x\in U\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \((\forall x\in U)(\forall V\in S(x))\ \det V\neq0.\)

notation.meaning: Matrices permitted by the selection rule at the point.
Neighborhood on which the condition is imposed.

knowledge_statements.title: Uniform Inverse Stability
knowledge_statements.scope_note: A common neighborhood bound on inverses of admissible Newton matrices.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(S(x)\subseteq\mathbb{R}^{n\times n}\) be the nonempty set of Newton matrices admissible at \(x\), and fix \(\bar x\in\mathbb{R}^n\). Uniform inverse stability at \(\bar x\) holds if there exist \(r>0\) and \(M<\infty\) such that
\[V\text{ is nonsingular and }\|V^{-1}\|\le M\quad\text{for every }x\in B_r(\bar x),\ V\in S(x).\]
The matrix norm is the operator norm induced by a fixed vector norm; in finite dimensions the qualitative property is independent of the chosen equivalent norm.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Every admissible nearby Newton matrix is invertible, and all inverse norms share one finite bound.

knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\exists r>0\ \exists M<\infty\ \forall x\in B_r(\bar x)\ \forall V\in S(x):\ \|V^{-1}\|\le M.\)

knowledge_statements.title: CD-Regularity
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Clarke-differential regularity of a square locally Lipschitz mapping.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(F:\mathbb{R}^n\to\mathbb{R}^n\) be locally Lipschitz near \(\bar x\). The mapping \(F\) is CD-regular at \(\bar x\) if every matrix in its Clarke generalized Jacobian is nonsingular:
\[\det V\neq0\qquad\text{for every }V\in\partial_CF(\bar x).\]
Since \(\partial_CF(\bar x)=\operatorname{co}\partial_BF(\bar x)\), CD-regularity also requires nonsingularity of convex combinations of Bouligand limiting Jacobians, not merely nonsingularity of the limiting Jacobians themselves.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A locally Lipschitz square mapping is CD-regular when every matrix in its Clarke generalized Jacobian at the point is invertible.
assumptions_latex: \(F:\mathbb{R}^n\to\mathbb{R}^n\) is locally Lipschitz near \(\bar x\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(F\text{ is CD-regular at }\bar x\iff(\forall V\in\partial_CF(\bar x))\ \det V\neq0.\)

children.title: Strong Metric-Regularity Route
children.top_down_role: Locally single-valued stability as a Newton regularity mechanism.

knowledge_statements.title: Strong Metric-Regularity Route
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite-dimensional strong metric regularity at a root, stated through a localized inverse.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
The mapping \(F\) is strongly metrically regular at \(\bar x\) for \(0\) if there exist neighborhoods \(U\) of \(\bar x\) and \(V\) of \(0\), and a Lipschitz mapping \(s:V\to U\), such that
\[
F^{-1}(y)\cap U=\{s(y)\}\qquad\text{for every }y\in V.
\]
Thus each \(y\in V\) has a unique associated solution \(s(y)\in U\), and there is a constant \(L\ge 0\) such that
\[
\|s(y_1)-s(y_2)\|\le L\|y_1-y_2\|\qquad\text{for all }y_1,y_2\in V.
\]
When combined with suitable Newton-approximation conditions, this stability property can serve as an alternative regularity route in local convergence analysis.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Strong metric regularity means that every sufficiently small residual perturbation has a unique nearby solution which depends Lipschitz-continuously on the perturbation; Newton use additionally requires compatible approximation conditions.
assumptions_latex: \(F:\mathbb{R}^n\rightrightarrows\mathbb{R}^n\) has locally closed graph near \((\bar x,0)\).
\(0\in F(\bar x)\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The localized inverse is single-valued and Lipschitz near \(0\), providing stable local solution recovery.

knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
A local error bound holds at \(\bar x\in S\) if there exist \(\kappa>0\) and a neighborhood \(U\) of \(\bar x\) such that
\[
\operatorname{dist}(x,S)\le \kappa\|F(x)\|\qquad\text{for all }x\in U.

children.title: Singular Generalized-Derivative Models
children.top_down_role: Generalized derivative families containing singular local models.

knowledge_statements.title: Singular Generalized-Derivative Models
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Concrete smooth example showing how a singular limiting Newton model destroys the usual superlinear conclusion.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(F:\mathbb{R}\to\mathbb{R}\) be defined by \(F(x)=x^2\). Its unique root is \(\bar x=0\), and
\[
\partial_BF(x)=\{2x\},\qquad \partial_BF(0)=\{0\}.
\]
For every nonzero Newton iterate \(x_k\), the update is
\[
x_{k+1}=\frac{x_k}{2}.
\]
Consequently, every sequence initialized with \(x_0\ne0\) converges to \(0\) Q-linearly with factor \(1/2\), while the limiting Bouligand model is singular. Thus the usual uniform-invertibility hypothesis for superlinear semismooth Newton convergence fails.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: For the smooth residual x squared, the Bouligand derivative becomes singular at the root and Newton iterates converge only Q-linearly with factor one half.
assumptions_latex: \(F:\mathbb{R}\to\mathbb{R}\) is given by \(F(x)=x^2\).
Newton models use the Bouligand differential \(\partial_BF(x)=\{2x\}\).
The Newton iteration starts from \(x_0\ne0\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The root model is singular, and \(x_{k+1}=x_k/2\), so the convergence is Q-linear with factor \(1/2\).

knowledge_statements.title: Nonisolated Root Geometry
knowledge_statements.scope_note: A square residual with a solution manifold illustrating the boundary of isolated-root Newton theory.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(F:\mathbb{R}^2\to\mathbb{R}^2\) be defined by \(F(x_1,x_2)=(x_1,0)\), and let \(\bar x=(0,0)\). Its zero set is
\[
S=F^{-1}(0)=\{(0,t):t\in\mathbb{R}\}.
\]
Hence \(\bar x\) is not an isolated root. The Jacobian
\[
F'(x)=\begin{pmatrix}1&0\\0&0\end{pmatrix}
\]
is singular and has a null direction tangent to \(S\). Residual reduction can control distance to \(S\), but convergence to the particular point \(\bar x\) requires an additional selection mechanism or transversal formulation.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The square residual F(x1,x2)=(x1,0) has a line of roots and a singular Jacobian tangent to that line, so isolated-root pointwise convergence conclusions do not apply.
assumptions_latex: \(F:\mathbb{R}^2\to\mathbb{R}^2\) is defined by \(F(x_1,x_2)=(x_1,0)\).
The reference root is \(\bar x=(0,0)\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The root \(\bar x\) is nonisolated, and the Jacobian is singular along the solution continuum.

children.title: Loss of Local Error Bounds

knowledge_statements.title: Loss of Local Error Bounds
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Quadratically flat residual disproving a local Lipschitz error bound.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(F:\mathbb{R}\to\mathbb{R}\) be defined by \(F(x)=x^2\), with solution set \(S=\{0\}\). For every \(x\ne0\),
\[
\frac{\operatorname{dist}(x,S)}{|F(x)|}=\frac{1}{|x|},
\]
and this ratio is unbounded near \(0\). Consequently, there are no constants \(\kappa>0\) and \(\delta>0\) such that
\[
\operatorname{dist}(x,S)\le\kappa|F(x)|\qquad\text{whenever }|x|<\delta.
\]
Thus this residual has no local Lipschitz error bound at its root.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: For F(x)=x squared, the distance-to-residual ratio is one divided by the absolute value of x and is unbounded near zero, so no local Lipschitz error bound holds.
assumptions_latex: \(F:\mathbb{R}\to\mathbb{R}\) is defined by \(F(x)=x^2\).
Its solution set is \(S=\{0\}\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: No constants \(\kappa>0\) and \(\delta>0\) satisfy \(|x|\le\kappa|F(x)|\) whenever \(|x|<\delta\).

children.title: B-Differential Local Convergence
children.top_down_role: Local convergence organized through Bouligand differential models.

assumptions_latex: \(F:\mathbb{R}^n\to\mathbb{R}^n\) is locally Lipschitz near a root \(\bar x\).
Every selected \(V\in\partial_BF(x)\) near \(\bar x\) is invertible with \(\|V^{-1}\|\le M\).
For some \(\eta<1/M\), \(\|F(x)-F(\bar x)-V(x-\bar x)\|\le\eta\|x-\bar x\|\) locally.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The B-differential Newton iteration is locally Q-linear with factor at most \(M\eta<1\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite-dimensional local convergence under a uniform B-differential approximation estimate.

source_refs.source_title: Finite-Dimensional Variational Inequalities and Complementarity Problems, Vol. II

knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Choose any \(V_k\in\partial_BF(x_k)\) and define
\[
x_{k+1}=x_k-V_k^{-1}F(x_k).
\]
For every initial point sufficiently near \(\bar x\), the iteration is well defined, remains in the neighborhood, and satisfies
\[
\|x_{k+1}-\bar x\|\le M\eta\|x_k-\bar x\|.
\]
Since \(M\eta<1\), the iterates converge Q-linearly to \(\bar x\). The conclusion is selection-independent because both the approximation estimate and inverse bound hold uniformly over all nearby Bouligand matrices.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Uniformly invertible Bouligand models with sufficiently accurate linearization give local Q-linear Newton convergence.

children.title: Linear Newton-Approximation Convergence
children.top_down_role: Local convergence organized through abstract linear approximation quality.

assumptions_latex: \(F:\mathbb{R}^n\to\mathbb{R}^n\) has a root \(\bar x\), and \(A(x)\) is a nonempty family of linear maps near \(\bar x\).
Every \(A\in A(x)\) is invertible with \(\|A^{-1}\|\le M\).
For some \(\eta<1/M\), \(\|F(x)-F(\bar x)-A(x-\bar x)\|\le\eta\|x-\bar x\|\) for every \(A\in A(x)\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Newton steps based on any admissible linear approximation converge locally Q-linearly.

notation.meaning: family of admissible linear Newton approximations

knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Given \(x_k\), choose \(A_k\in A(x_k)\), solve \(A_kd_k=-F(x_k)\), and set \(x_{k+1}=x_k+d_k\). For every sufficiently close initialization, these steps are defined and
\[
\|x_{k+1}-\bar x\|\le M\eta\|x_k-\bar x\|.
\]
Thus \(x_k\to\bar x\) Q-linearly with contraction factor no greater than \(M\eta\). The result depends only on approximation quality and stable solvability, so the family \(A(x)\) may arise from generalized derivatives, active-set models, or another linear Newton approximation.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Any uniformly invertible linear model family yields local linear convergence when its relative approximation error is small enough.

children.title: B-Differential Superlinear Route
children.top_down_role: Superlinear convergence through Bouligand differential selections.

knowledge_statements.title: B-Differential Superlinear Route
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Semismooth Newton theorem using arbitrary uniformly invertible Bouligand selections.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(F:\mathbb{R}^n\to\mathbb{R}^n\) be locally Lipschitz and semismooth at \(\bar x\), with \(F(\bar x)=0\). Suppose there are a neighborhood \(U\) of \(\bar x\) and a constant \(M>0\) such that every \(V\in\partial_BF(x)\), for \(x\in U\), is invertible and satisfies \(\|V^{-1}\|\le M\). For \(x_k\in U\), select any \(V_k\in\partial_BF(x_k)\) and set
\[
x_{k+1}=x_k-V_k^{-1}F(x_k).
\]
Every sufficiently close initial point \(x_0\) generates a well-defined sequence converging to \(\bar x\) Q-superlinearly:
\[
\lim_{k\to\infty}\frac{\|x_{k+1}-\bar x\|}{\|x_k-\bar x\|}=0,
\]
provided the denominator is nonzero.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Semismoothness and a uniform inverse bound for every nearby Bouligand matrix imply Q-superlinear convergence for arbitrary sufficiently local Bouligand Newton selections.
assumptions_latex: \(F:\mathbb{R}^n\to\mathbb{R}^n\) is locally Lipschitz and semismooth at a root \(\bar x\), with \(F(\bar x)=0\).
There are a neighborhood \(U\) of \(\bar x\) and \(M>0\) such that every \(V\in\partial_BF(x)\), for \(x\in U\), is invertible and satisfies \(\|V^{-1}\|\le M\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Every sufficiently local B-differential Newton sequence is well defined and converges Q-superlinearly to \(\bar x\).

knowledge_statements.title: Generalized-Jacobian Superlinear Route
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Classical finite-dimensional semismooth Newton theorem under generalized-Jacobian nonsingularity.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(F:\mathbb{R}^n\to\mathbb{R}^n\) be locally Lipschitz and semismooth at \(\bar x\), with \(F(\bar x)=0\), and suppose every matrix in \(\partial F(\bar x)\) is nonsingular. For \(x_k\) sufficiently near \(\bar x\), select any \(V_k\in\partial F(x_k)\) and set
\[
x_{k+1}=x_k-V_k^{-1}F(x_k).
\]
Every sufficiently close initial point generates a well-defined sequence converging to \(\bar x\) Q-superlinearly:
\[
\lim_{k\to\infty}\frac{\|x_{k+1}-\bar x\|}{\|x_k-\bar x\|}=0,
\]
provided the denominator is nonzero.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Semismoothness and nonsingularity of every Clarke generalized Jacobian matrix at the root imply local Q-superlinear convergence for arbitrary nearby generalized-Jacobian selections.
assumptions_latex: \(F:\mathbb{R}^n\to\mathbb{R}^n\) is locally Lipschitz and semismooth at \(\bar x\), with \(F(\bar x)=0\).

children.title: Q-Superlinear Sequence Regime
children.top_down_role: Sequence-level superlinear convergence classification.

assumptions_latex: A sequence \((x_k)\subset\mathbb{R}^n\) converges to \(\bar x\).
There is an index \(k_0\) such that \(x_k\ne\bar x\) for all \(k\ge k_0\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Q-superlinear convergence is characterized by successive-error ratios tending to zero.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Sequence-level definition in a finite-dimensional normed space.

source_refs.source_title: Finite-Dimensional Variational Inequalities and Complementarity Problems, Vol. II

knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
The sequence \((x_k)\) converges Q-superlinearly to \(\bar x\) when
\[
\lim_{k\to\infty}\frac{\|x_{k+1}-\bar x\|}{\|x_k-\bar x\|}=0.
\]
Equivalently, for every \(q\in(0,1)\), there exists \(K\) such that \(\|x_{k+1}-\bar x\|\le q\|x_k-\bar x\|\) for all \(k\ge K\). The designation concerns successive iterate errors and is stronger than Q-linear convergence with any fixed positive asymptotic factor.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A convergent sequence is Q-superlinear when each error divided by the preceding error tends to zero.
knowledge_statements.title: Q-Superlinear Sequence Regime

knowledge_statements.title: Strong-Semismooth Quadratic Route
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Classical quadratic semismooth Newton theorem in finite dimensions.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(F:\mathbb{R}^n\to\mathbb{R}^n\) be locally Lipschitz and strongly semismooth at \(\bar x\), with \(F(\bar x)=0\), and suppose every matrix in \(\partial F(\bar x)\) is nonsingular. For \(x_k\) sufficiently near \(\bar x\), select any \(V_k\in\partial F(x_k)\) and set
\[
x_{k+1}=x_k-V_k^{-1}F(x_k).
\]
There are constants \(C>0\) and \(\delta>0\) such that every initialization satisfying \(\|x_0-\bar x\|<\delta\) generates a well-defined sequence converging to \(\bar x\) and satisfying
\[
\|x_{k+1}-\bar x\|\le C\|x_k-\bar x\|^2
\]
for all sufficiently large \(k\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Strong semismoothness and nonsingularity of every Clarke generalized Jacobian matrix at the root imply local Q-quadratic generalized-Jacobian Newton convergence.
assumptions_latex: \(F:\mathbb{R}^n\to\mathbb{R}^n\) is locally Lipschitz and strongly semismooth at \(\bar x\), with \(F(\bar x)=0\).
Every \(V\in\partial F(\bar x)\) is nonsingular.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The generalized-Jacobian Newton iteration converges locally Q-quadratically to \(\bar x\).

knowledge_statements.title: Higher-Order Local Rate Route
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Order-semismooth Newton rate family for \(0<\alpha\le1\).
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(F:\mathbb{R}^n\to\mathbb{R}^n\) satisfy \(F(\bar x)=0\), let \(\alpha\in(0,1]\), and let \(\mathcal V(x)\) be a nonempty family of admissible Newton matrices for every \(x\) in a neighborhood of \(\bar x\). Suppose there are constants \(c>0\) and \(M>0\) such that every \(V\in\mathcal V(x)\) is invertible and
\[
\|V^{-1}\|\le M,
\qquad
\|F(x)-F(\bar x)-V(x-\bar x)\|\le c\|x-\bar x\|^{1+\alpha}.
\]
Select any \(V_k\in\mathcal V(x_k)\) and set
\[
x_{k+1}=x_k-V_k^{-1}F(x_k).
\]
Every sufficiently close initialization generates a well-defined sequence satisfying
\[
\|x_{k+1}-\bar x\|\le Mc\|x_k-\bar x\|^{1+\alpha}.
\]
The local Q-order is therefore at least \(1+\alpha\); the case \(\alpha=1\) gives a quadratic estimate.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A nonempty uniformly invertible Newton-model family with an order-one-plus-alpha linearization remainder yields local Q-order at least one plus alpha, including a quadratic estimate when alpha equals one.
assumptions_latex: \(F:\mathbb{R}^n\to\mathbb{R}^n\) satisfies \(F(\bar x)=0\), and \(\alpha\in(0,1]\).
For every nearby \(x\), the admissible matrix family \(\mathcal V(x)\) is nonempty.
There are \(c>0\) and \(M>0\) such that every \(V\in\mathcal V(x)\) satisfies \(\|F(x)-F(\bar x)-V(x-\bar x)\|\le c\|x-\bar x\|^{1+\alpha}\), is invertible, and obeys \(\|V^{-1}\|\le M\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Newton iterations using arbitrary \(V_k\in\mathcal V(x_k)\) have local Q-order at least \(1+\alpha\).

notation.meaning: nonempty family of admissible Newton matrices at x

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: An inexact semismooth Newton step satisfies \[V_kd_k=-F(x_k)+r_k,\qquad \|r_k\|\leq\eta_k\|F(x_k)\|.\] A fixed forcing regime requires a constant \(\bar\eta\in[0,1)\), independent of \(k\), such that \(0\leq\eta_k\leq\bar\eta\) at every nonterminal iteration. Thus each linearized system is solved only to a uniformly prescribed relative residual accuracy.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A fixed forcing regime bounds every relative linear-solve residual by one iteration-independent constant strictly below one.

knowledge_statements.title: Vanishing Forcing Regimes
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Asymptotically exact relative-residual forcing regime.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For steps satisfying \[V_kd_k=-F(x_k)+r_k,\qquad \|r_k\|\leq\eta_k\|F(x_k)\|,\] a vanishing forcing regime imposes \(0\leq\eta_k<1\) and \(\eta_k\to0\). Consequently, \(\|r_k\|=o(\|F(x_k)\|)\), so the linearized equations are solved increasingly accurately relative to the nonlinear residual.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A vanishing forcing regime sends the prescribed relative residual tolerance to zero, which makes the linear-solve residual negligible relative to the nonlinear residual.

children.title: Adaptive Forcing Regimes
children.top_down_role: Accuracy regimes adjusted using observed local model behavior.

assumptions_latex: \(F:\mathbb{R}^n\to\mathbb{R}^n\), \(V_k\in\partial F(x_k)\), and \(F(x_k)\neq0\).
Choose \(0<\eta_{\max}<1\), \(\gamma>0\), and \(\alpha>0\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(0\leq\eta_{k+1}\leq\eta_{\max}<1\), with accuracy tightened when the observed model defect decreases.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Model-defect-based adaptive forcing with an upper safeguard.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Given \(x_k\), choose \(V_k\in\partial F(x_k)\), compute \(d_k\) with \(V_kd_k=-F(x_k)+r_k\) and \(\|r_k\|\leq\eta_k\|F(x_k)\|\), and set \(x_{k+1}=x_k+d_k\). Define \[m_k=\frac{\|F(x_{k+1})-F(x_k)-V_kd_k\|}{\|F(x_k)\|},\qquad \eta_{k+1}=\min\{\eta_{\max},\gamma m_k^{\alpha}\}.\] Stop when \(F(x_{k+1})=0\); otherwise use \(\eta_{k+1}\) for the next linear solve.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The next solve tolerance is selected from the observed nonlinear-model defect and capped below one, tightening as local model agreement improves.
knowledge_statements.title: Adaptive Forcing Regimes

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The exact model-defect update, exponent, normalization, and safeguards are method-dependent and have no cited authoritative source. Source verification is required before this particular adaptive algorithm can be assessed reliably.

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: The squared residual merit function associated with the equation \(F(x)=0\) is \[\Psi(x)=\frac12\|F(x)\|_2^2.\] It is nonnegative and locally Lipschitz, and its global minimum value is zero whenever the equation has a solution. Moreover, \(\Psi(x)=0\) holds exactly when \(F(x)=0\). Thus decrease of \(\Psi\) measures reduction of the equation residual, although stationarity of \(\Psi\) alone need not imply a zero residual.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A residual merit function is one half the squared equation residual; its zeros coincide exactly with solutions, though nonzero stationary points may exist.

children.title: Complementarity Merit Functions
children.top_down_role: Merit-function families tailored to complementarity equations.

assumptions_latex: \(G:\mathbb{R}^n\to\mathbb{R}^n\) is continuous.
The complementarity problem is \(x\geq0\), \(G(x)\geq0\), and \(x_iG_i(x)=0\) for every \(i\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\Psi_{\mathrm{NCP}}(x)=0\) if and only if \(x\) solves the complementarity problem.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Fischer-Burmeister residual representation of nonlinear complementarity.

source_refs.source_title: Finite-Dimensional Variational Inequalities and Complementarity Problems, Vol. II

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Define the Fischer-Burmeister function by \(\phi(a,b)=\sqrt{a^2+b^2}-a-b\), the residual components by \(\Phi_i(x)=\phi(x_i,G_i(x))\), and the merit function by \[\Psi_{\mathrm{NCP}}(x)=\frac12\|\Phi(x)\|_2^2.\] Since \(\phi(a,b)=0\) exactly when \(a\geq0\), \(b\geq0\), and \(ab=0\), one has \(\Psi_{\mathrm{NCP}}(x)=0\) exactly when \(x\) satisfies all complementarity conditions.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Applying the Fischer-Burmeister function componentwise produces a squared residual merit whose zeros are exactly the complementarity solutions.
knowledge_statements.title: Complementarity Merit Functions

children.title: Dini Stationarity
children.top_down_role: A nonsmooth stationarity framework used in global convergence theory.

assumptions_latex: \(C\subseteq\mathbb{R}^n\) is closed, \(x\in C\), and \(f:C\to\mathbb{R}\) is finite near \(x\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(x\) is Dini stationary precisely when \(f'_{-}(x;d)\geq0\) for every \(d\in T_C(x)\).

notation.meaning: Contingent tangent cone to the feasible set at x

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Constrained lower-Dini stationarity on a closed finite-dimensional feasible set.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For \(d\in T_C(x)\), define the feasible lower Dini directional derivative by \[f'_{-}(x;d)=\liminf_{\substack{t\downarrow0,\ d'\to d\\ x+td'\in C}}\frac{f(x+td')-f(x)}{t}.\] The point \(x\) is Dini stationary for minimizing \(f\) over \(C\) when \(f'_{-}(x;d)\geq0\) for every \(d\in T_C(x)\). In the unconstrained case, \(T_C(x)=\mathbb{R}^n\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A feasible point is Dini stationary when its lower Dini directional derivative is nonnegative in every contingent feasible direction.
knowledge_statements.title: Dini Stationarity

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: Lower- and upper-Dini stationarity conventions differ, and the proposed feasible liminf derivative is not supported by any cited source. An authoritative definition with a precise locator is required.

children.title: Bounded-Level-Set Frameworks
children.top_down_role: Boundedness structures used to support nonlocal convergence arguments.

assumptions_latex: \(\Psi:\mathbb{R}^n\to(-\infty,+\infty]\) is lower semicontinuous and bounded below.
An algorithm produces \(\Psi(x_{k+1})\leq\Psi(x_k)\) for every \(k\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\{x_k\}\subseteq L_0\); if \(L_0\) is bounded, then the sequence has an accumulation point.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite-dimensional bounded initial-level-set framework for descent iterates.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Given an initial point \(x_0\), define \[L_0=\{x\in\mathbb{R}^n:\Psi(x)\leq\Psi(x_0)\}.\] A bounded-level-set framework assumes that \(L_0\) is bounded. Monotonicity of the merit values then gives \(x_k\in L_0\) for every \(k\). Because lower semicontinuity makes \(L_0\) closed, it is compact in finite dimensions; consequently, every infinite iterate sequence has an accumulation point in \(L_0\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: If descent keeps all iterates in a bounded initial merit level set, compactness guarantees accumulation points for the global convergence analysis.
knowledge_statements.title: Bounded-Level-Set Frameworks

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The compactness argument is standard and internally correct in finite dimensions, but the record supplies neither a source nor an explicit standard-field rationale. Evidence is required for candidate-review admission.

children.title: Basic Path-Search Methods
children.top_down_role: Path-search families for nonsmooth equation systems.

assumptions_latex: \(F:\mathbb{R}^n\to\mathbb{R}^n\) has merit function \(\Psi(x)=\frac12\|F(x)\|^2\).
At each nonterminal \(x_k\), a continuous trial path \(p_k:[0,1]\to\mathbb{R}^n\) satisfies \(p_k(0)=x_k\) and has predicted decrease \(\Delta_k>0\).
Choose \(\beta\in(0,1)\) and \(\sigma\in(0,1)\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\Psi(x_{k+1})\leq\Psi(x_k)-\sigma t_k\Delta_k<\Psi(x_k)\).

notation.meaning: Continuous search path from the current iterate

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Armijo backtracking along a prescribed continuous Newton-type path.

source_refs.locator: 5.5 Splitting Methods with Line Search p. 429
source_refs.source_title: The Linear Complementarity Problem
Finite-Dimensional Variational Inequalities and Complementarity Problems, Vol. II

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Starting from \(x_0\), stop if \(F(x_k)=0\). Otherwise construct \(p_k\) and choose the smallest integer \(j_k\geq0\) such that, with \(t_k=\beta^{j_k}\), \[\Psi(p_k(t_k))\leq\Psi(x_k)-\sigma t_k\Delta_k.\] Set \(x_{k+1}=p_k(t_k)\) and repeat. The path may interpolate between a safeguarded direction and a semismooth Newton candidate; the acceptance test enforces strict merit decrease at every nonterminal iteration.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A path-search method backtracks along a continuous Newton-type path until an Armijo merit decrease is achieved, then accepts that path point.

A method-specific local descent condition and source support for this exact path-search formulation are needed before the algorithm and its stated decrease conclusion can be trusted.

children.title: Regularized Path Search
children.top_down_role: Path-search families using regularized equation systems.

knowledge_statements.title: Regularized Path Search
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Regularized generalized-Newton path with residual-merit acceptance.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Given an iterate \(x_k\), choose \(V_k\in\partial F(x_k)\) and a continuous regularization schedule \(\lambda_k(t)>0\) for \(t\in[0,1]\). Define the trial path by \[d_k(t)=-(V_k+\lambda_k(t)I)^{-1}F(x_k),\qquad x_k(t)=x_k+d_k(t).\] Search over increasing \(t\) until \(\phi(x_k(t))\leq \phi(x_k)-\sigma\|d_k(t)\|^2\), where \(\phi(x)=\tfrac12\|F(x)\|^2\) and \(\sigma>0\). Set \(x_{k+1}=x_k(t_k)\); stop when \(\|F(x_k)\|\leq\varepsilon\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Trace regularized generalized-Newton trial points and accept the first path parameter producing sufficient residual-merit decrease.
assumptions_latex: \(F:\mathbb R^n\to\mathbb R^n\) is locally Lipschitz.
\(V_k+\lambda_k(t)I\) is nonsingular along the searched path.
\(0<\sigma\) and \(\varepsilon>0\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(x_{k+1}\) satisfies the prescribed residual-merit decrease.

notation.meaning: Clarke generalized Jacobian of F at x

children.title: Continuation Path Search
children.top_down_role: Path-search families embedded in parameter continuation.

knowledge_statements.title: Continuation Path Search
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Predictor-corrector continuation for a parameterized nonsmooth equation.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(H(x,\mu)=0\) approximate \(F(x)=0\) as \(\mu\downarrow0\). Starting from \((x_0,\mu_0)\) with \(\mu_0>0\), choose \(0<\theta<1\). At iteration \(k\), predict a trial pair on the solution path, set \(\mu_{k+1}=\theta\,\mu_k\), and correct \(x\) by solving \[D_xH(x_k^{\mathrm p},\mu_{k+1})d_k=-H(x_k^{\mathrm p},\mu_{k+1}),\qquad x_{k+1}=x_k^{\mathrm p}+d_k.\] Repeat corrections until the prescribed residual tolerance holds; terminate when both \(\mu_k\leq\varepsilon_bc\) and \(\|F(x_k)\|\leq\varepsilon_F\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Decrease the continuation parameter, predict along the parameterized solution path, and apply Newton corrections until the original residual is small.
assumptions_latex: \(H:\mathbb R^n\times(0,\mu_0]\to\mathbb R^n\) is continuously differentiable in \(x\).
\(H(x,\mu)\to F(x)\) locally uniformly as \(\mu\downarrow0\).
\(D_xH\) is nonsingular at accepted corrector points.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The output is an approximate zero of \(F\) reached through decreasing continuation parameters.

notation.meaning: parameterized approximation of the target equation
