knowledge_statements.title: Monotone Residual Line Searches
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Armijo backtracking on the squared residual merit function.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(F:\mathbb R^n\to\mathbb R^n\) and \(\phi(x)=\tfrac12\|F(x)\|^2\). At \(x_k\), choose \(V_k\in\partial F(x_k)\) and a direction \(d_k\) satisfying \(V_kd_k=-F(x_k)\). Given \(0<\beta<1\) and \(0<\sigma<1\), select the smallest integer \(j_k\geq0\) such that \[\phi(x_k+\beta^{j_k}d_k)\leq\phi(x_k)+\sigma\beta^{j_k}\phi'(x_k;d_k).\] Set \(x_{k+1}=x_k+\beta^{j_k}d_k\), and stop when \(\|F(x_k)\|\leq\varepsilon\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Backtrack along a generalized Newton direction until the squared residual satisfies monotone Armijo decrease.
assumptions_latex: \(F:\mathbb R^n\to\mathbb R^n\) is locally Lipschitz and directionally differentiable.
\(\phi'(x_k;d_k)<0\) whenever \(F(x_k)\neq0\).
\(0<\beta<1\), \(0<\sigma<1\), and \(\varepsilon>0\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\phi(x_{k+1})<\phi(x_k)\) whenever \(F(x_k)\neq0\).

children.title: Nonmonotone Line Searches
children.top_down_role: Line-search families permitting controlled temporary merit increases.

knowledge_statements.title: Nonmonotone Line Searches
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite-memory nonmonotone Armijo search for residual merit.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(F:\mathbb R^n\to\mathbb R^n\), \(\phi(x)=\tfrac12\|F(x)\|^2\), and fix an integer \(M\geq1\). Given a descent direction \(d_k\), define \[R_k=\max_{0\leq i\leq\min\{k,M-1\}}\phi(x_{k-i}).\] For \(0<\beta<1\) and \(0<\sigma<1\), select the smallest integer \(j_k\geq0\) such that \[\phi(x_k+\beta^{j_k}d_k)\leq R_k+\sigma\beta^{j_k}\phi'(x_k;d_k).\] Set \(x_{k+1}=x_k+\beta^{j_k}d_k\), and stop when \(\|F(x_k)\|\leq\varepsilon\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Permit temporary residual-merit increases while requiring Armijo decrease relative to the largest recent merit value.
assumptions_latex: \(\phi\) is directionally differentiable.
\(\phi'(x_k;d_k)<0\) whenever the stopping condition is not satisfied.
\(M\in\mathbb N\), \(M\geq1\), \(0<\beta<1\), \(0<\sigma<1\), and \(\varepsilon>0\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\phi(x_{k+1})\leq R_k+\sigma\beta^{j_k}\phi'(x_k;d_k)<R_k\).

children.title: Line-Search Transition to Fast Local Convergence
children.top_down_role: Recovery of full Newton behavior near a regular solution.

knowledge_statements.title: Line-Search Transition to Fast Local Convergence
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Eventual unit steps and semismooth Newton local rates.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(F:\mathbb R^n\to\mathbb R^n\) satisfy \(F(x_*)=0\), be semismooth near \(x_*\), and have every \(V\in\partial F(x)\) nonsingular with uniformly bounded inverse for \(x\) near \(x_*\). For \(V_k\in\partial F(x_k)\), let \(d_k=-V_k^{-1}F(x_k)\). Suppose \(x_k\to x_*\), and backtracking accepts \(\alpha_k\in(0,1]\) when \[\|F(x_k+\alpha_kd_k)\|^2\leq(1-2\sigma\alpha_k)\|F(x_k)\|^2\] for a fixed \(0<\sigma<\tfrac12\). Then \(\alpha_k=1\) for all sufficiently large \(k\), and \[\|x_{k+1}-x_*\|=o(\|x_k-x_*\|).\] If \(F\) is strongly semismooth near \(x_*\), then \[\|x_{k+1}-x_*\|=O(\|x_k-x_*\|^2).\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Near a regular root, residual Armijo backtracking with a parameter below one half eventually accepts full semismooth Newton steps, yielding superlinear convergence and quadratic convergence under strong semismoothness.
assumptions_latex: \(F:\mathbb R^n\to\mathbb R^n\) is semismooth near a zero \(x_*\).
Every \(V\in\partial F(x)\) near \(x_*\) is nonsingular, and the inverses are uniformly bounded.
\(x_k\to x_*\), and the displayed residual Armijo rule is used with \(0<\sigma<\tfrac12\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Eventually \(\alpha_k=1\), with superlinear convergence and quadratic convergence under strong semismoothness.

children.title: Nonsmooth Trust-Region Models
children.top_down_role: Trust-region model families using generalized Newton information.

knowledge_statements.title: Nonsmooth Trust-Region Models
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Generalized-Jacobian model of squared residual within a trust region.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For \(F:\mathbb R^n\to\mathbb R^n\), an iterate \(x_k\), and \(V_k\in\partial F(x_k)\), define \[m_k(d)=\tfrac12\|F(x_k)+V_kd\|^2,\qquad \|d\|\leq\Delta_k.\] A trial step \(d_k\) approximately minimizes this model in the trust-region ball of radius \(\Delta_k>0\). For \(\phi(x)=\tfrac12\|F(x)\|^2\), define \[\operatorname{pred}_k=m_k(0)-m_k(d_k),\qquad \operatorname{ared}_k=\phi(x_k)-\phi(x_k+d_k).\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Linearize the nonsmooth residual with a generalized Jacobian, minimize its squared norm in a trust-region ball, and compare predicted with actual residual-merit reduction.
assumptions_latex: \(F:\mathbb R^n\to\mathbb R^n\) is locally Lipschitz.
\(V_k\in\partial F(x_k)\).
\(\Delta_k>0\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(m_k\), \(\operatorname{pred}_k\), and \(\operatorname{ared}_k\) form the trust-region model-quality interface.

children.title: Trust-Region Global Convergence
children.top_down_role: Global convergence families for nonsmooth trust-region methods.

knowledge_statements.title: Trust-Region Global Convergence
knowledge_statements.scope_note: First-order global convergence of residual trust-region iterations.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let trial steps satisfy a uniform fraction of Cauchy decrease for \(m_k\), and accept them when \(\rho_k=operatorname{ared}_k/\operatorname{pred}_k\geq\eta\), with standard radius contraction after rejection and possible expansion after very successful steps. Suppose the initial residual level set is compact, the selected matrices \(V_k\) are bounded, and the model errors are first-order accurate uniformly on that set. Then \[\liminf_{k\to\infty}\|V_k^TF(x_k)\|=0.\] If the stationarity measure is uniformly continuous along the iterates, the limit is zero. If every stationary accumulation point is a zero of \(F\), every accumulation point solves \(F(x)=0\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Standard ratio-based trust-region updates drive the generalized residual stationarity measure to zero under compactness and accurate models.
assumptions_latex: The initial residual level set is compact and \(V_k\) is bounded.
Trial steps achieve a uniform fraction of Cauchy decrease.
Model errors are uniformly first-order accurate.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\liminf_k\|V_k^TF(x_k)\|=0\), with root convergence under the stated stationarity-to-root condition.

knowledge_statements.title: Implementable Decrease Conditions
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Computable fraction-of-Cauchy-decrease test for residual models.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For \[m_k(d)=\tfrac12\|F(x_k)+V_kd\|^2\] define \(g_k=V_k^TF(x_k)\). A step \(d_k\) with \(\|d_k\|\leq\Delta_k\) satisfies a fraction-of-Cauchy-decrease condition if, for a fixed \(0<\kappa\leq1\), \[m_k(0)-m_k(d_k)\geq\frac{\kappa}{2}\|g_k\|\min\left\{\Delta_k,\frac{\|g_k\|}{\|V_k^TV_k\|}\right\}.\] Here the matrix norm is the operator norm induced by the vector norm. The condition is computable before evaluating \(F(x_k+d_k)\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Require the computed feasible step to obtain a fixed fraction of a computable Cauchy reduction for the quadratic residual model.
assumptions_latex: \(F:\mathbb R^n\to\mathbb R^n\), \(V_k\in\partial F(x_k)\), and \(g_k=V_k^TF(x_k)\neq0\).
\(\Delta_k>0\).
\(0<\kappa\leq1\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The displayed inequality certifies adequate predicted decrease using computable quantities.

knowledge_statements.title: Trust-Region Transition to Fast Local Convergence
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Eventual acceptance of unrestricted semismooth Newton steps.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(x_k\to x_*\), where \(F(x_*)=0\), \(F\) is semismooth, and every generalized Jacobian near \(x_*\) is uniformly nonsingular. Suppose the trust-region method tests \(d_k=-V_k^{-1}F(x_k)\), uses the generalized-Newton residual model, and accepts steps whenever the actual-to-predicted reduction ratio exceeds a fixed threshold below one. Then \(\rho_k\to1\), the trust-region constraint is eventually inactive, and all sufficiently large Newton trial steps are accepted. Consequently, \[\|x_{k+1}-x_*\|=o(\|x_k-x_*\|).\] Strong semismoothness yields quadratic convergence.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Near a regular solution, model agreement approaches one, the trust region stops restricting Newton steps, and fast local convergence returns.
assumptions_latex: \(F\) is semismooth near a zero \(x_*\).
Generalized Jacobians near \(x_*\) are uniformly invertible.
The trust-region iterates converge to \(x_*\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\rho_k\to1\) and unrestricted Newton steps are eventually accepted, giving superlinear or quadratic convergence.

children.title: Smoothing Newton Methods
children.top_down_role: Newton families applied to parameterized smooth approximations.

knowledge_statements.title: Smoothing Newton Methods
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Newton iteration on smooth parameterized approximations of a nonsmooth equation.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(F:\mathbb R^n\to\mathbb R^n\) and let \(H:\mathbb R^n\times(0,\mu_0]\to\mathbb R^n\) be a smooth approximation of \(F\). Choose \(x_0\in\mathbb R^n\), \(\mu_0>0\), tolerances \(\varepsilon_F,\varepsilon_\mu>0\), and \(0<\theta<1\). At iteration \(k\), solve \[D_xH(x_k,\mu_k)d_k=-H(x_k,\mu_k).\] Choose \(\alpha_k\in(0,1]\) using a merit-function globalization for \(H(\cdot,\mu_k)\), set \(x_{k+1}=x_k+\alpha_kd_k\), and, after adequate correction, choose \(0<\mu_{k+1}\leq\theta\mu_k\). Stop when \(\|F(x_k)\|\leq\varepsilon_F\) and \(\mu_k\leq\varepsilon_\mu\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Apply globalized Newton corrections to smooth approximations while reducing the smoothing parameter toward zero, and stop when both the original residual and smoothing parameter are small.
assumptions_latex: For each \(\mu>0\), \(H(\cdot,\mu)\) is continuously differentiable.
\(H(x,\mu)\to F(x)\) locally uniformly as \(\mu\downarrow0\).
The displayed Newton systems are solvable at the generated iterates.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: If the stopping test is reached, the output satisfies \(\|F(x_k)\|\leq\varepsilon_F\) and \(\mu_k\leq\varepsilon_\mu\).

children.title: Newton Methods without Smoothing Steps
children.top_down_role: Direct semismooth Newton families avoiding auxiliary smoothing.

knowledge_statements.title: Newton Methods without Smoothing Steps
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Direct semismooth Newton iteration using generalized Jacobians and residual line search.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Given \(F:\mathbb R^n\to\mathbb R^n\), \(x_0\in\mathbb R^n\), and \(\varepsilon>0\), repeat while \(\|F(x_k)\|>\varepsilon\): choose a nonsingular \(V_k\in\partial F(x_k)\), compute \(d_k\) from \[V_kd_k=-F(x_k),\] choose \(\alpha_k\in(0,1]\) by a residual line-search acceptance rule, and set \(x_{k+1}=x_k+\alpha_kd_k\). No smooth approximation or auxiliary smoothing parameter is introduced. When \(\alpha_k=1\), the update is the direct semismooth Newton step.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Solve generalized-Jacobian Newton systems directly and globalize them by residual line search without introducing a smoothing parameter.
assumptions_latex: \(F:\mathbb R^n\to\mathbb R^n\) is locally Lipschitz and semismooth.
A nonsingular \(V_k\in\partial F(x_k)\) can be selected at each generated iterate.
The residual line-search rule is well defined for the generated directions.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: If the stopping test is reached, the output satisfies \(\|F(x_k)\|\leq\varepsilon\).

children.title: Jacobian Regularization
children.top_down_role: Stabilization families for singular or ill-conditioned Newton models.

knowledge_statements.title: Jacobian Regularization
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Additive identity regularization of a semismooth Newton matrix.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Given \(x_k\), choose \(V_k\in\partial F(x_k)\), an initial \(\lambda_k>0\), a growth factor \(\gamma>1\), and a conditioning threshold \(\tau>0\). While \(\sigma_{\min}(V_k+\lambda_k I)<\tau\), replace \(\lambda_k\) by \(\gamma\lambda_k\). If the test is met, compute \(d_k\) from
\[(V_k+\lambda_k I)d_k=-F(x_k).\]
For every accepted shift, \(V_k+\lambda_k I\) is nonsingular and
\[\bigl\|(V_k+\lambda_k I)^{-1}\bigr\|_2=\frac{1}{\sigma_{\min}(V_k+\lambda_k I)}\leq\frac{1}{\tau}.\]
A positive shift alone does not ensure nonsingularity for a general nonsymmetric \(V_k\), and the procedure requires a separate condition ensuring that a shift satisfying the test is eventually found.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Increase a positive identity shift until the shifted generalized Jacobian meets a specified smallest-singular-value threshold, then solve the regularized Newton system; positivity of the shift alone does not guarantee success.
assumptions_latex: \(F:\mathbb{R}^n\to\mathbb{R}^n\) is locally Lipschitz.
At iterate \(x_k\), \(V_k\in\partial F(x_k)\), \(\lambda_k>0\), \(\gamma>1\), and \(\tau>0\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: If \(\sigma_{\min}(V_k+\lambda_k I)\geq\tau\), then the regularized system is uniquely solvable and \(\|(V_k+\lambda_k I)^{-1}\|_2\leq1/\tau\).

notation.meaning: Clarke generalized Jacobian of F at x

children.title: Non-Descent Newton Directions
children.top_down_role: Newton directions incompatible with the selected merit framework.

assumptions_latex: \(F:\mathbb{R}^n\to\mathbb{R}^n\) is locally Lipschitz and \(\Psi(x)=\tfrac12\|F(x)\|^2\).
At \(x\), a Newton direction \(d\) satisfies \(Vd=-F(x)\) for some nonsingular \(V\in\partial F(x)\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: If \(\Psi^{\circ}(x;d)\geq0\), then \(d\) is not a strict descent direction for \(\Psi\), so an Armijo rule requiring a negative first-order decrease cannot be justified from this direction.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Failure of residual-merit descent for a selected generalized Newton direction.

source_refs.locator: 2.5 Basic Descent Methods for Smooth Problems p. 89
source_refs.source_title: Modern Nonconvex Nondifferentiable Optimization

knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
A generalized Newton equation may be solvable without producing descent for the chosen merit function. Specifically, let \(d\) solve \(Vd=-F(x)\) with \(V\in\partial F(x)\) nonsingular. If
\[\Psi^{\circ}(x;d)\geq0,\]
then there need not exist arbitrarily small \(t>0\) for which \(\Psi(x+td)<\Psi(x)\). Consequently, a globalization mechanism based solely on an Armijo decrease along \(d\) can reject every sufficiently small trial step; a descent modification, alternative merit function, or fallback direction is then required.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A solvable generalized Newton system can yield a direction with nonnegative merit derivative, preventing an Armijo descent line search from accepting small steps.
knowledge_statements.title: Non-Descent Newton Directions

children.title: Unbounded Merit Level Sets
children.top_down_role: Loss of bounded-iterate mechanisms in globalization analysis.

assumptions_latex: \(\Psi:\mathbb{R}^n\to\mathbb{R}\) is the merit function and \(x_0\in\operatorname{dom}\Psi\).
Accepted iterates satisfy \(\Psi(x_{k+1})\leq\Psi(x_k)\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: If \(L_0\) is unbounded, merit monotonicity alone does not imply boundedness of \((x_k)\) and therefore does not ensure the existence of an accumulation point.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Bounded-iterate conclusion lost when the initial merit sublevel set is unbounded.

source_refs.source_title: Introduction to Nonsmooth Optimization: Theory, Practice and Software

knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Define the initial sublevel set by
\[L_0:=\{x\in\mathbb{R}^n:\Psi(x)\leq\Psi(x_0)\}.\]
Merit monotonicity gives \(x_k\in L_0\) for every accepted iterate. If \(L_0\) is unbounded, this inclusion supplies no boundedness guarantee: a sequence can remain in \(L_0\) while \(\|x_k\|\to\infty\). Thus a convergence argument that extracts an accumulation point from merit decrease requires an additional boundedness or coercivity hypothesis; merit decrease by itself is insufficient.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: When the initial merit sublevel set is unbounded, decreasing merit does not prevent iterates from escaping to infinity or guarantee accumulation points.
knowledge_statements.title: Unbounded Merit Level Sets

children.title: Persistent Safeguard Failure Regimes
children.top_down_role: Globalization controls that remain active inside the expected fast local regime.

children.title: Persistent Damping Regimes
children.top_down_role: Local regimes where damping remains active despite proximity to a solution.

assumptions_latex: Iterates satisfy \(x_{k+1}=x_k+t_kd_k\) with \(t_k\in(0,1]\).
There is an infinite index set \(K\) and a constant \(\bar t<1\) such that \(t_k\leq\bar t\) for every \(k\in K\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Along \(K\), the method never enters the eventual full-step regime \(t_k=1\); hence any local superlinear-rate theorem requiring eventual full steps is inapplicable.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Persistent line-search damping as a boundary of eventual full-step convergence theory.

source_refs.locator: Chapter 2. General Schemes for Investigating Iterative Methods p. 37
source_refs.source_title: Introduction to Optimization

knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
A persistent damping regime occurs when there exist an infinite set \(K\subseteq\mathbb{N}\) and \(\bar t<1\) such that
\[0<t_k\leq\bar t\qquad(k\in K).\]
Then full Newton steps are not eventually accepted. Even if the undamped directions satisfy a local semismooth Newton estimate, that estimate does not by itself establish superlinear convergence of the actual iteration \(x_{k+1}=x_k+t_kd_k\), because the accepted displacement differs from \(d_k\) by the nonvanishing factor \(1-t_k\) along \(K\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: If accepted step lengths stay uniformly below one infinitely often, the method never reaches an eventual full-step regime and standard fast-rate results do not apply.
knowledge_statements.title: Persistent Damping Regimes

children.title: Persistent Regularization Regimes
children.top_down_role: Local regimes where stabilizing regularization fails to disappear.

knowledge_statements.title: Persistent Regularization Regimes
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Nonvanishing Jacobian regularization excludes local theory premised on asymptotically exact Newton systems.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
A persistent regularization regime occurs when \(R_k\not\to0\). Equivalently, in a finite-dimensional matrix norm, there exist \(\rho>0\) and an infinite set \(K\subseteq\mathbb{N}\) such that
\[\|R_k\|\geq\rho\qquad(k\in K).\]
The directions then solve a Newton equation whose perturbation is not asymptotically negligible. Consequently, a local semismooth Newton theorem requiring \(\|R_k\|\to0\), or a stronger residual-relative decay condition, cannot be applied without a separate result controlling the persistent perturbation. Nonsingularity of \(V_k+R_k\) alone does not supply such control.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Regularization that does not converge to zero remains a nonnegligible perturbation, so fast-rate theory requiring asymptotically exact Newton systems cannot be invoked without additional analysis.
assumptions_latex: The computed direction satisfies \((V_k+R_k)d_k=-F(x_k)\), where \(V_k\in\partial F(x_k)\).
The matrices are finite-dimensional and \(R_k\not\to0\) in the specified matrix norm.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: A local convergence theorem requiring \(\|R_k\|\to0\), or a stronger residual-relative decay condition, cannot be invoked for this regime without a separate perturbation result.

notation.meaning: infinite index set on which regularization is bounded away from zero

children.title: Fast-Regime Suppression
children.top_down_role: Loss of the expected fast local behavior under persistent safeguards.

knowledge_statements.title: Fast-Regime Suppression
knowledge_statements.scope_note: An asymptotically nonnegligible aggregate globalization modification can suppress the fast local Newton mechanism.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Suppose the pure Newton update satisfies
\[\|x_k+d_k-x_*\|=o(\|x_k-x_*\|).\]
For actual updates \(x_{k+1}=x_k+t_kd_k+r_k\), define the aggregate globalization modification by
\[q_k:=-(1-t_k)d_k+r_k.\]
Then
\[x_{k+1}-x_*=(x_k+d_k-x_*)+q_k.\]
If \(q_k\) is not \(o(\|x_k-x_*\|)\), the accepted iteration does not inherit the displayed superlinear estimate. Conditions on the damping and safeguard terms separately are insufficient unless they also control their aggregate, since those terms may cancel.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A fast pure-Newton estimate is suppressed when the combined damping and safeguard modification is not negligible relative to the current error; examining the two modifications separately does not exclude cancellation.
assumptions_latex: The iterates satisfy \(x_k\neq x_*\) on the indices considered and the pure Newton update obeys \(\|x_k+d_k-x_*\|=o(\|x_k-x_*\|)\).
Actual steps satisfy \(x_{k+1}=x_k+t_kd_k+r_k\), and \(q_k:=-(1-t_k)d_k+r_k\) is not \(o(\|x_k-x_*\|)\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The actual iterates do not satisfy \(\|x_{k+1}-x_*\|=o(\|x_k-x_*\|)\) under the stated aggregate-modification condition.

children.title: Safeguard Deactivation Failure
children.top_down_role: Conditions and diagnostics associated with safeguards that do not become inactive.

assumptions_latex: A safeguarded method selects a pure Newton step only when a test \(S_k\) is satisfied.
The iterates converge to \(x_*\), but \(S_k\) fails for infinitely many indices.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The safeguard does not deactivate eventually, so any convergence theorem conditional on eventual pure Newton steps does not apply to the generated sequence.

notation.meaning: safeguard acceptance predicate at iteration k

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Logical boundary for local results requiring eventual selection of pure Newton steps.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let the update use \(d_k=d_k^N\) when the predicate \(S_k\) holds and \(d_k=d_k^S\) otherwise. Safeguard deactivation means that there exists \(k_0\) such that \(S_k\) holds for every \(k\geq k_0\). Deactivation fails precisely when
\[\forall k_0\in\mathbb{N}\;\exists k\geq k_0\text{ such that }S_k\text{ fails}.\]
In that case safeguarded steps occur infinitely often, and a local superlinear-convergence argument that identifies the tail iteration with the pure semismooth Newton method has an unmet hypothesis.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: If the safeguard test keeps failing arbitrarily late, safeguarded steps occur infinitely often and eventual pure-Newton convergence theory is unavailable.
knowledge_statements.title: Safeguard Deactivation Failure

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The logical formulation is coherent and the failure-boundary kind fits, but the record supplies no citation for the safeguard predicate, its algorithmic interpretation, or the local theorem whose hypothesis is said to fail.

children.title: Fischer-Burmeister Equation Representation
children.top_down_role: Equation-level Fischer-Burmeister representation of complementarity.

assumptions_latex: \(a,b\in\mathbb{R}^n\).
Complementarity is interpreted componentwise.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The complementarity system \(a\geq0\), \(b\geq0\), and \(a^{\mathsf T}b=0\) is equivalent to \(\Phi_{\mathrm{FB}}(a,b)=0\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Componentwise finite-dimensional representation using the nonnegative-complementarity sign convention.

source_refs.source_title: Finite-Dimensional Variational Inequalities and Complementarity Problems, Vol. II

knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Define
\[\phi_{\mathrm{FB}}(s,t):=\sqrt{s^2+t^2}-s-t\]
and \(\Phi_{\mathrm{FB}}(a,b)_i:=\phi_{\mathrm{FB}}(a_i,b_i)\). For every scalar pair,
\[\phi_{\mathrm{FB}}(s,t)=0\quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad s\geq0,\quad t\geq0,\quad st=0.\]
Therefore
\[\Phi_{\mathrm{FB}}(a,b)=0\quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad a\geq0,\quad b\geq0,\quad a^{\mathsf T}b=0.\]
For a nonlinear complementarity problem with \(a=x\) and \(b=F(x)\), its solutions are exactly the zeros of \(x\mapsto\Phi_{\mathrm{FB}}(x,F(x))\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The componentwise Fischer-Burmeister residual vanishes exactly when both vectors are nonnegative and complementary.
knowledge_statements.title: Fischer-Burmeister Equation Representation

children.title: Fischer-Burmeister Generalized-Jacobian Geometry
children.top_down_role: Generalized derivative structures specific to the Fischer-Burmeister mapping.

knowledge_statements.title: Fischer-Burmeister Generalized-Jacobian Geometry
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Scalar Clarke generalized-Jacobian formula underlying componentwise Fischer-Burmeister systems.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
For \((s,t)\neq(0,0)\), put \(r:=\sqrt{s^2+t^2}\). Then
\[\partial_C\phi_{\mathrm{FB}}(s,t)=\left\{\left(\frac{s}{r}-1,\frac{t}{r}-1\right)\right\}.\]
At the origin,
\[\partial_C\phi_{\mathrm{FB}}(0,0)=\{(u-1,v-1):u^2+v^2\leq1\}.\]
The limiting gradients at the origin correspond to \(u^2+v^2=1\), while the Clarke generalized Jacobian is their convex hull, namely the translated closed unit disk. For a componentwise Fischer-Burmeister residual paired with smooth mappings, generalized-Jacobian matrices are assembled from these scalar selections using an applicable generalized chain rule.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Away from the origin the Fischer-Burmeister derivative is unique. At the origin the limiting gradients form a translated unit circle, whose convex hull is the Clarke generalized-Jacobian disk.
assumptions_latex: \(\phi_{\mathrm{FB}}(s,t)=\sqrt{s^2+t^2}-s-t\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Away from \((0,0)\), the Clarke generalized Jacobian is the singleton containing the classical gradient; at \((0,0)\), it is \(\{(u-1,v-1):u^2+v^2\leq1\}\), the convex hull of the limiting-gradient circle.

notation.meaning: Euclidean norm of the argument pair

children.title: Fischer-Burmeister Merit Framework
children.top_down_role: Merit-function families derived from the Fischer-Burmeister residual.

assumptions_latex: \(F:\mathbb{R}^n\to\mathbb{R}^n\) is continuously differentiable.
\(H(x):=\Phi_{\mathrm{FB}}(x,F(x))\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The function \(\Psi_{\mathrm{FB}}(x)=\tfrac12\|H(x)\|^2\) is nonnegative, and \(\Psi_{\mathrm{FB}}(x)=0\) holds exactly at solutions of the nonlinear complementarity problem.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Squared Euclidean residual merit function for nonlinear complementarity.

source_refs.source_title: Finite-Dimensional Variational Inequalities and Complementarity Problems, Vol. II

knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Define the residual and merit function by
\[H(x):=\Phi_{\mathrm{FB}}(x,F(x)),\qquad \Psi_{\mathrm{FB}}(x):=\frac12\|H(x)\|_2^2.\]
Then \(\Psi_{\mathrm{FB}}(x)\geq0\) for every \(x\), and
\[\Psi_{\mathrm{FB}}(x)=0\quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad x\geq0,\quad F(x)\geq0,\quad x^{\mathsf T}F(x)=0.\]
Although \(H\) is generally nonsmooth at biactive components, its squared residual is the canonical scalar merit quantity used to compare trial points and to formulate descent or sufficient-decrease tests.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The squared norm of the Fischer-Burmeister residual is nonnegative and vanishes exactly at complementary solutions, making it a natural globalization merit function.
knowledge_statements.title: Fischer-Burmeister Merit Framework

children.title: Minimum-Function Reformulation
children.top_down_role: Complementarity equations constructed from componentwise minimum mappings.

assumptions_latex: \(a,b\in\mathbb{R}^n\).
Minimum and inequalities are interpreted componentwise.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The equation \(M(a,b)=0\) is equivalent to \(a\geq0\), \(b\geq0\), and \(a^{\mathsf T}b=0\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Componentwise minimum equation for nonnegative complementarity.

source_refs.source_title: Finite-Dimensional Variational Inequalities and Complementarity Problems, Vol. II

knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Define the componentwise minimum mapping by
\[M(a,b)_i:=\min\{a_i,b_i\},\qquad i=1,\ldots,n.\]
For each component, \(\min\{a_i,b_i\}=0\) holds exactly when \(a_i\geq0\), \(b_i\geq0\), and \(a_ib_i=0\). Hence
\[M(a,b)=0\quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad a\geq0,\quad b\geq0,\quad a^{\mathsf T}b=0.\]
In particular, the nonlinear complementarity problem for \(F\) is equivalently the nonsmooth equation \(M(x,F(x))=0\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The componentwise minimum of two vectors vanishes exactly when they are nonnegative and complementary, yielding an equation reformulation of complementarity.
knowledge_statements.title: Minimum-Function Reformulation

children.title: General C-Function Reformulations
children.top_down_role: Alternative complementarity-function selections beyond the principal Fischer-Burmeister and minimum maps.

knowledge_statements.title: General C-Function Reformulations
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Generic componentwise reformulation generated by any exact scalar complementarity function.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
A scalar complementarity function is a mapping \(\phi:\mathbb{R}^2\to\mathbb{R}\) satisfying
\[\phi(s,t)=0\quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad s\geq0,\quad t\geq0,\quad st=0.\]
Its componentwise residual for the nonlinear complementarity problem is
\[H_\phi(x)_i:=\phi(x_i,F_i(x)),\qquad i=1,\ldots,n.\]
Consequently,
\[H_\phi(x)=0\quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad x\geq0,\quad F(x)\geq0,\quad x^{\mathsf T}F(x)=0.\]
Additional assumptions such as local Lipschitz continuity or semismoothness of \(\phi\) are needed only when derivative-based solution methods are applied to this exact reformulation.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Any scalar function whose zeros exactly encode nonnegative complementarity produces, componentwise, an equation system equivalent to the nonlinear complementarity problem.
assumptions_latex: \(\phi:\mathbb{R}^2\to\mathbb{R}\) satisfies \(\phi(s,t)=0\) exactly when \(s\geq0\), \(t\geq0\), and \(st=0\).
\(F:\mathbb{R}^n\to\mathbb{R}^n\) is given.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Zeros of \(H_\phi(x)=(\phi(x_i,F_i(x)))_{i=1}^n\) coincide exactly with solutions of the nonlinear complementarity problem for \(F\).

notation.meaning: residual induced by the complementarity function

children.title: Smoothed NCP Reformulations
children.top_down_role: Parameterized smooth approximations of complementarity equations.

knowledge_statements.title: Smoothed NCP Reformulations
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Uses the standard smooth Fischer-Burmeister approximation with positive smoothing parameter.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(n\in\mathbb{N}\), let \(F:\mathbb{R}^n\to\mathbb{R}^n\) be continuously differentiable, and let \(\mu>0\). For \(a,b\in\mathbb{R}\), define \(\phi_\mu(a,b)=\sqrt{a^2+b^2+2\mu^2}-a-b\), and for \(x\in\mathbb{R}^n\) and \(i\in\{1,\ldots,n\}\), define \(\Phi_\mu(x)_i=\phi_\mu(x_i,F_i(x))\). Then \(\Phi_\mu\) is continuously differentiable, and \(\phi_\mu(a,b)=0\) holds exactly when \(a>0\), \(b>0\), and \(ab=\mu^2\). As \(\mu\downarrow0\), \(\phi_\mu\) converges locally uniformly on \(\mathbb{R}^2\) to \(\phi_0(a,b)=\sqrt{a^2+b^2}-a-b\), and \(\Phi_\mu\) converges locally uniformly on \(\mathbb{R}^n\) to \(\Phi_0\). Moreover, \(\Phi_0(x)=0\) holds exactly when \(x\ge0\), \(F(x)\ge0\), and \(x_iF_i(x)=0\) for every \(i\in\{1,\ldots,n\}\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: For a positive smoothing parameter, the smoothed Fischer-Burmeister residual is continuously differentiable when the underlying mapping is continuously differentiable. Its scalar zeros are positive pairs with product equal to the squared smoothing parameter, and it converges locally uniformly to the exact nonlinear-complementarity residual as the parameter tends to zero.
assumptions_latex: \(n\in\mathbb{N}\).
\(F:\mathbb{R}^n\to\mathbb{R}^n\) is continuously differentiable.
The complementarity convention is \(x\ge0\), \(F(x)\ge0\), and \(x_iF_i(x)=0\) for every \(i\in\{1,\ldots,n\}\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: As \(\mu\downarrow0\), \(\Phi_\mu\to\Phi_0\) locally uniformly on \(\mathbb{R}^n\), and \(\Phi_0(x)=0\) is equivalent to the nonlinear complementarity conditions.

children.title: Pointwise Fischer-Burmeister Regularity
children.top_down_role: Point-local regularity for Fischer-Burmeister Newton models.

assumptions_latex: \(\Phi:\mathbb{R}^n\to\mathbb{R}^n\) is a locally Lipschitz Fischer-Burmeister residual.
\(\bar x\) satisfies \(\Phi(\bar x)=0\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Every admissible Fischer-Burmeister Newton linearization at \(\bar x\) is nonsingular.

notation.meaning: Clarke generalized Jacobian of the Fischer-Burmeister residual.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Pointwise condition for the Clarke generalized-Jacobian Newton model at a complementarity solution.

source_refs.source_title: Finite-Dimensional Variational Inequalities and Complementarity Problems, Vol. II

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: The Fischer-Burmeister residual \(\Phi\) is pointwise Fischer-Burmeister regular at a solution \(\bar x\) when every matrix \(V\in\partial_C\Phi(\bar x)\) is nonsingular. Equivalently, because \(\partial_C\Phi(\bar x)\) is compact, there exists \(\gamma>0\) such that \(\sigma_{\min}(V)\ge\gamma\) for every \(V\in\partial_C\Phi(\bar x)\). This condition concerns only Newton models admitted at \(\bar x\); it does not by itself quantify models selected at nearby points unless outer semicontinuity of the selected approximation family is also imposed.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Pointwise Fischer-Burmeister regularity requires every generalized Jacobian matrix admitted at the solution to be invertible, uniformly over the compact pointwise matrix set.
knowledge_statements.title: Pointwise Fischer-Burmeister Regularity

children.top_down_role: Regularity along sequences of Fischer-Burmeister Newton models.

\(\mathcal M(x)\) is the specified family of admissible Fischer-Burmeister Newton matrices at \(x\).

Equivalently, no such sequence can satisfy \(\sigma_{\min}(V_k)\to0\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Sequential regularity rules out nearby sequences of admissible Fischer-Burmeister Newton matrices whose smallest singular values approach zero.

children.title: NCP Newton-Approximation Nonsingularity
children.top_down_role: Nonsingularity families for complementarity-specific Newton approximations.

knowledge_statements.title: NCP Newton-Approximation Nonsingularity
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Uniform local nonsingularity condition for the nonempty Newton-approximation family used by an NCP method.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(\Phi:\mathbb{R}^n\to\mathbb{R}^n\) be an NCP residual with \(\Phi(\bar x)=0\), and suppose \(\mathcal M(x)\subset\mathbb{R}^{n\times n}\) is nonempty for every \(x\) in a neighborhood of \(\bar x\). The family \(\mathcal M\) is uniformly nonsingular at \(\bar x\) if there exist a neighborhood \(U\) of \(\bar x\) and \(\gamma>0\) such that \(\sigma_{\min}(V)\ge\gamma\) for every \(x\in U\) and every \(V\in\mathcal M(x)\). With the Euclidean operator norm, this is equivalent to invertibility of every such \(V\) together with \(\sup\{\lVert V^{-1}\rVert:x\in U,\ V\in\mathcal M(x)\}\le\gamma^{-1}\). Consequently, for every \(x\in U\) and \(V\in\mathcal M(x)\), the Newton equation \(Vd=-\Phi(x)\) has a unique solution satisfying \(\lVert d\rVert\le\gamma^{-1}\lVert\Phi(x)\rVert\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A nonempty complementarity Newton family is uniformly nonsingular at a solution when every nearby approximation matrix has smallest singular value bounded away from zero. Equivalently, all nearby Newton equations have unique steps and uniformly bounded inverse operators.
assumptions_latex: \(\Phi:\mathbb{R}^n\to\mathbb{R}^n\) is an NCP residual and \(\bar x\in\mathbb{R}^n\) satisfies \(\Phi(\bar x)=0\).
\(\mathcal M(x)\subset\mathbb{R}^{n\times n}\) is nonempty for every \(x\) near \(\bar x\).
Singular values and operator norms are induced by the Euclidean norm.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: All Newton systems generated sufficiently near \(\bar x\) have unique solutions with uniformly bounded inverse operators.

notation.meaning: Nonempty family of complementarity-specific Newton approximations.
Smallest singular value of a matrix.

children.title: Complementarity Regularity Regime Geometry
children.top_down_role: Regular and degenerate geometries affecting complementarity Newton systems.

children.title: Strict-Complementarity Regime
children.top_down_role: Complementarity geometry under strict activity separation.

assumptions_latex: \((x,y)\in\mathbb{R}^n\times\mathbb{R}^n\) satisfies \(x\ge0\), \(y\ge0\), and \(x_i y_i=0\) for all \(i\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Strict complementarity holds exactly when no index has \(x_i=y_i=0\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite-dimensional componentwise complementarity with no biactive indices.

source_refs.source_title: Finite-Dimensional Variational Inequalities and Complementarity Problems, Vol. II

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A complementary pair \((x,y)\) lies in the strict-complementarity regime when \(x_i+y_i>0\) for every \(i\). Under \(x_i\ge0\), \(y_i\ge0\), and \(x_i y_i=0\), this is equivalent to the disjoint partition \(\{1,\ldots,n\}=I_x\mathbin{\dot\cup}I_y\), where \(I_x=\{i:x_i>0,\ y_i=0\}\) and \(I_y=\{i:x_i=0,\ y_i>0\}\). Thus each complementarity pair lies on exactly one smooth branch, and the active branch is locally stable under sufficiently small complementary perturbations.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Strict complementarity means every complementary pair has exactly one positive member, so there are no indices at which both members vanish.
knowledge_statements.title: Strict-Complementarity Regime

source_witnesses.source_title: Finite-Dimensional Variational Inequalities and Complementarity Problems, Vol. II

children.title: Degenerate Complementarity Regime
children.top_down_role: Complementarity geometry with ambiguous or vanishing activity margins.

assumptions_latex: \((x,y)\in\mathbb{R}^n\times\mathbb{R}^n\) satisfies componentwise complementarity.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Degeneracy occurs precisely when the biactive index set is nonempty.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Componentwise degeneracy identified by simultaneous vanishing of both complementary quantities.

source_refs.source_title: Finite-Dimensional Variational Inequalities and Complementarity Problems, Vol. II

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A complementary pair \((x,y)\) lies in the degenerate complementarity regime when its biactive set \(I_0=\{i:x_i=0,\ y_i=0\}\) is nonempty. At every \(i\in I_0\), both branches \(x_i=0\) and \(y_i=0\) meet, so the local complementarity set is not a single smooth manifold at that component. For Fischer-Burmeister and minimum-function reformulations, these are exactly the indices at which the scalar NCP function is evaluated at its nonsmooth junction.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Complementarity is degenerate when at least one pair has both entries zero, where its two active branches meet.
knowledge_statements.title: Degenerate Complementarity Regime

source_witnesses.source_title: Finite-Dimensional Variational Inequalities and Complementarity Problems, Vol. II

children.title: Regime-Transition Geometry
children.top_down_role: Structural changes occurring between strict and degenerate regimes.

assumptions_latex: The scalar complementarity set is \(K=\{(a,b)\in\mathbb{R}_+^2:ab=0\}\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The origin is the unique scalar transition point between the two strict-complementarity branches.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Local branch geometry of one complementarity pair; products yield the multidimensional stratification.

source_refs.source_title: Variational Analysis

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: The scalar complementarity set decomposes as \(K=K_a\cup K_b\cup\{(0,0)\}\), where \(K_a=\{(a,0):a>0\}\) and \(K_b=\{(0,b):b>0\}\). Each of \(K_a\) and \(K_b\) is a smooth one-dimensional stratum, while their closures intersect only at \((0,0)\). Hence a continuous path in \(K\) that changes from the branch with \(a>0\) to the branch with \(b>0\) must pass through \((0,0)\). For \(n\) pairs, regime transitions occur when at least one component enters its biactive stratum.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The two strict scalar complementarity branches meet only at the degenerate origin, so every branch change must pass through degeneracy.
knowledge_statements.title: Regime-Transition Geometry

children.title: Nonsingularity-Loss Boundaries
children.top_down_role: Degenerate configurations associated with loss of usable Newton models.

knowledge_statements.title: Nonsingularity-Loss Boundaries
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Spectral characterization of the boundary of the region where a nonempty complementarity Newton family is locally uniformly nonsingular.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(D\subset\mathbb{R}^q\), and let \(\mathcal M(z)\subset\mathbb{R}^{n\times n}\) be nonempty for every \(z\in D\). Define \(m(z)=\inf_{V\in\mathcal M(z)}\sigma_{\min}(V)\) and the locally uniformly nonsingular region \(\mathcal R=\{z\in D:\text{there exist a relative neighborhood }U\text{ of }z\text{ and }\gamma>0\text{ such that }m(w)\ge\gamma\text{ for every }w\in U\}\). A point \(\bar z\in D\) lies on the relative boundary \(\partial_D\mathcal R\) only if it is approached by points of \(\mathcal R\) and there exist \(z^k\to\bar z\) in \(D\) and \(V_k\in\mathcal M(z^k)\) such that \(\sigma_{\min}(V_k)\to0\). Conversely, a point approached both by \(\mathcal R\) and by such a singular-value-collapse sequence lies in \(\partial_D\mathcal R\). Along the collapse sequence, either some \(V_k\) is singular, or, after restricting to invertible matrices, \(\lVert V_k^{-1}\rVert=1/\sigma_{\min}(V_k)\to\infty\). Degenerate complementarity indices may enlarge \(\mathcal M(z)\), but they do not alone imply singular-value collapse.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The loss boundary separates parameters with a locally uniform singular-value margin from parameters admitting nearby Newton matrices whose smallest singular values collapse to zero. At collapse, matrices are singular or their inverse norms diverge; complementarity degeneracy alone does not force this behavior.
assumptions_latex: \(D\subset\mathbb{R}^q\).
\(\mathcal M(z)\subset\mathbb{R}^{n\times n}\) is nonempty for every \(z\in D\).
Singular values and operator norms are induced by the Euclidean norm.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The relative boundary \(\partial_D\mathcal R\) is characterized by approach from the locally uniformly nonsingular region together with nearby admissible matrices whose smallest singular values approach zero.

notation.meaning: Least singular-value margin of the approximation family.

children.title: One-Sided Bounded Complementarity
children.top_down_role: Complementarity systems with finite lower or upper bounds only.

assumptions_latex: \(F:\mathbb{R}^n\to\mathbb{R}^n\) is given.
Each variable has either a finite lower bound only or a finite upper bound only.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Each one-sided bound condition is equivalent to a scalar complementarity relation after an affine sign change.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Componentwise lower-only and upper-only bounded complementarity conditions.

source_refs.source_title: Finite-Dimensional Variational Inequalities and Complementarity Problems, Vol. II

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For \(i\in L\) with finite lower bound \(\ell_i\), one-sided bounded complementarity is \(x_i-\ell_i\ge0\), \(F_i(x)\ge0\), and \((x_i-\ell_i)F_i(x)=0\). For \(i\in U\) with finite upper bound \(u_i\), it is \(u_i-x_i\ge0\), \(-F_i(x)\ge0\), and \((u_i-x_i)(-F_i(x))=0\). Thus both cases reduce to the standard nonnegative complementarity template by using the slack \(x_i-\ell_i\) or \(u_i-x_i\) and applying the corresponding sign to \(F_i\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Lower-only and upper-only bound conditions both become standard nonnegative complementarity after choosing the appropriate slack and residual sign.
knowledge_statements.title: One-Sided Bounded Complementarity

children.title: Mixed Complementarity Problems
children.top_down_role: Systems combining free, bounded, and complementary variables.

assumptions_latex: \(F:\mathbb{R}^n\to\mathbb{R}^n\) is continuous.
Bounds satisfy \(-\infty\le\ell_i<u_i\le+\infty\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: A mixed complementarity solution enforces the residual sign dictated by whether each variable is lower-active, interior, or upper-active.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Standard finite-dimensional mixed complementarity problem with finite, infinite, or absent bounds.

source_refs.source_title: Finite-Dimensional Variational Inequalities and Complementarity Problems, Vol. II

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: The mixed complementarity problem \(\operatorname{MCP}(F,\ell,u)\) is to find \(x\in[\ell,u]\) such that, for every \(i\), \(F_i(x)\ge0\) if \(x_i=\ell_i\), \(F_i(x)=0\) if \(\ell_i<x_i<u_i\), and \(F_i(x)\le0\) if \(x_i=u_i\). Conditions involving an infinite endpoint are omitted. In particular, a free variable with \(\ell_i=-\infty\) and \(u_i=+\infty\) satisfies \(F_i(x)=0\), while one-sided variables reduce to lower- or upper-bound complementarity.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A mixed complementarity problem combines equations for free or interior variables with signed residual conditions at finite lower and upper bounds.
knowledge_statements.title: Mixed Complementarity Problems

children.title: Box-Constrained Variational Inequalities
children.top_down_role: Projection and complementarity equations for box-constrained variational inequalities.

assumptions_latex: \(B=[\ell,u]\subset\mathbb{R}^n\) is a nonempty box, allowing infinite endpoints.
\(F:B\to\mathbb{R}^n\) is continuous and \(\alpha>0\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The box variational inequality is equivalent to a projection fixed-point equation and to componentwise mixed complementarity conditions.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Euclidean projection representation of a finite-dimensional variational inequality over a box.

source_refs.source_title: Finite-Dimensional Variational Inequalities and Complementarity Problems, Vol. II

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For \(x\in B\), the variational inequality \(\langle F(x),y-x\rangle\ge0\) for every \(y\in B\) holds if and only if \(x=P_B(x-\alpha F(x))\). Componentwise, this is equivalent to \(F_i(x)\ge0\) when \(x_i=\ell_i\), \(F_i(x)=0\) when \(\ell_i<x_i<u_i\), and \(F_i(x)\le0\) when \(x_i=u_i\), with nonexistent endpoint cases omitted. Therefore the residual \(R_\alpha(x)=x-P_B(x-\alpha F(x))\) vanishes exactly at the box-constrained variational-inequality solutions.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A box variational inequality is exactly a projected fixed point, equivalently a mixed complementarity system determined componentwise by active bounds.
knowledge_statements.title: Box-Constrained Variational Inequalities

children.top_down_role: Complementarity equations arising from constrained optimization optimality systems.

A constraint qualification holds at the local minimizer \(\bar x\) for \(g(x)\le0\) and \(h(x)=0\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The KKT conditions form a system of smooth equations coupled to nonnegative complementarity pairs.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: First-order KKT system for smooth inequality- and equality-constrained optimization.

For the problem \(\min_x f(x)\) subject to \(g(x)\le0\) and \(h(x)=0\), the KKT system seeks \((x,\lambda,
u)\) satisfying \(

u)=0\), \(h(x)=0\), \(-g(x)\ge0\), \(\lambda\ge0\), and \(\lambda_i(-g_i(x))=0\) for every \(i\). Thus each inequality constraint contributes the complementarity pair \((\lambda_i,-g_i(x))\). children.title: Basic Newton Method for Variational Inequalities
children.top_down_role: The direct nonsmooth Newton route for variational-inequality equations.

knowledge_statements.title: Basic Newton Method for Variational Inequalities
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Semismooth Newton applied to an equation equivalent to a finite-dimensional variational inequality.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Given an equation mapping \(H:\mathbb{R}^n\to\mathbb{R}^n\) whose zeros are exactly the solutions of the target variational inequality, choose \(z^0\in\mathbb{R}^n\). At iteration \(k\), stop and return \(z^k\) if \(H(z^k)=0\). Otherwise select \(V_k\in\partial H(z^k)\), solve \(V_kd^k=-H(z^k)\), and set \(z^{k+1}=z^k+d^k\). Here \(\partial H\) is a specified generalized Jacobian. If the linear system is singular or inconsistent, the basic method declares failure; damping or regularization belongs to a globalized variant.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Apply generalized Newton steps to a nonsmooth equation equivalent to the variational inequality, stopping at zero residual and declaring failure when the Newton system cannot be solved.
assumptions_latex: \(H\) is locally Lipschitz and semismooth on a neighborhood of the iterates.
The chosen equation satisfies \(H(z)=0\) exactly when its associated point solves the variational inequality.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(z^{k+1}=z^k-V_k^{-1}H(z^k)\) whenever \(V_k\) is nonsingular.

notation.meaning: Specified generalized Jacobian of the equation mapping at z.

children.title: Fischer-Burmeister KKT Methods
children.top_down_role: KKT-based VI methods using Fischer-Burmeister equations.

knowledge_statements.title: Fischer-Burmeister KKT Methods
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Fischer–Burmeister reformulation for polyhedral variational inequalities in inequality form.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(K=\{x\in\mathbb{R}^n:Ax-b\geq0\}\), define \(s(x)=Ax-b\), and introduce \(\lambda\in\mathbb{R}^m\). Form \(H(x,\lambda)=(F(x)-A^{\mathsf T}\lambda,\Phi(\lambda,s(x)))\), where \(\Phi_i(\lambda,s)=\sqrt{\lambda_i^2+s_i^2}-\lambda_i-s_i\). Starting from \((x^0,\lambda^0)\), stop when \(H(x^k,\lambda^k)=0\); otherwise choose \(V_k\in\partial H(x^k,\lambda^k)\), solve \(V_k(d_x^k,d_\lambda^k)=-H(x^k,\lambda^k)\), and update \((x^{k+1},\lambda^{k+1})=(x^k,\lambda^k)+(d_x^k,d_\lambda^k)\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Encode KKT complementarity with the Fischer–Burmeister function and apply a generalized Newton step to the resulting square nonsmooth system.
assumptions_latex: \(F:\mathbb{R}^n\to\mathbb{R}^n\) is continuously differentiable.
The KKT system characterizes the variational inequality on \(K\), for example under an applicable constraint qualification.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(H(x,\lambda)=0\) implies \(F(x)-A^{\mathsf T}\lambda=0\), \(s(x)\geq0\), \(\lambda\geq0\), and \(\lambda_i s_i(x)=0\) for every \(i\).

knowledge_statements.title: Minimum-Function KKT Methods
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Minimum-function reformulation for polyhedral variational inequalities in inequality form.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(K=\{x\in\mathbb{R}^n:Ax-b\geq0\}\), set \(s(x)=Ax-b\), and define \(H_{\min}(x,\lambda)=(F(x)-A^{\mathsf T}\lambda,M(\lambda,s(x)))\), with \(M_i(\lambda,s)=\min\{\lambda_i,s_i\}\). Choose \((x^0,\lambda^0)\). At iteration \(k\), return \((x^k,\lambda^k)\) when \(H_{\min}(x^k,\lambda^k)=0\); otherwise select \(V_k\in\partial H_{\min}(x^k,\lambda^k)\), solve \(V_kd^k=-H_{\min}(x^k,\lambda^k)\), and set \((x^{k+1},\lambda^{k+1})=(x^k,\lambda^k)+d^k\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Represent KKT complementarity by componentwise minima and apply generalized Newton iterations to the resulting piecewise-smooth equation.
assumptions_latex: \(F:\mathbb{R}^n\to\mathbb{R}^n\) is continuously differentiable.
The KKT conditions characterize the variational inequality on \(K\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(H_{\min}(x,\lambda)=0\) is equivalent to stationarity together with \(s(x)\geq0\), \(\lambda\geq0\), and \(\lambda_i s_i(x)=0\) for all \(i\).

children.title: Normal-Map VI Equations
children.top_down_role: Normal-map reductions of variational inequalities to nonsmooth equations.

knowledge_statements.title: Normal-Map VI Equations
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Euclidean normal-map equation for a variational inequality on a closed convex set.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For a nonempty closed convex set \(K\subseteq\mathbb{R}^n\), let \(P_K\) be the Euclidean projector and define the normal map \(F_K:\mathbb{R}^n\to\mathbb{R}^n\) by \[F_K(z)=F(P_Kz)+z-P_Kz.\] A point \(z\) satisfies \(F_K(z)=0\) if and only if \(x=P_Kz\) satisfies \[\langle F(x),y-x\rangle\geq0\qquad\text{for every }y\in K.\] Conversely, every solution \(x\) of this variational inequality generates the normal-map zero \(z=x-F(x)\), for which \(P_Kz=x\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Project the normal-map variable onto the feasible set; zeros of the resulting equation correspond exactly to variational-inequality solutions.
assumptions_latex: \(K\subseteq\mathbb{R}^n\) is nonempty, closed, and convex.
\(F:K\to\mathbb{R}^n\) is defined at every projected point.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(F_K(z)=0\iff x=P_Kz\text{ solves }\operatorname{VI}(K,F)\).

children.title: Projected-Residual VI Equations
children.top_down_role: Projection-based residual equations for constrained variational systems.

knowledge_statements.title: Projected-Residual VI Equations
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Fixed-point residual equation using Euclidean projection and a positive stepsize.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For \(\tau>0\), define the projected residual \[R_\tau(x)=x-P_K\bigl(x-\tau F(x)\bigr),\qquad x\in K.\] Then \(x\) solves the variational inequality \[\langle F(x),y-x\rangle\geq0\qquad\text{for every }y\in K\] if and only if \(R_\tau(x)=0\). Thus the constrained variational inequality is represented by a generally nonsmooth equation in the primal variable. The zero set is independent of the chosen positive value of \(\tau\), although conditioning and generalized derivatives may depend on it.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A feasible point solves the variational inequality exactly when it is unchanged by projection after a positive forward step along negative F.
assumptions_latex: \(K\subseteq\mathbb{R}^n\) is nonempty, closed, and convex.
\(F:K\to\mathbb{R}^n\) is defined and \(\tau>0\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(R_\tau(x)=0\iff x\text{ solves }\operatorname{VI}(K,F)\).

children.top_down_role: Regularized gap-function representation for variational inequalities.

knowledge_statements.title: Regularized Gap Function
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Quadratically regularized primal gap for a finite-dimensional variational inequality.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For \(c>0\), define \[g_c(x)=\max_{y\in K}\left\{\langle F(x),x-y\rangle-\frac{c}{2}\lVert x-y\rVert^2\right\},\qquad x\in K.\] The maximizer is unique and equals \(y_c(x)=P_K(x-c^{-1}F(x))\). Moreover, \(g_c(x)\geq0\) for every \(x\in K\), and \[g_c(x)=0\iff x=y_c(x)\iff \langle F(x),y-x\rangle\geq0\quad\text{for every }y\in K.\] Hence \(g_c\) is an exact nonnegative merit function for the variational inequality.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The regularized gap maximizes linearized VI violation minus a quadratic penalty; it is nonnegative and vanishes exactly at VI solutions.
assumptions_latex: \(K\subseteq\mathbb{R}^n\) is nonempty, closed, and convex.
\(F:K\to\mathbb{R}^n\) is defined and \(c>0\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(g_c(x)\geq0\) and \(g_c(x)=0\iff x\text{ solves }\operatorname{VI}(K,F)\).

notation.meaning: Regularized gap function with parameter c.
Unique maximizer in the regularized gap problem.

children.title: Linearized Gap Function
children.top_down_role: Linearized gap-function representation for variational inequalities.

knowledge_statements.title: Linearized Gap Function
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Unregularized primal gap obtained by maximizing the linearized variational-inequality residual.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Define the linearized gap function by \[g(x)=\max_{y\in K}\langle F(x),x-y\rangle,\qquad x\in K.\] Because \(y=x\) is admissible, \(g(x)\geq0\). Furthermore, \[g(x)=0\iff \langle F(x),x-y\rangle\leq0\quad\text{for every }y\in K\iff \langle F(x),y-x\rangle\geq0\quad\text{for every }y\in K.\] Thus its zeros are exactly the solutions of the variational inequality. Compactness of \(K\) ensures that the displayed maximum is finite and attained.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Maximal linearized VI violation is a nonnegative gap whose zeros are precisely the variational-inequality solutions.
assumptions_latex: \(K\subseteq\mathbb{R}^n\) is nonempty, compact, and convex.
\(F:K\to\mathbb{R}^n\) is defined.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(g(x)\geq0\) and \(g(x)=0\iff x\text{ solves }\operatorname{VI}(K,F)\).

knowledge_statements.title: D-Gap Merit Function
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Difference of two regularized gaps with distinct positive regularization parameters.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For \(0<a<b\), let \(g_a\) and \(g_b\) be the regularized gap functions and define \[G_{a,b}(x)=g_a(x)-g_b(x),\qquad x\in K.\] If \(y_c(x)=P_K(x-c^{-1}F(x))\), then \[G_{a,b}(x)\geq\frac{b-a}{2}\lVert x-y_b(x)\rVert^2\geq0.\] Consequently, \[G_{a,b}(x)=0\iff x=y_b(x)\iff x\text{ solves }\operatorname{VI}(K,F).\] The D-gap therefore supplies a finite, exact merit function without requiring boundedness of \(K\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Subtracting two regularized gaps with increasing penalty parameters yields a nonnegative merit function that vanishes exactly at VI solutions.
assumptions_latex: \(K\subseteq\mathbb{R}^n\) is nonempty, closed, and convex.
\(F:K\to\mathbb{R}^n\) is defined and \(0<a<b\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(G_{a,b}(x)\geq0\) and \(G_{a,b}(x)=0\iff x\text{ solves }\operatorname{VI}(K,F)\).

children.title: Merit-Based VI Algorithms
children.top_down_role: Global algorithm families organized by variational-inequality merit functions.

knowledge_statements.title: Merit-Based VI Algorithms
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Armijo-globalized descent framework for an exact variational-inequality merit function.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Given \(x^0\in K\), parameters \(\beta\in(0,1)\), \(\sigma\in(0,1)\), and an exact merit function \(\Psi:K\to[0,\infty)\), repeat: if \(\Psi(x^k)=0\), return \(x^k\). Choose a feasible direction \(d^k\) satisfying \(\Psi^{\circ}(x^k;d^k)<0\). Select the smallest integer \(j_k\geq0\) such that \(x^k+\beta^{j_k}d^k\in K\) and \[\Psi(x^k+\beta^{j_k}d^k)\leq\Psi(x^k)+\sigma\beta^{j_k}\Psi^{\circ}(x^k;d^k).\] Set \(x^{k+1}=x^k+\beta^{j_k}d^k\). If no acceptable step exists, declare globalization failure.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Repeatedly choose a feasible merit-descent direction and use Armijo backtracking; stop when the exact VI merit function reaches zero.
assumptions_latex: \(K\subseteq\mathbb{R}^n\) is nonempty and closed.
\(\Psi\) is locally Lipschitz, nonnegative, and satisfies \(\Psi(x)=0\) exactly at variational-inequality solutions.
Each nonterminal iterate admits the stipulated feasible descent direction.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Every accepted nonterminal step satisfies \(\Psi(x^{k+1})<\Psi(x^k)\), while termination at zero returns a variational-inequality solution.

notation.meaning: Clarke directional derivative of the merit function.

children.title: Active Partition
children.top_down_role: Indices or regions classified as active in reduced Newton systems.

knowledge_statements.title: Active Partition
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Active constrained coordinates for mixed lower-bound and structurally free variables.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let the coordinate set be the disjoint union \(\{1,\ldots,n\}=C\mathbin{\dot\cup}U\), where coordinates in \(C\) have lower bounds \(x_i\geq\ell_i\) and coordinates in \(U\) are structurally free. For a feasible point \(x\), its active partition is \[\mathcal A(x)=\{i\in C:x_i=\ell_i\}.\] These are precisely the constrained coordinates lying on their bounds. Together with the inactive constrained partition \(\mathcal I(x)=\{i\in C:x_i>\ell_i\}\) and the free partition \(\mathcal F=U\), it yields a disjoint partition of all coordinates.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The active partition consists of bound-constrained coordinates currently equal to their lower bounds.
assumptions_latex: \(x_i\geq\ell_i\) for every \(i\in C\).
\(C\mathbin{\dot\cup}U=\{1,\ldots,n\}\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\mathcal A(x)=\{i\in C:x_i=\ell_i\}\).

notation.meaning: Index set of structurally free coordinates.

children.title: Inactive Partition
children.top_down_role: Indices or regions classified as inactive in reduced Newton systems.

knowledge_statements.title: Inactive Partition
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Strictly interior constrained coordinates for mixed lower-bound and structurally free variables.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(C\) index coordinates with lower bounds \(x_i\geq\ell_i\), and let \(U\) index structurally free coordinates, with \(C\mathbin{\dot\cup}U=\{1,\ldots,n\}\). For a feasible point \(x\), its inactive partition is \[\mathcal I(x)=\{i\in C:x_i>\ell_i\}.\] Thus an inactive coordinate is constrained in the model but its bound is locally slack at \(x\). It is distinct from the free partition \(\mathcal F=U\), whose coordinates possess no such bound.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The inactive partition contains constrained coordinates lying strictly above their lower bounds; structurally unconstrained coordinates are excluded.
assumptions_latex: \(x_i\geq\ell_i\) for every \(i\in C\).
\(C\mathbin{\dot\cup}U=\{1,\ldots,n\}\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\mathcal I(x)=\{i\in C:x_i>\ell_i\}\).

notation.meaning: Index set of structurally free coordinates.

children.title: Free Partition
children.top_down_role: Unconstrained or undecided components retained in the free subsystem.

knowledge_statements.title: Free Partition
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Structurally unbounded coordinates in a mixed bound-constrained variable partition.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Suppose \(\{1,\ldots,n\}=C\mathbin{\dot\cup}U\), where coordinates indexed by \(C\) obey lower bounds \(x_i\geq\ell_i\) and coordinates indexed by \(U\) have no corresponding bound. The free partition is \[\mathcal F=U.\] It is independent of the current feasible point. For every feasible \(x\), defining \(\mathcal A(x)=\{i\in C:x_i=\ell_i\}\) and \(\mathcal I(x)=\{i\in C:x_i>\ell_i\}\) gives \[\{1,\ldots,n\}=\mathcal A(x)\mathbin{\dot\cup}\mathcal I(x)\mathbin{\dot\cup}\mathcal F.\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The free partition contains coordinates having no modeled bound and is independent of the current iterate.
assumptions_latex: \(C\mathbin{\dot\cup}U=\{1,\ldots,n\}\).
Only coordinates in \(C\) carry the lower bounds \(x_i\geq\ell_i\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\mathcal F=U\) and \(\mathcal A(x)\mathbin{\dot\cup}\mathcal I(x)\mathbin{\dot\cup}\mathcal F=\{1,\ldots,n\}\).

notation.meaning: Index set of structurally unbounded coordinates.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The definition is internally coherent and its content kind fits the leaf, but active-set literature uses multiple meanings of free indices, including iteration-dependent free sets. No inspectable source is supplied to establish that this container intends the structurally unbounded, point-independent convention.

children.title: Partition-Transition Interfaces
children.top_down_role: Interfaces where components change partition status.

knowledge_statements.title: Partition-Transition Interfaces
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite-index switching-score description of interfaces between active-set partitions.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(U\) be a topological space, let \(m\in\mathbb N\), and let \(s_i:U\to\mathbb R\) be continuous for every \(i\in\{1,\ldots,m\}\). Define \(\mathcal A(x)=\{i:s_i(x)>0\}\), \(\mathcal I(x)=\{i:s_i(x)<0\}\), and \(\Gamma_i=\{x\in U:s_i(x)=0\}\). The set \(\Gamma_i\) is the partition-transition interface for index \(i\). If a continuous path \(\gamma:[0,1]\to U\) satisfies \(s_i(\gamma(0))s_i(\gamma(1))<0\), then \(\gamma([0,1])\cap\Gamma_i\neq\varnothing\). Moreover, the complete sign partition is locally constant at every \(x\in U\setminus\bigcup_{i=1}^m\Gamma_i\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: For finitely many continuous switching scores, the transition interface for an index is its zero set. A path whose endpoint scores have opposite signs crosses that interface, and the complete sign partition is locally constant away from all interfaces.
assumptions_latex: \(U\) is a topological space and \(m\in\mathbb N\).
For each \(i\in\{1,\ldots,m\}\), the switching score \(s_i:U\to\mathbb R\) is continuous.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\Gamma_i=s_i^{-1}(0)\) is the interface across which index \(i\) may change partition, and the finite sign partition is locally constant away from \(\bigcup_{i=1}^m\Gamma_i\).

children.title: Degenerate Sets

knowledge_statements.title: Degenerate Sets
knowledge_statements.scope_note: KKT degeneracy for smooth finite-dimensional inequality constraints inside active-set methods.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Consider \(\min_{x\in\mathbb R^n} f(x)\) subject to \(g_i(x)\leq0\) for \(i\in\{1,\ldots,m\}\), and let \((x^*,\lambda^*)\) be a KKT pair with \(\lambda^*\in\mathbb R_+^m\). Define \[\mathcal D(x^*,\lambda^*):=\{i\in\{1,\ldots,m\}:g_i(x^*)=0\ \text{and}\ \lambda_i^*=0\}.\] Its elements are the degenerate active indices. The remaining indices comprise \(\mathcal A_+(x^*,\lambda^*)=\{i:g_i(x^*)=0,\ \lambda_i^*>0\}\) and \(\mathcal I(x^*)=\{i:g_i(x^*)<0\}\). Strict complementarity holds exactly when \(\mathcal D(x^*,\lambda^*)=\varnothing\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: For a finite inequality-constrained problem, a degenerate index is an active constraint whose KKT multiplier is zero; strict complementarity holds exactly when no such index exists.
assumptions_latex: \(f:\mathbb R^n\to\mathbb R\) and \(g_i:\mathbb R^n\to\mathbb R\), \(i\in\{1,\ldots,m\}\), define the problem \(\min f(x)\) subject to \(g_i(x)\leq0\).
\((x^*,\lambda^*)\) is a KKT pair with \(\lambda^*\in\mathbb R_+^m\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\mathcal D(x^*,\lambda^*)=\{i\in\{1,\ldots,m\}:g_i(x^*)=0,\ \lambda_i^*=0\}\) is the degenerate active set.

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Given an iterate with biactive set \(\mathcal B=\{i:a_i=b_i=0\}\), choose once and for all a deterministic weight \(\theta_i\in[0,1]\) for each \(i\in\mathcal B\). Solve the resulting Newton system, update the primal-dual variables, and stop when the complementarity residual and smooth KKT residual satisfy the prescribed tolerances.

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For the parametric problem \(\min_{x\geq0}\tfrac12(x-t)^2\), the unique KKT solution is \[x^*(t)=\max\{t,0\},\qquad \lambda^*(t)=\max\{-t,0\}.\] For \(t<0\), the lower bound is active with positive multiplier; for \(t>0\), it is inactive; and at \(t=0\), both \(x^*(0)\) and \(\lambda^*(0)\) vanish. Thus strict-complementarity failure is a boundary at which finite or locally constant activity identification cannot be inferred from proximity alone.

knowledge_statements.title: Critical-Cone Activity Structure
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Smooth finite-dimensional inequality-constrained critical cone at a KKT point under MFCQ.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(\Omega=\{x\in\mathbb R^n:g_i(x)\leq0,\ i=1,\ldots,m\}\), let \((x^*,\lambda^*)\) be a KKT pair, and let \(I(x^*)=\{i:g_i(x^*)=0\}\). If the Mangasarian--Fromovitz constraint qualification holds at \(x^*\), then the critical cone \(K(x^*,\lambda^*)=T_\Omega(x^*)\cap
abla f(x^*)^\perp\) has the representation \[K(x^*,\lambda^*)=\{d\in\mathbb R^n:
abla g_i(x^*)^	op d=0\ 	ext{when}\ \lambda_i^*>0,\quad 
abla g_i(x^*)^	op d\leq0\ 	ext{when}\ i\in I(x^*),\ \lambda_i^*=0\}.\] Thus positive-multiplier active constraints impose equalities on critical directions, whereas degenerate active constraints impose one-sided inequalities.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Under MFCQ, positive-multiplier active constraints impose directional equalities in the critical cone, while zero-multiplier active constraints impose directional inequalities.
assumptions_latex: \(f,g_1,\ldots,g_m:\mathbb R^n\to\mathbb R\) are continuously differentiable, and \(\Omega=\{x:g_i(x)\leq0,\ i=1,\ldots,m\}\).
\((x^*,\lambda^*)\) is a KKT pair with \(\lambda^*\in\mathbb R_+^m\).
The Mangasarian--Fromovitz constraint qualification holds at \(x^*\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The representation of \(K(x^*,\lambda^*)\) separates equality conditions from positive-multiplier active indices and inequality conditions from degenerate active indices.

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Initialize \((x^0,\lambda^0)\). At iteration \(k\), set \(\mathcal A_k=\{i:\lambda_i^k-cx_i^k>0\}\) and \(\mathcal I_k=\{1,\ldots,n\}\setminus\mathcal A_k\). Impose \(x_{\mathcal A_k}^{k+1}=0\) and \(\lambda_{\mathcal I_k}^{k+1}=0\), solve the reduced system \[H_{\mathcal I_k\mathcal I_k}x_{\mathcal I_k}^{k+1}=q_{\mathcal I_k},\] and recover \(\lambda_{\mathcal A_k}^{k+1}=H_{\mathcal A_k\mathcal I_k}x_{\mathcal I_k}^{k+1}-q_{\mathcal A_k}\). Stop when the partition is unchanged and the KKT residual meets tolerance; otherwise repeat.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Classify indices by a primal-dual switching score, solve only for inactive primal variables, recover active multipliers, and stop after partition stabilization and KKT convergence.

children.title: Bound-Constraint Primal-Dual Active Sets
children.top_down_role: Primal-dual active-set methods for one-sided and bilateral bounds.

knowledge_statements.title: Bound-Constraint Primal-Dual Active Sets
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Local bilateral-bound primal-dual active-set equations near a KKT point, where lower and upper switching tests do not conflict.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For \(\ell\leq x\leq u\), define \(L_i=\lambda_i^\ell-c(x_i-\ell_i)\) and \(U_i=\lambda_i^u-c(u_i-x_i)\). In a neighborhood where \(L_i\) and \(U_i\) are not simultaneously positive, set \(\mathcal A^\ell=\{i:L_i>0\}\), \(\mathcal A^u=\{i:U_i>0\}\), and \(\mathcal F=\{1,\ldots,n\}\setminus(\mathcal A^\ell\cup\mathcal A^u)\), using a fixed rule for zero-score ties. Solve \[x_i=\ell_i,\ \lambda_i^u=0\ \text{on}\ \mathcal A^\ell;\qquad x_i=u_i,\ \lambda_i^\ell=0\ \text{on}\ \mathcal A^u;\qquad \lambda_i^\ell=\lambda_i^u=0\ \text{on}\ \mathcal F,\] together with \(\nabla f(x)-\lambda^\ell+\lambda^u=0\). Update the partition and stop when it is unchanged and the KKT residual meets the prescribed tolerance.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Locally, bilateral bounds define disjoint lower-active, upper-active, and free sets. The method fixes active variables, zeros the multiplier of the opposite bound, zeros both multipliers on free indices, and solves stationarity until the partition and KKT residual converge.
assumptions_latex: \(f:\mathbb R^n\to\mathbb R\) is continuously differentiable, and \(\ell_i<u_i\) for every \(i\in\{1,\ldots,n\}\).
\(c>0\) is fixed.
The iteration is local to a neighborhood in which the lower and upper switching scores are not simultaneously positive for any index.

children.title: Semismooth-Newton Equivalence of Active-Set Methods

children.title: Max-Min Equation Equivalence
children.top_down_role: Active-set equivalence induced by max- or min-based complementarity equations.

assumptions_latex: \(a,b\in\mathbb R^m\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Componentwise complementarity is equivalent to either a min equation or a max equation, with identical branch partitions away from ties.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Componentwise nonlinear-complementarity equivalence underlying active-set branch selection.

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Componentwise complementarity satisfies \[a\geq0,\quad b\geq0,\quad a_i b_i=0\ \text{for all}\ i\quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad \Phi_{\min}(a,b):=\min\{a,b\}=0.\] It is also equivalent to \[\Phi_{\max}(a,b):=a-\max\{0,a-b\}=0.\] If \(a_i\neq b_i\), both equations select the same differentiable branch and therefore the same active-set Newton row. When \(a_i=b_i\), both are nonsmooth and equivalence of a particular Newton step additionally requires compatible generalized-derivative selections.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Nonnegative complementarity is equivalent to either a componentwise min equation or an associated max equation; their Newton branches agree away from ties.

children.title: Reduced-Full Newton System Correspondence
children.top_down_role: Relationship between eliminated active-set systems and coupled Newton systems.

children.title: Reduced Newton Systems
children.top_down_role: Newton systems formed after elimination using an active partition.

assumptions_latex: \(F(u,v)=0\) is linearized by a block matrix \(M=\begin{pmatrix}A&B\\ C&D\end{pmatrix}\).
The block \(D\) is nonsingular.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Eliminating \(\Delta v\) yields the reduced Newton system with Schur complement \(A-BD^{-1}C\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact block elimination in a finite-dimensional generalized Newton step.

source_refs.source_title: Finite-Dimensional Variational Inequalities and Complementarity Problems, Vol. II

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Consider the full Newton equations \[A\Delta u+B\Delta v=-r_u,\qquad C\Delta u+D\Delta v=-r_v.\] If \(D\) is nonsingular, then \(\Delta v=-D^{-1}(r_v+C\Delta u)\), and \(\Delta u\) is determined by the reduced system \[(A-BD^{-1}C)\Delta u=-r_u+BD^{-1}r_v.\] Conversely, every solution of this reduced system, followed by the displayed recovery formula, solves the full system. Thus exact elimination preserves the Newton step whenever the eliminated block and the Schur complement are nonsingular.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: An invertible Newton block can be eliminated exactly, producing a Schur-complement system whose solution reconstructs the same full Newton step.

children.title: Full Newton Systems
children.top_down_role: Coupled Newton systems retaining all primal-dual components.

knowledge_statements.title: Full Newton Systems
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Block generalized-Newton system for finite-dimensional complementarity residuals.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(F:\mathbb R^n\to\mathbb R^n\) be continuously differentiable and define \(H(x,\lambda)=(F(x)-\lambda,\min\{x,\lambda\})\), where the minimum is componentwise. For every \(i\), select \((\alpha_i,\beta_i)\in\partial_C\min(x_i,\lambda_i)\), and set \(D_x=\operatorname{diag}(\alpha_i)\) and \(D_\lambda=\operatorname{diag}(\beta_i)\). Thus \(\alpha_i,\beta_i\ge0\) and \(\alpha_i+\beta_i=1\), with \((\alpha_i,\beta_i)=(1,0)\) when \(x_i<\lambda_i\) and \((\alpha_i,\beta_i)=(0,1)\) when \(x_i>\lambda_i\). A full semismooth Newton step \((d_x,d_\lambda)\) solves \[\begin{pmatrix}F'(x)&-I\\D_x&D_\lambda\end{pmatrix}\begin{pmatrix}d_x\\d_\lambda\end{pmatrix}=-\begin{pmatrix}F(x)-\lambda\\\min\{x,\lambda\}\end{pmatrix}.\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The full Newton formulation simultaneously updates primal and multiplier variables using a jointly selected generalized derivative of the componentwise minimum residual.
assumptions_latex: \(F\) is continuously differentiable near the current iterate.
A generalized-gradient pair is selected for every component of the minimum map.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \((d_x,d_\lambda)\) is the unique solution of the displayed full primal-dual Newton system whenever its block matrix is nonsingular.

notation.meaning: diagonal matrices formed from joint generalized-derivative selections for the minimum map

children.title: Elimination Correspondence
children.top_down_role: Structural correspondence induced by elimination or reconstruction.

knowledge_statements.title: Elimination Correspondence
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact algebraic correspondence between pure-selection full and reduced Newton systems.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For the full system, choose a partition \(\mathcal A\cup\mathcal I=\{1,\ldots,n\}\) such that the minimum derivative selects \(x_i\) on \(\mathcal A\) and \(\lambda_i\) on \(\mathcal I\). Then \(d_{x,\mathcal A}=-x_{\mathcal A}\) and \(d_{\lambda,\mathcal I}=-\lambda_{\mathcal I}\). Substitution into the stationarity rows gives \[F'(x)_{\mathcal I\mathcal I}d_{x,\mathcal I}=-(F(x)-\lambda)_{\mathcal I}+d_{\lambda,\mathcal I}-F'(x)_{\mathcal I\mathcal A}d_{x,\mathcal A}.\] After solving this reduced system, recover \(d_{\lambda,\mathcal A}=(F(x)-\lambda)_{\mathcal A}+F'(x)_{\mathcal A,:}d_x\). Thus elimination and reconstruction reproduce the full step exactly.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Pure active/inactive derivative selections permit exact elimination of fixed primal and multiplier components; solving and reconstructing yields the same full Newton step.
assumptions_latex: \(D_x,D_\lambda\) make complementary zero-one selections on \(\mathcal A\) and \(\mathcal I\).
\(F'(x)_{\mathcal I\mathcal I}\) is nonsingular.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The reduced solution and recovered variables equal the unique solution of the full Newton system.

notation.meaning: indices where the minimum derivative selects the primal variable
indices where the minimum derivative selects the multiplier
