children.title: Equivalence-Breakdown Regimes
children.top_down_role: Configurations where reduced and full formulations cease to be interchangeable.

knowledge_statements.title: Equivalence-Breakdown Regimes
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Conditions limiting the pure-selection reduced-system representation and uniqueness of its Newton step.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: The coordinate-fixing reduction based on a partition \(\mathcal A\cup\mathcal I=\{1,\ldots,n\}\) requires a pure minimum-derivative selection: \((D_x)_{ii}=1\) and \((D_\lambda)_{ii}=0\) on \(\mathcal A\), and the reverse on \(\mathcal I\). A fractional selection at a tied component \(x_i=\lambda_i\) replaces coordinate fixing by a linear relation between \(d_{x,i}\) and \(d_{\lambda,i}\), so that this particular active/inactive reduced system no longer represents the full system. Under a pure selection, elimination and reconstruction still give a bijection between the solution sets of the full and reduced systems. Nonsingularity of \(F'(x)_{\mathcal I\mathcal I}\) is additionally required for that corresponding step to be unique; if this block is singular, both formulations may be inconsistent or may admit multiple corresponding solutions.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Fractional tie selections invalidate the stated coordinate-fixing reduction, while a singular inactive Jacobian block removes unique solvability but not the pure-selection solution-set correspondence.
assumptions_latex: The complementarity residual is represented by the componentwise minimum map.
The reduced system is the active/inactive coordinate-elimination system associated with a pure derivative selection.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Pure derivative selection is required for the stated coordinate reduction, and nonsingularity of \(F'(x)_{\mathcal I\mathcal I}\) is required for a unique corresponding Newton step.

notation.meaning: indices where the pure minimum derivative selects the primal variable
indices where the pure minimum derivative selects the multiplier

children.title: Function-Space Active-Set Equivalence
children.top_down_role: Active-set and semismooth-Newton correspondence for pointwise function-space constraints.

knowledge_statements.title: Function-Space Active-Set Equivalence
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Pointwise box-constraint equivalence for projection residuals on function spaces.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(U=L^p(\Omega)\), let \(a,b\in L^\infty(\Omega)\) satisfy \(a<b\) almost everywhere, and let \(G:U\to U\). For \(c>0\), define \(R(u)=u-P_{[a,b]}(u-cG(u))\). With \(w=u-cG(u)\), set \(\mathcal A_a=\{w\le a\}\), \(\mathcal A_b=\{w\ge b\}\), and \(\mathcal I=\{a<w<b\}\), modulo null sets. A pointwise Newton derivative of the projection imposes \(u+d=a\) on \(\mathcal A_a\), \(u+d=b\) on \(\mathcal A_b\), and the linearized equation \(G(u)+G'(u)d=0\) on \(\mathcal I\). These are precisely the primal-dual active-set update equations for the same partition.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A Newton derivative of the pointwise box projection produces the same bound fixing and inactive linearized equation as a function-space active-set update.
assumptions_latex: The projection superposition operator is Newton differentiable between the chosen function spaces.
\(G\) is Newton differentiable and the inactive linearized operator is invertible.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The projection-residual Newton step and the primal-dual active-set step coincide almost everywhere for the same derivative selection.

notation.meaning: pointwise projection onto the box interval
lower-active, upper-active, and inactive measurable sets

exact function-space mapping and norm-gap source required

children.title: Equivalence Failure Boundaries
children.top_down_role: Representation and degeneracy regimes disrupting direct method identification.

knowledge_statements.title: Equivalence Failure Boundaries
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Representation, regularity, and degeneracy boundaries for identifying active-set and semismooth-Newton iterations.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Direct iteration-by-iteration identification requires the same complementarity representation, the same generalized-derivative selection at switching points, and unique solvability of the selected Newton system. Equivalence may fail if two algebraically equivalent residuals have different generalized Jacobians, if a tie admits incompatible selections, if the selected Newton matrix is singular, or if globalization modifies one step but not the other. In function spaces it may also fail when the pointwise max, min, or projection operator is not Newton differentiable in the asserted domain and codomain norms. Equality of solution sets alone therefore does not imply equality of generated iterates.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Equivalent solution equations need not generate equivalent iterations when derivative selections, linear solvability, globalization, or function-space differentiability differ.
assumptions_latex: Two methods encode the same underlying complementarity conditions but may use different residuals or derivative selections.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Method equivalence is confined to regimes with compatible representations, compatible selections, and well-posed Newton subproblems.

children.title: Finite Active-Set Identification
children.top_down_role: Finite stabilization families for locally correct active sets.

children.title: Strictly Complementary Identification
children.top_down_role: Finite identification in separated primal-dual regimes.

knowledge_statements.title: Strictly Complementary Identification
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite identification by a convergent primal-dual sequence under a strict sign margin.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Consider lower-bound complementarity \(x\ge0\), \(\lambda\ge0\), and \(x_i\lambda_i=0\). Let \((x^k,\lambda^k)\to(x^*,\lambda^*)\), fix \(c>0\), and classify \(i\) as active when \(s_i^k=x_i^k-c\lambda_i^k\le0\). Suppose strict complementarity holds: for every \(i\), either \(x_i^*>0\) and \(\lambda_i^*=0\), or \(x_i^*=0\) and \(\lambda_i^*>0\). Then \(s_i^*\ne0\) for all \(i\). Hence there exists \(K\) such that, for every \(k\ge K\), the computed active set equals \(\{i:x_i^*=0\}\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Convergence plus strict complementarity gives a nonzero classification margin, so the active set is identified after finitely many iterations.
assumptions_latex: \((x^k,\lambda^k)\) converges to a complementary pair \((x^*,\lambda^*)\).
Strict complementarity holds at every index.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\exists K\;\forall k\ge K:\ \mathcal A_k=\{i:x_i^*=0\}\).

notation.meaning: indices classified active at iteration k

children.title: Polyhedral Identification

knowledge_statements.title: Polyhedral Identification
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite identification of the minimal active face under polyhedral nondegeneracy.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(C\subset\mathbb R^n\) be polyhedral, let \(x^k\in C\) and \(v^k\in N_C(x^k)\), and suppose \((x^k,v^k)\to(x^*,v^*)\). Let \(F\) be the minimal face of \(C\) containing \(x^*\). If \(v^*\in\operatorname{ri}N_C(x^*)\), then the normal pair lies in the locally identifiable stratum associated with \(F\). Consequently, there exists \(K\) such that \(x^k\in\operatorname{ri}F\) for every \(k\ge K\); equivalently, the active inequalities defining the face stabilize finitely.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: For a polyhedral feasible set, convergence of primal-normal pairs and relative-interior nondegeneracy force finite identification of the limiting face.
assumptions_latex: \(C\) is a nonempty polyhedral convex set.
\((x^k,v^k)\in\operatorname{gph}N_C\) converges to \((x^*,v^*)\).
\(v^*\in\operatorname{ri}N_C(x^*)\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\exists K\;\forall k\ge K:\ x^k\in\operatorname{ri}F\).

notation.meaning: convex-analytic normal cone to C at x
minimal face of C containing the limit point

children.title: Degenerate Activity Stabilization
children.top_down_role: Set stabilization when activity is not uniquely separated.

knowledge_statements.title: Degenerate Activity Stabilization
knowledge_statements.scope_note: A sufficient hysteresis condition for stabilizing classifications at degenerate indices.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(s_i^k=x_i^k-c\lambda_i^k\to s_i^*\), and let \(\tau_k>0\) satisfy \(\tau_k\to0\). Apply the hysteretic rule: declare inactive if \(s_i^k>\tau_k\), active if \(s_i^k<-\tau_k\), and otherwise retain the preceding classification. Suppose every degenerate index satisfies \(s_i^*=0\) and \(|s_i^k|\le\tau_k\) for all sufficiently large \(k\). Then every index with \(s_i^*\ne0\) eventually receives its limiting sign classification, and every degenerate index eventually retains a fixed classification. Thus the entire active set stabilizes after finitely many iterations, although its degenerate portion need not be unique.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: With thresholds tending to zero, hysteresis stabilizes degenerate indices that eventually remain inside the tie band, while separated indices acquire their limiting sign classification.
assumptions_latex: \(s_i^k\to s_i^*\) for every index.
\(\tau_k>0\) and \(\tau_k\to0\).
Every zero-limit score eventually remains within its hysteresis band.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\exists K\;\forall k\ge K:\ \mathcal A_{k+1}=\mathcal A_k\).
review_flags: standard_field_rationale: stabilization follows from threshold decay, convergence, retention, and eventual band containment

children.title: Activity Switching Failure Regimes
children.top_down_role: Persistent switching among competing activity patterns.

children.title: Active-Set Cycling
children.top_down_role: Repeated recurrence of previously visited activity patterns.

knowledge_statements.title: Active-Set Cycling
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact periodic recurrence of active-set states without termination.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \((\mathcal A_k)_{k\ge0}\) be the active-set sequence produced by an iterative method on a finite index set. The method exhibits active-set cycling from iteration \(K\) with period \(p\ge2\) if \[\mathcal A_{k+p}=\mathcal A_k\quad\text{for every }k\ge K,\] and no smaller positive integer has this property, while at least two sets among \(\mathcal A_K,\ldots,\mathcal A_{K+p-1}\) differ. Cycling is nonterminating when no state in this periodic orbit satisfies the method's stopping criterion.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Active-set cycling is a nonconstant periodic repetition of active sets, typically accompanied by failure to meet the stopping test.
assumptions_latex: The active-set sequence is indexed by iterations over a finite constraint index set.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Cycling is characterized by an eventual minimal period \(p\ge2\) and a nonconstant periodic orbit.

children.title: Activity Chattering
children.top_down_role: Rapid local switching among closely competing activity classifications.

knowledge_statements.title: Activity Chattering
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Infinitely repeated local switching without requiring an exact periodic orbit.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For an index \(i\), let \(a_i^k=1\) when \(i\in\mathcal A_k\) and \(a_i^k=0\) otherwise. Index \(i\) chatters if \[\#\{k\ge0:a_i^{k+1}\ne a_i^k\}=\infty.\] An active-set sequence chatters if at least one index chatters. Unlike cycling, chattering does not require any exact period or repetition of the complete iterate; it may occur when an activity score converges to zero while changing sign infinitely often.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Chattering means that at least one constraint switches active status infinitely often, possibly without any periodic repetition of full active sets or iterates.
assumptions_latex: An infinite sequence of active-set classifications is generated.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Activity chattering occurs exactly when some binary membership sequence has infinitely many transitions.

notation.meaning: binary activity indicator for index i

review_flags: standard_field_rationale: infinite switching is the standard mathematical distinction between chattering and finite stabilization

children.title: Switching-Pattern Diagnostics
children.top_down_role: Observable signatures used to distinguish persistent switching behaviors.

knowledge_statements.title: Switching-Pattern Diagnostics
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite-history diagnostics for periodic cycling and near-boundary chattering.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Given active sets \(\mathcal A_0,\ldots,\mathcal A_K\), activity scores \(s^0,\ldots,s^K\), a window length \(m\), tolerance \(\varepsilon\), and maximum tested period \(p_{\max}\), compute \(W_i=\sum_{k=K-m}^{K-1}\mathbf1\{\mathbf1_{\mathcal A_{k+1}}(i)\ne\mathbf1_{\mathcal A_k}(i)\}\). Report a period-\(p\) cycle candidate if \(\mathcal A_{K-j}=\mathcal A_{K-j-p}\) for every \(0\le j<p\) and some \(2\le p\le\min\{p_{\max},\lfloor(K+1)/2\rfloor\}\). Report a chattering candidate at index \(i\) if \(W_i\ge2\) and \(\max_{K-m\le k\le K}|s_i^k|\le\varepsilon\). Otherwise report no switching pattern detected. These finite-history outputs are diagnostics, not proofs of future behavior.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Count recent membership changes, compare two available consecutive active-set blocks for a possible cycle, and flag frequently switching indices whose scores remain near the activity boundary.
assumptions_latex: \(K\ge m\ge1\), \(p_{\max}\ge2\), and \(\varepsilon\ge0\).
Active sets and compatible activity scores are recorded for all indicated history indices.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The output is a cycle candidate, a set of chattering candidates, or no detected switching pattern.

notation.meaning: number of recent membership changes for index i

review_flags: standard_field_rationale: transition counts and repeated-block tests operationalize the preceding definitions
diagnostic thresholds and decision rules require an algorithmic source

children.title: Stabilization-Failure Regimes
children.top_down_role: Degenerate or poorly separated regimes where activity patterns do not stabilize.

knowledge_statements.title: Stabilization-Failure Regimes
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Sharp sign-oscillation mechanism preventing finite active-set stabilization.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A convergent activity score need not yield finite identification when its limit lies on the switching boundary. For one index, take \(s^k=(-1)^k/(k+1)\) and classify it as active exactly when \(s^k\le0\). Then \(s^k\to0\), but the classification changes at every iteration, so no \(K\) satisfies \(\mathcal A_{k+1}=\mathcal A_k\) for all \(k\ge K\). More generally, any index whose score crosses the decision boundary infinitely often prevents stabilization unless a tie-breaking, hysteresis, or comparable safeguarding rule suppresses those crossings.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Convergence to a degenerate boundary does not ensure identification: an activity score can approach zero while alternating sign and switching forever.
assumptions_latex: Activity is decided by the sign rule \(s^k\le0\).
No hysteresis or persistent tie-breaking rule is applied.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The sequence \(s^k=(-1)^k/(k+1)\) produces a nonstabilizing active-set classification despite \(s^k\to0\).

notation.meaning: scalar activity score for one constraint

review_flags: standard_field_rationale: the explicit alternating sequence directly verifies the claimed failure mechanism

children.title: Globalized Active-Set Methods
children.top_down_role: Active-set families equipped with merit or continuation mechanisms.

children.title: Merit-Globalized Active Sets
children.top_down_role: Active-set methods globalized through complementarity or residual merit functions.

knowledge_statements.title: Merit-Globalized Active Sets
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Residual-merit line-search globalization for a finite-dimensional active-set Newton iteration.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Given \(x_k\), select an active set and compute a generalized Newton direction \(d_k\) for \(F(x)=0\). Choose the first \(\alpha_k\in\{1,\beta,\beta^2,\ldots\}\), with fixed \(\beta\in(0,1)\), satisfying
\[
\Psi(x_k+\alpha_kd_k)\leq \Psi(x_k)+\sigma\alpha_k\Psi'(x_k;d_k),\qquad \sigma\in(0,1).
\]
Set \(x_{k+1}=x_k+\alpha_kd_k\), recompute the active set, and stop when \(\|F(x_k)\|_2\leq\varepsilon\). At every accepted nonterminal iteration, \(\Psi(x_{k+1})<\Psi(x_k)\). If an accumulation point \(\bar x\) is directionally stationary for \(\Psi\), and every directionally stationary point in the relevant level set is a root of \(F\), then \(F(\bar x)=0\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Compute an active-set Newton direction and backtrack until the residual merit satisfies the Armijo condition. Every accepted nonterminal step strictly decreases the merit. An accumulation point is a root only when it is directionally stationary and all such stationary points in the relevant level set are roots.
assumptions_latex: \(F:\mathbb{R}^n\to\mathbb{R}^n\) is locally Lipschitz, and the target system is \(F(x)=0\).
The merit function \(\Psi(x)=\tfrac12\|F(x)\|_2^2\) is directionally differentiable, and each accepted Newton or active-set direction \(d_k\) satisfies \(\Psi'(x_k;d_k)<0\) unless \(F(x_k)=0\).
The parameters satisfy \(\beta\in(0,1)\), \(\sigma\in(0,1)\), and \(\varepsilon\geq0\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: At every accepted nonterminal iteration, \(\Psi(x_{k+1})<\Psi(x_k)\). If an accumulation point \(\bar x\) is directionally stationary for \(\Psi\), and every directionally stationary point in the relevant level set is a root of \(F\), then \(F(\bar x)=0\).

notation.meaning: Complementarity or residual mapping whose zeros encode the active-set system.

children.title: Continuation Active Sets
children.top_down_role: Active-set methods embedded in regularization or penalty continuation.

assumptions_latex: For each \(\mu>0\), \(F_\mu:X\to Y\) is a regularized or penalized residual map between Banach spaces.
A schedule \(\mu_j\downarrow0\) and tolerances \(\tau_j\downarrow0\) is chosen so that approximate roots remain in the domain of the next-stage local solver.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The output is a sequence \((x_j,\mu_j)\) satisfying \(\|F_{\mu_j}(x_j)\|_Y\le\tau_j\). If \(x_j\to\bar x\) and the consistency condition \(F_{\mu_j}(x_j)\to F_0(\bar x)\) holds, then \(F_0(\bar x)=0\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Outer continuation with an active-set semismooth Newton solve at each parameter value.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Choose \(\mu_0>0\), an initial point \(x_{-1}\), and sequences \(\mu_j\downarrow0\) and \(\tau_j\downarrow0\). For \(j=0,1,\ldots\), initialize the active-set semismooth Newton solver for \(F_{\mu_j}(x)=0\) at \(x_{j-1}\), perform its active-set updates until
\[
\|F_{\mu_j}(x_j)\|_Y\le\tau_j,
\]
and warm-start the next stage with \(x_j\). Terminate when both \(\mu_j\le\varepsilon_\mu\) and \(\|F_{\mu_j}(x_j)\|_Y\le\varepsilon_F\). Consistency of \(F_\mu\) as \(\mu\downarrow0\) transfers convergent continuation sequences to roots of the limiting system.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Solve a sequence of regularized active-set systems, warm-starting each stage from the preceding solution while decreasing both the continuation parameter and inner tolerance.
knowledge_statements.title: Continuation Active Sets

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The algorithm fits the continuation leaf, but no source supports the continuation schedule, warm-start conditions, or limiting consistency claim.

children.title: Active-Set Application Cross-Indexes
children.top_down_role: Interfaces from active-set theory to major variational-inequality application classes.

children.title: Obstacle-Problem Active-Set Cross-Index
children.top_down_role: Navigation from active-set theory to obstacle-problem Newton and dual formulations.

assumptions_latex: \(V\) is a real Hilbert space, \(K=\{v\in V:v\ge\psi\}\), and \(A:V\to V^*\) defines the obstacle variational inequality.
A primal-dual pair \((u,\lambda)\) satisfies \(Au-f-\lambda=0\), \(u-\psi\ge0\), \(\lambda\ge0\), and \(\langle\lambda,u-\psi\rangle=0\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The obstacle variational inequality, its primal-dual complementarity system, and the projection equation have the same solutions under the stated identification of \(V\) and \(V^*\). Consequently, a semismooth Newton active-set partition is obtained from the sign of \(\lambda-c(u-\psi)\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Primal-dual complementarity representation underlying obstacle-problem active sets.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
The variational inequality
\[
u\in K,\qquad \langle Au-f,v-u\rangle\ge0\quad\text{for every }v\in K
\]
is represented by
\[
Au-f-\lambda=0,
\qquad u-\psi\ge0,
\qquad \lambda\ge0,
\qquad \langle\lambda,u-\psi\rangle=0.
\]
Whenever the pointwise positive part is defined in the chosen function-space realization, complementarity is equivalently expressed, for any \(c>0\), as
\[
\lambda-[\lambda-c(u-\psi)]_+=0.
\]
The induced active set is \(\mathcal A_c=\{\lambda-c(u-\psi)>0\}\), with \(u=\psi\) imposed there and \(\lambda=0\) on its complement.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: An obstacle variational inequality is equivalently a primal-dual complementarity system whose positive-part equation directly defines the active and inactive regions.
knowledge_statements.title: Obstacle-Problem Active-Set Cross-Index

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The representation fits the obstacle cross-index, but its pointwise order, positive-part map, multiplier space, and identification of the Hilbert space with its dual require an obstacle-specific source and precise function-space hypotheses.

children.title: Contact-Problem Active-Set Cross-Index
children.top_down_role: Navigation from active-set theory to unilateral and complementarity contact systems.

assumptions_latex: \(V\) is a real Hilbert space, \(B:V\to Q\) is the normal-gap operator, and \(g(u)=Bu-b\) is constrained by \(g(u)\ge0\).
The equilibrium equation is \(Au-f-B^*\lambda=0\), with contact pressure \(\lambda\ge0\) paired with \(g(u)\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The unilateral contact conditions are equivalent to the positive-part residual equation, and its sign partition identifies contact and noncontact regions for a primal-dual active-set or semismooth Newton iteration.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Complementarity representation for frictionless unilateral contact with a fixed sign convention.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
With the convention that positive \(g(u)it\) means separation and positive \(\lambda\) means compressive pressure, unilateral contact is
\[
Au-f-B^*\lambda=0,
\qquad g(u)\ge0,
\qquad \lambda\ge0,
\qquad \langle\lambda,g(u)\rangle=0.
\]
For any \(c>0\), the complementarity conditions are represented pointwise by
\[
\lambda-[\lambda-cg(u)]_+=0.
\]
Thus \(\mathcal A_c=\{\lambda-cg(u)>0\}\) is the candidate contact set, where the Newton active-set step imposes \(g(u)=0\); on \(\mathcal I_c=\Omega\setminus\mathcal A_c\), it imposes \(\lambda=0\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Frictionless unilateral contact becomes a positive-part complementarity equation whose sign test divides the domain into contact and noncontact regions.
knowledge_statements.title: Contact-Problem Active-Set Cross-Index

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The contact representation is plausible but unsupported. The expression “\(g(u)it\)” is corrupted, the space containing \(\lambda\) is not introduced, and the mechanical sign convention and pointwise positive-part formulation require a contact-specific source.

children.title: Semismooth Operators in Banach Spaces
children.top_down_role: Operator-level semismoothness and generalized differential structures.

assumptions_latex: \(X\) and \(Y\) are Banach spaces, \(U\subset X\) is open, and \(F:U\to Y\).
\(\mathcal G:U\rightrightarrows\mathcal L(X,Y)\) has nonempty values near \(x\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The displayed remainder condition defines semismoothness relative to \(\mathcal G\); replacing \(o(\|h\|_X)\) by \(O(\|h\|_X^{1+\gamma})\), with \(\gamma\in(0,1]\), defines semismoothness of order \(\gamma\).

notation.meaning: Space of bounded linear operators from X to Y.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Newton-type semismoothness relative to an operator-valued generalized differential.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
The mapping \(F\) is semismooth at \(x\in U\) relative to \(\mathcal G\) if \(F\) is locally Lipschitz near \(x\), directionally differentiable at \(x\), and
\[
\sup_{G\in\mathcal G(x+h)}
\frac{\|F(x+h)-F(x)-Gh\|_Y}{\|h\|_X}
\longrightarrow0
\quad\text{as }h\to0,
\]
where the quotient is considered only for nonzero \(h\) with \(x+h\in U\). A single-valued selection \(G(x+h)\in\mathcal G(x+h)\) is a Newton derivative when the same limit holds for that selection.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A Banach-space operator is semismooth when every nearby generalized derivative linearizes its increment with an error negligible relative to the perturbation norm.
knowledge_statements.title: Semismooth Operators in Banach Spaces

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: This is an appropriate definition for the leaf, but Banach-space semismoothness and Newton differentiability have materially different variants. A dedicated source must verify the simultaneous local-Lipschitz, directional-differentiability, and supremum-over-all-generalized-derivatives formulation.

children.title: Banach-Space Semismooth Newton Method
children.top_down_role: The basic semismooth Newton family for Banach-space operator equations.

assumptions_latex: \(F:U\subset X\to Y\) is semismooth relative to \(\mathcal G\), and the equation is \(F(x)=0\).
For each iterate, an operator \(G_k\in\mathcal G(x_k)\) is selected and the linear equation \(G_ks=-F(x_k)\) is solvable.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: If the iteration reaches \(F(x_k)=0\), it returns a root. Local superlinear convergence requires semismoothness at a root and uniformly bounded inverses of the selected generalized derivatives near that root.

notation.meaning: Selected generalized derivative at the current iterate.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact local semismooth Newton iteration for a Banach-space operator equation.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Given \(x_0\in U\) and a tolerance \(\varepsilon\ge0\), repeat while \(\|F(x_k)\|_Y>\varepsilon\): choose \(G_k\in\mathcal G(x_k)\), solve
\[
G_ks_k=-F(x_k),
\]
and set \(x_{k+1}=x_k+s_k\), provided \(x_k+s_k\in U\). Stop and return \(x_k\) when the residual tolerance is met. If \(x_*\) is a root, \(F\) is semismooth at \(x_*\), and all admissible \(G\in\mathcal G(x)\) near \(x_*\) are invertible with uniformly bounded inverses, then sufficiently close iterates converge superlinearly to \(x_*\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Select a generalized derivative, solve the linearized operator equation, and add the correction; uniform local invertibility and semismoothness yield superlinear local convergence.
knowledge_statements.title: Banach-Space Semismooth Newton Method

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The iteration fits the algorithm leaf, but the superlinear convergence assertion needs a source confirming the precise semismoothness notion, admissible generalized differential, neighborhood invariance, and uniform inverse hypotheses.

children.title: Banach-Space Inexact Semismooth Newton
children.top_down_role: Function-space semismooth Newton methods with approximate local solves.

assumptions_latex: \(F:U\subset X\to Y\) is semismooth near a root, and selected \(G_k\in\mathcal G(x_k)\) have uniformly bounded inverses.
The forcing terms satisfy \(0\le\eta_k<1\); for superlinear convergence, \(\eta_k\to0\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: For sufficiently close initialization, the residual-controlled inexact iteration is locally convergent. It is superlinearly convergent when \(\eta_k\to0\), subject to the stated semismoothness and uniform inverse bounds.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Residual-forced inexact semismooth Newton iteration in Banach spaces.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Given \(x_0\in U\), at iteration \(k\) select \(G_k\in\mathcal G(x_k)\) and compute \(s_k\in X\) such that
\[
r_k:=G_ks_k+F(x_k),
\qquad
\|r_k\|_Y\le\eta_k\|F(x_k)\|_Y.
\]
Set \(x_{k+1}=x_k+s_k\) and stop when \(\|F(x_k)\|_Y\le\varepsilon\). Uniformly bounded inverse operators and forcing terms bounded strictly below one give the local contraction mechanism; the stronger condition \(\eta_k\to0\), together with semismoothness, yields superlinear local convergence.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The Newton equation may be solved approximately when its linear residual is controlled by a forcing fraction of the nonlinear residual; vanishing forcing terms recover superlinear convergence.
knowledge_statements.title: Banach-Space Inexact Semismooth Newton

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The inexact Newton residual condition fits the leaf. However, forcing terms merely bounded below one do not by themselves state a quantitatively sufficient contraction condition for the general Banach-space formulation; the local and superlinear claims require a dedicated source.

children.title: Projected Inexact Operator Newton
children.top_down_role: Projected inexact semismooth Newton methods in Banach spaces.

assumptions_latex: \(C\subset X\) is nonempty and admits a continuous retraction \(P_C:X\to C\), and \(F:U\to Y\) is semismooth on a neighborhood of \(C\cap U\).
At \(x_k\in C\), an inexact correction satisfies \(\|G_ks_k+F(x_k)\|_Y\le\eta_k\|F(x_k)\|_Y\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Every iterate lies in \(C\). Any returned point satisfies the residual stopping test, while local convergence requires compatibility of the retraction, the constrained solution, and the generalized linearizations.

notation.meaning: Retraction or projection onto the feasible set.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Feasibility-preserving projection of an inexact operator Newton trial point.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Choose \(x_0\in C\cap U\), a tolerance \(\varepsilon\ge0\), and forcing terms \(\eta_k\in[0,1)\). While \(\|F(x_k)\|_Y>\varepsilon\), select \(G_k\in\mathcal G(x_k)\), compute \(s_k\) satisfying
\[
\|G_ks_k+F(x_k)\|_Y\le\eta_k\|F(x_k)\|_Y,
\]
and update
\[
x_{k+1}=P_C(x_k+s_k).
\]
Stop when the residual tolerance is met. Because \(P_C(X)\subset C\), feasibility is preserved. A convergence assertion additionally requires local regularity of the constrained equation and stability of \(P_C\) near its solution.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Compute an inexact generalized Newton correction and retract the trial point onto the feasible set, thereby preserving feasibility at every iteration.
knowledge_statements.title: Projected Inexact Operator Newton

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The feasibility-preserving update fits the projected-algorithm leaf, but an arbitrary continuous retraction is too broad for a sourced projected Newton method. The intended projection geometry and compatibility conditions require specification and evidence.

children.title: Alternative Operator Regularity
children.top_down_role: Function-space regularity routes beyond direct generalized differential invertibility.

assumptions_latex: \(X,Y\) are Banach spaces and the problem is the generalized equation \(0\in F(x)+Q(x)\), with \(F:X\to Y\) and \(Q:X\rightrightarrows Y\).
At a solution \(x_*\), a linearization \(G_*\) of \(F\) is available.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Strong metric regularity of the linearized generalized equation supplies a locally single-valued Lipschitz solution map for perturbed inclusions, providing a regularity route that does not require \(G_*:X\to Y\) itself to be invertible.

notation.meaning: Set-valued part of the generalized equation.
Reference linearization of the single-valued part.
Localized solution mapping of the linearized inclusion.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Strong metric regularity of a linearized generalized equation as an alternative Newton regularity condition.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Define the linearized solution mapping
\[
S(y):=\{x\in X:y\in F(x_*)+G_*(x-x_*)+Q(x)\}.
\]
The linearized generalized equation is strongly metrically regular at \((x_*,0)\) when neighborhoods \(U\) of \(x_*\) and \(V\) of \(0\) exist such that \(S(y)\cap U\) is a singleton for every \(y\in V\), and the resulting mapping \(s:V\to U\) is Lipschitz. This condition replaces direct invertibility of \(G_*\) by stable local solvability of the complete linearized inclusion.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Strong metric regularity requires the perturbed linearized inclusion to have a unique Lipschitz-localized solution, even when the linear operator alone is not invertible.
knowledge_statements.title: Alternative Operator Regularity

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The condition fits the alternative-regularity leaf and resembles strong metric regularity of the complete linearized generalized equation, but the exact localization, base point, and perturbation convention need an authoritative source.

children.title: Superposition-Operator Calculus
children.top_down_role: Generalized differentials and semismoothness for pointwise nonlinear operators.

children.title: Generalized Differentials for Superposition Operators
children.top_down_role: Newton derivative constructions for pointwise operator mappings.

assumptions_latex: \((\Omega,\Sigma,\mu)\) is a measure space and \(1\le p,q\le\infty\).
The scalar map \(\phi:\Omega\times\mathbb R\to\mathbb R\) is measurable in its first argument and admits measurable generalized derivative selections \(a(\omega,t)\).
For each relevant \(u\), multiplication by \(a(\cdot,u(\cdot))\) defines a bounded operator from \(L^p(\Omega)\) to \(L^q(\Omega)\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The generalized differential candidate for the superposition operator at \(u\) consists of multiplication operators generated by admissible measurable pointwise selections from the scalar generalized differential.

notation.meaning: Superposition operator induced by the scalar integrand.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Pointwise generalized derivatives lifted to bounded multiplication operators between Lebesgue spaces.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let
\[
(\Phi(u))(\omega)=\phi(\omega,u(\omega))
\]
whenever the right-hand side belongs to \(L^q(\Omega)\). For an admissible measurable selection satisfying
\[
a(\omega,u(\omega))\in\partial_N\phi(\omega,u(\omega))
\quad\text{for almost every }\omega,
\]
define
\[
(M_a(u)h)(\omega)=a(\omega,u(\omega))h(\omega).
\]
Provided \(M_a(u)\in\mathcal L(L^p,L^q)\), the collection of all such multiplication operators is the pointwise-lifted generalized differential \(\mathcal G_\Phi(u)\) used in a Newton linearization of \(\Phi\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A pointwise generalized derivative of a scalar nonlinearity lifts to a multiplication operator, provided the measurable selection acts boundedly between the chosen function spaces.
knowledge_statements.title: Generalized Differentials for Superposition Operators

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The multiplication-operator representation fits the leaf, but \(\partial_N\) is not defined and no source establishes which scalar generalized differential, measurable-selection conditions, or growth bounds produce the asserted operator differential.

children.title: Semismoothness of Superposition Operators
children.top_down_role: Semismoothness regimes for pointwise nonlinear operators between function spaces.

assumptions_latex: \(1\le q<p<\infty\), \(\mu(\Omega)<\infty\), and \(\Phi:L^p(\Omega)\to L^q(\Omega)\) is induced by \(\phi(\omega,t)\).
The scalar maps are uniformly semismooth on bounded \(t\)-sets almost everywhere, with measurable derivative selections having growth sufficient to define bounded multipliers from \(L^p\) to \(L^q\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Under these uniform remainder and growth conditions, the superposition operator is Newton semismooth from \(L^p(\Omega)\) to \(L^q(\Omega)\) relative to the pointwise multiplication operators.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: A norm-gap sufficient regime for semismooth superposition operators on finite-measure domains.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
For \(u,h\in L^p(\Omega)\), define the pointwise remainder
\[
r(u,h)=\Phi(u+h)-\Phi(u)-M_a(u+h)h,
\]
where \(M_a(u+h)\) is an admissible pointwise generalized derivative. If the scalar semismooth remainder is uniform on bounded scalar sets and the derivative growth provides an \(L^q\)-integrable domination for bounded \(L^p\)-sequences, then the norm gap \(q<p\) yields
\[
\sup_{M_a(u+h)\in\mathcal G_\Phi(u+h)}
\frac{\|r(u,h)\|_{L^q}}{\|h\|_{L^p}}\longrightarrow0
\quad\text{as }\|h\|_{L^p}\to0.
\]
Thus \(\Phi\) is semismooth from \(L^p\) to \(L^q\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Uniform pointwise semismoothness, suitable growth, and a strict integrability gap can lift scalar semismoothness to a superposition operator between Lebesgue spaces.
knowledge_statements.title: Semismoothness of Superposition Operators

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The property belongs in this leaf, but phrases such as “uniform on bounded scalar sets” and “growth provides an integrable domination” are not precise enough to verify the displayed supremum limit. Exact exponents and domination hypotheses require a source.

children.title: Two-Norm Semismoothness
children.top_down_role: Semismoothness using distinct norms for perturbations and residuals.

assumptions_latex: \(X\) is a vector space equipped with a perturbation norm \(\|\cdot\|_X\), and \(Y\) is equipped with a residual norm \(\|\cdot\|_Y\).
\(F:U\subset X\to Y\) and \(\mathcal G(x)\subset\mathcal L(X,Y)\) is nonempty near \(x\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The displayed mixed-norm remainder limit defines two-norm semismoothness. It permits a stronger norm to measure perturbations and a weaker norm to measure residuals, while Newton convergence additionally requires stability of the linear solves in these norms.

notation.meaning: Norm measuring nonlinear remainders and residuals.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Mixed-norm Newton remainder condition for function-space mappings.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
The mapping \(F\) is two-norm semismooth at \(x\in U\), relative to \(\mathcal G\), when
\[
\sup_{G\in\mathcal G(x+h)}
\frac{\|F(x+h)-F(x)-Gh\|_Y}{\|h\|_X}
\longrightarrow0
\quad\text{as }\|h\|_X\to0,
\]
for nonzero admissible perturbations \(h\). The domain norm controls the size of the Newton perturbation, whereas the codomain norm measures the linearization error. The two norms need not arise from the same function-space exponent or topology, but every \(G\) used in the quotient must act boundedly from \(X\) to \(Y\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Two-norm semismoothness measures perturbations in one norm and linearization errors in another, requiring the mixed-norm remainder to be little-o of the perturbation size.
knowledge_statements.title: Two-Norm Semismoothness

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The content kind fits the leaf, but the statement may conflate ordinary semismoothness between distinct domain and codomain Banach spaces with the specialized two-norm framework, which commonly involves different topologies on the relevant function-space variables. A dedicated source is required before fixing the definition.

children.title: Semismooth Composite-Operator Rules
children.top_down_role: Composition and chain-rule structures for semismooth operators.

assumptions_latex: \(X,Y,Z\) are Banach spaces, \(H:X\to Y\) is continuously Fréchet differentiable near \(\bar x\).
\(F:Y\to Z\) is Newton differentiable near \(H(\bar x)\), with Newton derivative selection \(G_F\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(F\circ H\) is Newton differentiable at \(\bar x\) with derivative selection \(G_{F\circ H}(x)=G_F(H(x))H'(x)\).

notation.meaning: Newton derivative selection for the outer operator

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Banach-space chain rule with a smooth inner operator and a semismooth outer operator.

source_refs.source_title: Finite-Dimensional Variational Inequalities and Complementarity Problems, Vol. II

knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
For \(x\) near \(\bar x\), define \(G_{F\circ H}(x):=G_F(H(x))H'(x)\). Then
\[
\|(F\circ H)(x+h)-(F\circ H)(x)-G_{F\circ H}(x+h)h\|_Z=o(\|h\|_X)
\]
as \(h\to0\). Hence composition with a continuously Fréchet differentiable inner map preserves Newton differentiability. If the remainder for \(F\) is of order \(O(\|k\|_Y^{1+\alpha})\) and \(H'\) is locally Hölder continuous of order \(\alpha\), then the composite remainder has order \(O(\|h\|_X^{1+\alpha})\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Composing a semismooth outer operator with a continuously differentiable inner operator preserves Newton differentiability, with generalized derivative obtained by the operator chain rule.
knowledge_statements.title: Semismooth Composite-Operator Rules

source_witnesses.source_title: Finite-Dimensional Variational Inequalities and Complementarity Problems, Vol. II

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The mathematical claim is plausible, but the cited source is explicitly finite-dimensional while the record asserts a Banach-space Newton-differentiability chain rule and an order-alpha remainder result. The plain statement also calls the outer map semismooth whereas the formal assumptions specify Newton differentiability. An inspectable function-space source fixing the precise derivative convention and higher-order hypotheses is required.

children.title: Superposition-Operator Failure Regimes
children.top_down_role: Loss of operator semismoothness through incompatible spaces, norms, or growth behavior.

assumptions_latex: \(1\le p<\infty\), \(\Omega=(-1,1)\), and \(N(u)=\max\{0,u\}\) acts from \(L^p(\Omega)\) to itself.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The usual active-set derivative \(G(v)h=\mathbf 1_{\{v>0\}}h\) does not make \(N:L^p(\Omega)\to L^p(\Omega)\) Newton differentiable.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Concrete same-norm obstruction for the positive-part superposition operator.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(u(t)=t\) and \(h_n(t)=-2t\mathbf 1_{(0,1/n)}(t)\). On \((0,1/n)\), one has \(u+h_n=-t<0\), so \(G(u+h_n)h_n=0\), while
\[
N(u+h_n)-N(u)-G(u+h_n)h_n=-t\mathbf 1_{(0,1/n)}(t).
\]
Consequently,
\[
\frac{\|N(u+h_n)-N(u)-G(u+h_n)h_n\|_{L^p}}{\|h_n\|_{L^p}}=\frac12
\]
for every \(n\), although \(h_n\to0\) in \(L^p\). Thus the required Newton remainder is not little-oh in the same norm; a norm gap or stronger domain control is essential.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The positive-part superposition operator can fail Newton differentiability when domain and range use the same Lebesgue norm, because errors concentrated near switching points do not decay relatively.
knowledge_statements.title: Superposition-Operator Failure Regimes

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The displayed sequence correctly shows that the stated active-set selection fails the Newton remainder test at the chosen function. It does not by itself establish failure for every admissible generalized derivative, and the assertion that a norm gap or stronger domain control is essential is broader than the example. No source is supplied for the intended operator-level failure boundary.

children.title: Function-Space Bound Constraints
children.top_down_role: Projection and active-set equations for pointwise bounds.

assumptions_latex: \(U=L^2(\Omega)\), and \(a,b\in L^2(\Omega)\) satisfy \(a\le b\) almost everywhere.
\(K=\{u\in U:a\le u\le b\ \text{almost everywhere}\}\), \(g\in U\), and \(c>0\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: For \(u\in K\), the inclusion \(0\in g+N_K(u)\) holds if and only if \(u=P_K(u-cg)\), and \(P_K\) is given by pointwise clipping between \(a\) and \(b\).

notation.meaning: metric projection onto the admissible set
convex normal cone to the admissible set

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Projection representation of first-order conditions for measurable pointwise bounds in a Hilbert function space.

source_refs.locator: 7.4 Minimax Control of Parabolic Systems with Pointwise State Constraints p. 398
source_refs.source_title: Variational Analysis and Generalized Differentiation II

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For \(u\in K\), the variational inequality \[\langle g,v-u\rangle_U\ge 0\qquad\text{for every }v\in K\] is equivalent to \(0\in g+N_K(u)\). For every \(c>0\), these conditions are also equivalent to \[u-P_K(u-cg)=0.\] The metric projection is the superposition operator \[(P_Kw)(\omega)=\min\{b(\omega),\max\{a(\omega),w(\omega)\}\}\] for almost every \(\omega\). Thus the lower-active, inactive, and upper-active regions are determined by whether \(u-cg\) lies below \(a\), between \(a\) and \(b\), or above \(b\), respectively.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A pointwise box-constrained variational inequality is equivalent to a projection equation whose clipping formula identifies the lower-active, inactive, and upper-active regions.
knowledge_statements.title: Function-Space Bound Constraints

source_witnesses.locator: 7.4 Minimax Control of Parabolic Systems with Pointwise State Constraints p. 398

children.title: Function-Space Pointwise Convex Constraints
children.top_down_role: Operator equations for general pointwise convex constraint sets.

assumptions_latex: \(U=L^2(\Omega;\mathbb R^m)\), and \(C(\omega)\subset\mathbb R^m\) is nonempty, closed, convex, and measurably varying.
\(K=\{u\in U:u(\omega)\in C(\omega)\ \text{a.e.}\}\), \(g\in U\), and \(c>0\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(0\in g+N_K(u)\) is equivalent to \(u(\omega)=P_{C(\omega)}(u(\omega)-cg(\omega))\) almost everywhere.

notation.meaning: Euclidean projection onto the fiber constraint

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Decomposable convex constraints represented by a pointwise metric-projection equation.

source_refs.locator: 5.1.2 Necessary Conditions under Operator Constraints p. 9
source_refs.source_title: Variational Analysis and Generalized Differentiation II

knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
For \(u\in K\), the inclusion \(0\in g+N_K(u)\) is equivalent to
\[
u=P_K(u-cg).
\]
Because \(K\) is decomposable and its fibers are closed and convex, its metric projection is pointwise:
\[
(P_Kw)(\omega)=P_{C(\omega)}(w(\omega))
\]
for almost every \(\omega\). Therefore the mixed variational condition has the operator-equation form
\[
u(\omega)-P_{C(\omega)}(u(\omega)-cg(\omega))=0
\]
almost everywhere. For polyhedral fibers, generalized derivatives of this residual are determined by the faces active at each \(\omega\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A decomposable pointwise convex constraint yields a projection equation evaluated independently in each fiber; polyhedral fibers additionally provide face-based generalized derivatives.
knowledge_statements.title: Function-Space Pointwise Convex Constraints

assumptions_latex: \(Y,U,Z\) are Hilbert spaces, \(J:Y\times U\to\mathbb R\) and \(E:Y\times U\to Z\) are continuously Fréchet differentiable.
\(K\subset U\) is nonempty, closed, and convex, and \((y,u,p)\in Y\times K\times Z\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The equality-constrained KKT conditions and the control variational inequality are represented by one coupled primal-adjoint-projection operator equation.

knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
For any fixed \(c>0\), define
\[
\mathcal F(y,u,p)=\bigl(E(y,u),\ D_y\mathcal L(y,u,p),\ u-P_K(u-cD_u\mathcal L(y,u,p))\bigr).
\]
Then \(\mathcal F(y,u,p)=0\) is equivalent to
\[
E(y,u)=0,\qquad D_y\mathcal L(y,u,p)=0,\qquad 0\in D_u\mathcal L(y,u,p)+N_K(u).
\]
Thus the state equation, adjoint equation, and constrained stationarity condition form a single mixed operator system. When \(P_K\) is semismooth between the selected function spaces, \(\mathcal F\) is a candidate semismooth Newton residual.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: State feasibility, adjoint stationarity, and constrained control stationarity combine into a coupled primal-dual operator equation using the metric projection onto the feasible set.

children.title: Reduced Operator Systems
children.top_down_role: Operator formulations obtained by eliminating selected mixed variables.

assumptions_latex: \(Y\) and \(Z\) are Banach spaces, \(U\) is a Hilbert space, \(J:Y\times U\to\mathbb R\), and \(E:Y\times U\to Z\).
The equation \(E(y,u)=0\) has a locally unique solution \(y=S(u)\), where \(S\) is continuously Fréchet differentiable.
\(K\subset U\) is nonempty, closed, and convex; \(j(u)=J(S(u),u)\) is Fréchet differentiable, its derivative is identified with its Riesz representative in \(U\), and \(c>0\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: For \(u\in K\), reduced stationarity is equivalent to the reduced operator equation \(R(u)=u-P_K(u-cj'(u))=0\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: State-eliminated projection system for a locally single-valued control-to-state map.

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Eliminating the state through \(y=S(u)\) gives the reduced objective \(j(u)=J(S(u),u)\). Define \[R(u):=u-P_K(u-cj'(u)).\] For \(u\in K\), the reduced variational inequality \[\langle j'(u),v-u\rangle_U\ge 0\qquad\text{for every }v\in K\] holds if and only if \(R(u)=0\). Thus the state-eliminated constrained stationarity conditions are represented by a single operator equation in the control variable.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: When the state is locally and uniquely determined by the control, eliminating it produces a reduced projection residual whose zeros are exactly the reduced stationary controls.

children.title: Full Operator Systems
children.top_down_role: Coupled operator formulations retaining the complete mixed-variable structure.

assumptions_latex: \(Y,U,Z\) are Hilbert spaces, \(J:Y\times U\to\mathbb R\) and \(E:Y\times U\to Z\) are continuously Fréchet differentiable.
\(K\subset U\) is nonempty, closed, and convex; \(c>0\), and \((y,u,p)\in Y\times K\times Z\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The state equation, adjoint equation, and projected control stationarity condition are represented by the three-block equation \(F_{\mathrm{full}}(y,u,p)=0\) in \(Z\times Y\times U\).

notation.meaning: metric projection onto the control constraint

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Unreduced primal-adjoint-control operator system for convexly constrained optimization in Hilbert spaces.

source_refs.source_title: Finite-Dimensional Variational Inequalities and Complementarity Problems, Vol. II

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Define \[F_{\mathrm{full}}(y,u,p):=\begin{pmatrix}E(y,u)\\ J_y(y,u)+E_y(y,u)^*p\\ u-P_K\bigl(u-c[J_u(y,u)+E_u(y,u)^*p]\bigr)\end{pmatrix}\in Z\times Y\times U.\] Then \(F_{\mathrm{full}}(y,u,p)=0\) if and only if \[E(y,u)=0,\qquad J_y(y,u)+E_y(y,u)^*p=0,\] and \[0\in J_u(y,u)+E_u(y,u)^*p+N_K(u).\] Hence the full formulation retains the state, control, and adjoint as unknowns in one coupled operator system.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The full formulation retains state, control, and adjoint variables and combines primal feasibility, adjoint stationarity, and constrained control stationarity in a three-block operator equation.
knowledge_statements.title: Full Operator Systems

children.title: Operator-Elimination Correspondence
children.top_down_role: Structural correspondence between reduced and coupled realizations.

assumptions_latex: \(Y,U,Z\) are Hilbert spaces, \(J:Y\times U\to\mathbb R\) and \(E:Y\times U\to Z\) are continuously Fréchet differentiable near \((\bar y,\bar u)\), and \(E(\bar y,\bar u)=0\).
The operator \(E_y(\bar y,\bar u):Y\to Z\) is a bounded linear isomorphism, so \(E(y,u)=0\) defines a continuously Fréchet differentiable local map \(y=S(u)\).
\(K\subset U\) is nonempty, closed, and convex, \(c>0\), and the reduced and full residuals are defined using the same projection \(P_K\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Near \((\bar y,\bar u)\), the map \(u\mapsto(S(u),u,p(u))\), where \(p(u)\) is the unique adjoint solution, gives a one-to-one correspondence between zeros of the reduced and full residuals.

notation.meaning: unique adjoint associated with a control

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Local equivalence obtained by eliminating uniquely solvable state and adjoint equations.

source_refs.locator: 7.2.2 Analysis of State and Adjoint Systems in the Neumann Problem p. 369
source_refs.source_title: Variational Analysis and Generalized Differentiation II

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: The implicit-function relation gives \[S'(u)=-E_y(S(u),u)^{-1}E_u(S(u),u).\] Let \(p(u)\in Z\) be the unique solution of \[E_y(S(u),u)^*p(u)+J_y(S(u),u)=0.\] For \(j(u)=J(S(u),u)\), the reduced derivative is \[j'(u)=J_u(S(u),u)+E_u(S(u),u)^*p(u).\] Define \[R(u)=u-P_K(u-cj'(u))\] and let \(F_{\mathrm{full}}\) be the corresponding state-adjoint-projection residual. Then, locally, \[R(u)=0\quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad F_{\mathrm{full}}(S(u),u,p(u))=0.\] Conversely, every nearby zero \((y,u,p)\) of \(F_{\mathrm{full}}\) satisfies \(y=S(u)\), \(p=p(u)\), and \(R(u)=0\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Invertibility of the state linearization permits unique local elimination of state and adjoint variables, giving a one-to-one correspondence between nearby full KKT zeros and reduced stationary controls.
knowledge_statements.title: Operator-Elimination Correspondence

children.title: Operator-Equivalence Boundaries
children.top_down_role: Functional or regularity regimes limiting equivalence between the realizations.

assumptions_latex: \(E(y,u)=y^2-u\) is considered on \(\mathbb R\times\mathbb R\) at \((\bar y,\bar u)=(0,0)\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: A locally single-valued differentiable control-to-state map does not exist at \((0,0)\), so reduced-full operator equivalence based on smooth elimination fails.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Loss of elimination equivalence when the state equation is singular or multivalued.

knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
For \(u>0\), the equation \(E(y,u)=0\) has the two solutions \(y=\sqrt u\) and \(y=-\sqrt u\), whereas for \(u<0\) it has no real solution. Moreover,
\[
E_y(0,0)=0,
\]
so the implicit-function hypothesis required for a differentiable map \(y=S(u)\) fails. Neither branch has a bounded derivative as \(u\downarrow0\). Therefore a reduced residual based on smooth state elimination is not locally equivalent to the full operator system at \((0,0)\); branch selection, solvability, or singular adjoint equations must be handled separately.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: At a singular, branching state equation, no smooth single-valued state elimination exists, so reduced and full operator systems need not be locally equivalent.
knowledge_statements.title: Operator-Equivalence Boundaries

children.title: Mixed-Problem Smoothing Families

assumptions_latex: \((\Omega,\mathcal A,\nu)\) is a finite measure space, \(a,b\in L^\infty(\Omega)\), and \(\mu>0\).
Pointwise complementarity means \(a(\omega)\ge 0\), \(b(\omega)\ge 0\), and \(a(\omega)b(\omega)=0\) for almost every \(\omega\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The scalar function \(\phi_\mu\) is continuously differentiable for every \(\mu>0\), its superposition operator \(\Phi_\mu:L^\infty(\Omega)^2\to L^2(\Omega)\) is continuously Fréchet differentiable, and \(\Phi_\mu(a,b)\to\Phi_0(a,b)\) in \(L^2(\Omega)\) as \(\mu\downarrow0\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Fischer-Burmeister smoothing applied pointwise, with an explicit function-space mapping in which scalar smoothness induces operator differentiability.

source_refs.locator: Chapter 11. Interior and Smoothing Methods p. 989
source_refs.source_title: Finite-Dimensional Variational Inequalities and Complementarity Problems, Vol. II

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Define \[\phi_\mu(s,t)=\sqrt{s^2+t^2+2\mu^2}-s-t\] and \[(\Phi_\mu(a,b))(\omega)=\phi_\mu(a(\omega),b(\omega)).\] For every \(\mu>0\), the scalar function \(\phi_\mu\) is continuously differentiable on \(\mathbb R^2\). On a finite measure space, the associated map \(\Phi_\mu:L^\infty(\Omega)^2\to L^2(\Omega)\) is continuously Fréchet differentiable. Moreover, \[\|\Phi_\mu(a,b)-\Phi_0(a,b)\|_{L^2}\le \sqrt{2}\,\mu\,\nu(\Omega)^{1/2},\] so \(\Phi_\mu(a,b)\to\Phi_0(a,b)\) in \(L^2(\Omega)\) as \(\mu\downarrow0\). The zero set of \(\phi_0\) is exactly the set of \((s,t)\) satisfying \(s\ge0\), \(t\ge0\), and \(st=0\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Fischer-Burmeister smoothing gives a differentiable pointwise complementarity residual for positive smoothing parameters and converges to the exact complementarity residual as the parameter vanishes; an L-infinity to L2 norm choice makes the operator statement well defined.
knowledge_statements.title: Mixed-Problem Smoothing Families

children.title: Mixed-Operator Regularity
children.top_down_role: Regularity structures governing Newton models for mixed systems.

assumptions_latex: \(F:X\to Y\) is locally Lipschitz between Banach spaces and is semismooth at a zero \(\bar x\).
\(\mathcal G(x)\subset\mathcal L(X,Y)\) is a nonempty generalized derivative model near \(\bar x\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Uniform bounded invertibility of every \(G\in\mathcal G(x)\) is the mixed-operator regularity condition supporting locally well-defined semismooth Newton steps.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Uniform generalized-Jacobian regularity for a mixed semismooth Newton residual.

source_refs.source_title: Finite-Dimensional Variational Inequalities and Complementarity Problems, Vol. II

knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Mixed-operator regularity at \(\bar x\) means that there exist a neighborhood \(V\) of \(\bar x\) and a constant \(M<\infty\) such that every \(G\in\mathcal G(x)\), with \(x\in V\), is a bounded linear isomorphism from \(X\) onto \(Y\) and
\[
\sup_{x\in V}\sup_{G\in\mathcal G(x)}\|G^{-1}\|_{\mathcal L(Y,X)}\le M.
\]
Under this condition, each Newton equation \(G_kd_k=-F(x_k)\) is uniquely solvable near \(\bar x\). Combined with semismoothness, the uniform inverse bound yields local superlinear convergence for sufficiently close initial iterates.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Mixed-operator regularity requires every nearby generalized derivative to be invertible with uniformly bounded inverse, ensuring solvable Newton steps and supporting local superlinear convergence.
knowledge_statements.title: Mixed-Operator Regularity

source_witnesses.source_title: Finite-Dimensional Variational Inequalities and Complementarity Problems, Vol. II

The record also does not specify the approximation property linking the set-valued model G to semismoothness, yet concludes local superlinear convergence for Newton selections from that model. A Banach-space semismooth Newton source with the exact derivative convention and convergence hypotheses is required.

children.title: Smoothing-Induced Conditioning
children.top_down_role: Conditioning effects associated with smoothed mixed formulations.

assumptions_latex: \(F_\mu:\mathbb R^n\to\mathbb R^n\) is differentiable, \(F_\mu(x_\mu)=0\), and \(A_\mu=F_\mu'(x_\mu)\) is nonsingular.
The Euclidean operator norm and its associated singular values are used.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: If \(\sigma_{\min}(A_\mu)\to0\) while \(\sigma_{\max}(A_\mu)\) stays bounded below, then \(\kappa_2(A_\mu)\to\infty\) as \(\mu\downarrow0\).

notation.meaning: Jacobian of the smoothed residual at its solution

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Conditioning of finite-dimensional Jacobians generated by a vanishing smoothing parameter.

source_refs.locator: Chapter 11. Interior and Smoothing Methods p. 989
source_refs.source_title: Finite-Dimensional Variational Inequalities and Complementarity Problems, Vol. II

knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
At a solution \(x_\mu\) of the smoothed system, the local linear conditioning of a Newton step is
\[
\kappa_2(A_\mu)=\|A_\mu\|_2\|A_\mu^{-1}\|_2
=\frac{\sigma_{\max}(A_\mu)}{\sigma_{\min}(A_\mu)}.
\]
Hence, if \(\sigma_{\max}(A_\mu)\ge c>0\) and \(\sigma_{\min}(A_\mu)\to0\) as \(\mu\downarrow0\), then \(\kappa_2(A_\mu)\to\infty\). Thus smoothing may produce differentiable residuals while simultaneously degrading the conditioning of their Newton systems near a degenerate complementarity limit. Uniform mixed-operator regularity prevents this mechanism by imposing a parameter-independent inverse bound.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: As smoothing vanishes, a collapsing smallest singular value makes Newton systems increasingly ill-conditioned even though each smoothed residual remains differentiable.
knowledge_statements.title: Smoothing-Induced Conditioning

knowledge_statements.title: Mixed-Regularity Failure Regimes
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Failure criterion for smoothed mixed systems whose blocks have incompatible function-space regularity.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(F_\varepsilon:X_1\times X_2\to Y_1\times Y_2\) have solution \(z_\varepsilon^*\), and let \(M_\varepsilon(z)\) be a selected generalized derivative. Mesh-independent semismooth Newton analysis fails whenever, as \(\varepsilon\downarrow0\), at least one of the following occurs: \[\sup_{0<\lVert d\rVert_X\le t}\frac{\lVert F_\varepsilon(z_\varepsilon^*+d)-F_\varepsilon(z_\varepsilon^*)-M_\varepsilon(z_\varepsilon^*+d)d\rVert_Y}{\lVert d\rVert_X}\not\to0\] uniformly in \(\varepsilon\); \(M_\varepsilon(z)^{-1}\) is unbounded uniformly near \(z_\varepsilon^*\); or a block action required by \(M_\varepsilon\) is not bounded from \(X_j\) to its asserted residual space. These failures preclude uniform local Newton estimates in the chosen norms.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Uniform Newton analysis fails if mixed-block remainders do not vanish uniformly, inverse derivatives become unbounded, or a derivative block is not bounded between the selected spaces.
assumptions_latex: \(X_1,X_2,Y_1,Y_2\) are Banach spaces with product norms.
\(F_\varepsilon(z_\varepsilon^*)=0\) for every regularization parameter \(\varepsilon>0\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: No mesh- and regularization-independent local semismooth Newton estimate follows in the stated norms.

Solution of the regularized mixed system.

children.title: Uniform Semismoothness
children.top_down_role: Semismoothness controlled uniformly across discrete problem families.

knowledge_statements.title: Uniform Semismoothness
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Uniform semismoothness of a family of discretized residual mappings at corresponding solutions.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For an index set \(H\), let \(F_h:X_h\to Y_h\), let \(x_h^*\) satisfy \(F_h(x_h^*)=0\), and let \(\mathcal D_h(x)\) be a nonempty set of admissible generalized derivatives. The family is uniformly semismooth at \((x_h^*)_{h\in H}\) if there exist \(r>0\) and a modulus \(\omega:[0,r]\to[0,\infty)\), independent of \(h\), with \(\omega(t)\to0\) as \(t\downarrow0\), such that for every \(h\in H\), \(0<\lVert d\rVert_{X_h}\le r\), and \(M\in\mathcal D_h(x_h^*+d)\), \[\lVert F_h(x_h^*+d)-F_h(x_h^*)-Md\rVert_{Y_h}\le \omega(\lVert d\rVert_{X_h})\lVert d\rVert_{X_h}.\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A discrete family is uniformly semismooth when one mesh-independent modulus bounds every admissible linearization remainder near the corresponding solutions.
assumptions_latex: \(X_h\) and \(Y_h\) are normed spaces for every \(h\in H\).
\(F_h(x_h^*)=0\) and \(\mathcal D_h(x)\ne\varnothing\) locally.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The semismoothness remainder is \(o(\lVert d\rVert_{X_h})\) uniformly over \(h\in H\).

notation.meaning: Admissible generalized derivatives of the discrete residual.

knowledge_statements.title: Uniform-Growth Regime
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Power-type semismoothness remainder with mesh-independent exponent, constant, and neighborhood.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: The family \((F_h,\mathcal D_h,x_h^*)_{h\in H}\) is in the uniform-growth regime of order \(1+\alpha\) if there exist \(\alpha\in(0,1]\), \(C>0\), and \(r>0\), all independent of \(h\), such that for every \(h\in H\), every \(d\) with \(\lVert d\rVert_{X_h}\le r\), and every \(M\in\mathcal D_h(x_h^*+d)\), \[\lVert F_h(x_h^*+d)-F_h(x_h^*)-Md\rVert_{Y_h}\le C\lVert d\rVert_{X_h}^{1+\alpha}.\] Thus uniform semismoothness holds with the common modulus \(\omega(t)=Ct^\alpha\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A common power, constant, and radius bound all discrete linearization remainders, yielding uniform semismoothness.
assumptions_latex: \(F_h:X_h\to Y_h\) and \(F_h(x_h^*)=0\) for every \(h\in H\).
\(\mathcal D_h(x)\) is nonempty in the stated neighborhoods.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The family is uniformly semismooth with modulus \(\omega(t)=Ct^\alpha\).

notation.meaning: Mesh-independent remainder constant and neighborhood radius.

knowledge_statements.title: Nonuniform-Growth Regime
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Mesh-uniform semismoothness obtained despite mesh-dependent power-growth parameters.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Suppose that for each \(h\in H\) there are \(C_h>0\), \(r_h>0\), and \(\alpha_h\in(0,1]\) giving a local bound \(\lVert R_h(d,M)\rVert_{Y_h}\le C_h\lVert d\rVert_{X_h}^{1+\alpha_h}\), where \(R_h(d,M)=F_h(x_h^*+d)-F_h(x_h^*)-Md\). The family is in the nonuniform-growth, mesh-uniform regime when no common positive lower bound on \(\alpha_h\), nor common upper bound on \(C_h\), is assumed, but there still exist \(r>0\) and \(\omega(t)\downarrow0\), independent of \(h\), such that \[\sup_{\substack{0<\lVert d\rVert_{X_h}\le t\\M\in\mathcal D_h(x_h^*+d)}}\frac{\lVert R_h(d,M)\rVert_{Y_h}}{\lVert d\rVert_{X_h}}\le\omega(t),\qquad 0<t\le r.\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Meshwise power estimates may deteriorate, yet a separate common little-o modulus can still establish uniform semismoothness.
assumptions_latex: \(F_h(x_h^*)=0\) and the meshwise remainder bounds hold.
The displayed suprema are finite for \(0<t\le r\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Uniform semismoothness holds although the meshwise power-growth parameters are not uniform.
review_flags: The intended distinction from the growth-free regime is taxonomy-specific.

children.title: Growth-Free Regime
children.top_down_role: Mesh-independent semismoothness without growth conditions.

knowledge_statements.title: Growth-Free Regime
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Sequential mesh-uniform semismoothness stated without any power or prescribed growth model.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(R_h(d,M)=F_h(x_h^*+d)-F_h(x_h^*)-Md\). The family is in the growth-free regime if, for every sequence \(h_k\in H\), every \(d_k\in X_{h_k}\) with \(0<\lVert d_k\rVert_{X_{h_k}}\to0\), and every \(M_k\in\mathcal D_{h_k}(x_{h_k}^*+d_k)\), \[\frac{\lVert R_{h_k}(d_k,M_k)\rVert_{Y_{h_k}}}{\lVert d_k\rVert_{X_{h_k}}}\longrightarrow0.\] No estimate of the form \(C\lVert d\rVert^{1+\alpha}\), and no preassigned remainder-growth modulus, is included in the hypothesis. The sequential condition is the direct mesh-uniform semismoothness requirement.

knowledge_statements.title: Uniform-Growth Convergence Regime
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Uniform local Newton convergence derived from uniform power-growth and inverse bounds.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Assume the uniform-growth remainder estimate of order \(1+\alpha\) holds with constants \(C,r\), and every \(M\in\mathcal D_h(x)\) for \(\lVert x-x_h^*\rVert_{X_h}\le r\) is invertible with \(\lVert M^{-1}\rVert\le\kappa\), uniformly in \(h\). knowledge_statements.title: Growth-Free Convergence Regime

knowledge_statements.title: Mesh-Dependent Convergence
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Failure to admit a common local convergence radius and uniformly vanishing Newton error quotient under refinement.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(H\) be a family of mesh indices, let \(T_h:X_h\to X_h\) be a semismooth Newton update, and let \(x_h^*\in X_h\) satisfy \(T_h(x_h^*)=x_h^*\). Local convergence is mesh-independent if there exist \(r>0\) and \(q:(0,r]\to[0,\infty)\), both independent of \(h\), with \(q(t)\to0\) as \(t\downarrow0\), such that for every \(h\in H\) and every \(x\in X_h\) with \(0<\lVert x-x_h^*\rVert_{X_h}\le r\), \[\lVert T_h(x)-x_h^*\rVert_{X_h}\le q(\lVert x-x_h^*\rVert_{X_h})\lVert x-x_h^*\rVert_{X_h}.\] Local convergence is mesh-dependent when no such common pair \((r,q)\) exists.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Convergence is mesh-dependent when no positive mesh-independent neighborhood admits a common Newton error-quotient bound that vanishes as the error tends to zero.
assumptions_latex: \(X_h\) is a normed space for each \(h\in H\).
\(T_h(x_h^*)=x_h^*\) for every \(h\in H\).

knowledge_statements.title: Continuous-Discrete Activity Mismatch
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Failure of discrete active regions to converge to the function-space active region.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(s=\psi-y\) be the continuous slack and \(s_h=\psi_h-y_h\) its discrete counterpart on a common measure space \(\Omega\). Define \(A=\{\xi\in\Omega:s(\xi)=0\}\) and \(A_h=\{\xi\in\Omega:s_h(\xi)\le\tau_h\}\), where \(\tau_h\downarrow0\) is the discrete activity tolerance. A continuous-discrete activity mismatch persists if \[\limsup_{h\to0}\mu(A_h\mathbin{\triangle}A)>0.\] Such a mismatch prevents active-set indicators from converging in \(L^1(\Omega)\), because \(\lVert\mathbf1_{A_h}-\mathbf1_A\rVert_{L^1}=\mu(A_h\mathbin{\triangle}A)\), and can invalidate transfer of continuous generalized-derivative structure to discrete Newton systems.

knowledge_statements.title: State-Constraint Regularization Paths
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Solution paths generated by smoothing the complementarity relation for a state inequality.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(E(y,u)=0\) be a state equation, let \(G(y,u,\lambda)=0\) collect stationarity equations, and impose the state constraint \(y\le\psi\) with multiplier \(\lambda\ge0\). Define \(\phi_\varepsilon(a,b)=\sqrt{a^2+b^2+2\varepsilon^2}-a-b\) for \(\varepsilon>0\), applied pointwise. The state-constraint regularization path is the parameterized solution set \[\mathcal P=\{(\varepsilon,y_\varepsilon,u_\varepsilon,\lambda_\varepsilon):\varepsilon>0,\ E(y_\varepsilon,u_\varepsilon)=0,\ G(y_\varepsilon,u_\varepsilon,\lambda_\varepsilon)=0,\ \phi_\varepsilon(\psi-y_\varepsilon,\lambda_\varepsilon)=0\}.\] A branch is a single-valued selection \(\varepsilon\mapsto(y_\varepsilon,u_\varepsilon,\lambda_\varepsilon)\); any limit as \(\varepsilon\downarrow0\) is expected to satisfy complementarity only when convergence and closedness are separately established.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A regularization path consists of state, control, and multiplier solutions obtained by replacing state-constraint complementarity with a parameterized smooth equation.

\(E\) and \(G\) have compatible state, control, multiplier, and residual spaces.

children.title: Regularization-Path Stability

knowledge_statements.title: Regularization-Path Stability
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Strong stability of quadratic state-constraint penalty paths in Hilbert spaces.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(U,Y\) be Hilbert spaces, let \(S:U\to Y\) be bounded and linear, and let \(J:U\to\mathbb R\cup\{+\infty\}\) be proper, lower semicontinuous, coercive, and strongly convex. Assume \(C=\{u\in U:S u\leq\psi\}\neq\varnothing\), with the inequality understood almost everywhere. For \(\gamma>0\), define
\[
u_\gamma=\operatorname*{argmin}_{u\in U}\left[J(u)+\frac{1}{2\gamma}\|(S u-\psi)_+\|_Y^2\right].
\]
If \(u_*\) minimizes \(J\) over \(C\), then \(u_\gamma\to u_*\) strongly in \(U\) as \(\gamma\downarrow0\), and \(\|(S u_\gamma-\psi)_+\|_Y=O(\sqrt\gamma)\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Quadratic-penalty minimizers converge strongly to the unique state-constrained minimizer, while their state-constraint violation is at most order square root of the penalty parameter.
assumptions_latex: \(S:U\to Y\) is bounded and linear.
\(J\) is proper, lower semicontinuous, coercive, and strongly convex.
\(\{u:S u\leq\psi\}\neq\varnothing\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(u_\gamma\to u_*\) strongly and \(\|(S u_\gamma-\psi)_+\|_Y=O(\sqrt\gamma)\).

children.title: Dual Regularization Interpretation
children.top_down_role: Dual-space interpretation of state-constraint regularization.

knowledge_statements.title: Dual Regularization Interpretation
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Fenchel dual form of the quadratic positive-part state penalty.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(Y=L^2(\Omega)\), let \(g\in Y\), and let \(Y_+=\{\mu\in Y:\mu\geq0\text{ a.e.}\}\). For every \(\gamma>0\),
\[
\frac{1}{2\gamma}\|g_+\|_Y^2
=
\sup_{\mu\in Y_+}\left\{\langle\mu,g\rangle_Y-\frac{\gamma}{2}\|\mu\|_Y^2\right\}.
\]
The supremum is attained uniquely at \(\mu_\gamma=\gamma^{-1}g_+\). Consequently, for \(g=S u-\psi\), quadratic state-constraint regularization is equivalent to adding a dual variable constrained by \(\mu\geq0\) and penalizing its squared norm by \(\gamma/2\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The quadratic positive-part penalty is the maximized dual pairing with a nonnegative multiplier minus a quadratic dual regularizer.
assumptions_latex: \(g\in Y\) and \(\gamma>0\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\frac{1}{2\gamma}\|g_+\|_Y^2=\sup_{\mu\in Y_+}\{\langle\mu,g\rangle_Y-\frac{\gamma}{2}\|\mu\|_Y^2\}\), with \(\mu_\gamma=\gamma^{-1}g_+\).

knowledge_statements.title: Black-Box Elliptic Newton Methods
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Reduced semismooth Newton iteration using elliptic state and adjoint solution operators.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(S:U\to Y\) be the bounded linear solution operator of an elliptic state equation, let \(U_{ad}=\{u:a\leq u\leq b\}\), and let \(\alpha>0\). Define \(p(u)=S^*(S u-y_d)\) and
\[
F(u)=u-P_{[a,b]}(-\alpha^{-1}p(u)).
\]
Given \(u^0\), iteration \(k\) evaluates the state \(S u^k\), the adjoint \(p(u^k)\), and a pointwise generalized derivative \(\chi_k\in\partial P_{[a,b]}(-\alpha^{-1}p(u^k))\). It solves
\[
\left(I+\alpha^{-1}\chi_k S^*S\right)\delta u^k=-F(u^k),\qquad u^{k+1}=u^k+\delta u^k,
\]
and stops when \(F(u^k)=0\) within tolerance.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Each reduced Newton step calls black-box state and adjoint solvers, identifies projection activity, and solves the resulting generalized control-space Newton equation.
assumptions_latex: \(S:U\to Y\) is a bounded linear elliptic solution operator.
\(a<b\) almost everywhere and \(\alpha>0\).
The selected generalized Newton operator is invertible near the solution.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The output satisfies the reduced projection equation \(u=P_{[a,b]}(-\alpha^{-1}S^*(S u-y_d))\) to the prescribed tolerance.

notation.meaning: pointwise projection onto the admissible interval

knowledge_statements.title: All-at-Once Elliptic Newton Methods
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Coupled primal-dual active-set Newton system for box-constrained elliptic control.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(A y-Bu=f\) be a linear elliptic state equation and consider a quadratic tracking objective with control cost \(\alpha\|u\|^2/2\) and bounds \(a\leq u\leq b\). Retain \(x=(y,p,u,\lambda_a,\lambda_b)\) and impose
\[
Ay-Bu-f=0,\quad A^*p+y-y_d=0,\quad \alpha u+B^*p-\lambda_a+\lambda_b=0,
\]
with \(0\leq u-a\perp\lambda_a\geq0\) and \(0\leq b-u\perp\lambda_b\geq0\). From \(x^k\), choose generalized derivatives of complementarity functions, solve the coupled generalized Jacobian equation \(G_k\delta x^k=-F(x^k)\), update \(x^{k+1}=x^k+\delta x^k\), and stop when the KKT residual meets tolerance.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The all-at-once method Newton-linearizes the state, adjoint, stationarity, and bound-complementarity equations while retaining every primal and dual variable.
assumptions_latex: \(A\) is an invertible elliptic operator.
\(\alpha>0\) and \(a<b\) almost everywhere.
A nonsingular generalized KKT Jacobian is selected near the solution.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The returned variables satisfy the coupled state, adjoint, stationarity, and bound-complementarity system to tolerance.

knowledge_statements.title: Discrete Elliptic Newton Architectures
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Algebraic equivalence of reduced and all-at-once finite-element Newton systems.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let conforming finite-element discretization yield
\[
K y-Bu=f,\qquad K^{\mathsf T}p+M(y-y_d)=0,
\]
where \(K\) is nonsingular, and let \(M_u\) be the control mass matrix. Eliminating \(y\) and \(p\) from an all-at-once Newton linearization produces the reduced control Hessian
\[
H_h=\alpha M_u+B^{\mathsf T}K^{-\mathsf T}M K^{-1}B.
\]
For a diagonal free-set mask \(D\), the reduced active-set equation has coefficient \(D H_hD+(I-D)\). Conversely, introducing state and adjoint increments recovers a sparse saddle-point system whose Schur complement in the free control variables is precisely the restriction of \(H_h\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Finite-element reduced and all-at-once Newton systems are algebraically equivalent: eliminating state and adjoint variables yields the reduced active-set Hessian.
assumptions_latex: \(K\) is the nonsingular discrete elliptic operator.
\(M\) and \(M_u\) are symmetric positive definite mass matrices.
\(D\) is the diagonal indicator of free control degrees of freedom.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The free-control Schur complement of the all-at-once system equals the corresponding restriction of \(H_h\).

children.title: Elliptic Newton-System Solution
