knowledge_statements.title: Elliptic Newton-System Solution
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Structure-exploiting direct and preconditioned iterative solution of active-set Newton equations.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
At iteration \(k\), let the elliptic active-set linearization be \(J_k\delta x=-r_k\), with state, adjoint, free-control, and active-control blocks. First eliminate active-control increments using their identity equations. The remaining system may be solved either by block factorization using elliptic solves with \(K\) and \(K^{\mathsf T}\), or by a Krylov method with block preconditioner \(P_k\). If the preconditioned Schur complement satisfies
\[
c\langle P_kv,v\rangle\leq\langle J_kv,v\rangle\leq C\langle P_kv,v\rangle
\]
for constants \(0<c\leq C\) independent of mesh size and the current active set, then the symmetric preconditioned iteration count for a fixed residual reduction is uniformly bounded.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Eliminate active variables and exploit elliptic block solves; uniform spectral equivalence of the preconditioner gives mesh- and active-set-independent iteration counts.
assumptions_latex: The inactive Newton system is symmetric positive definite, or is reduced to such a Schur complement.
\(P_k\) is symmetric positive definite.
The spectral-equivalence constants are independent of mesh and active set.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: A fixed relative residual reduction requires a number of preconditioned symmetric Krylov iterations bounded independently of the mesh and active set.

knowledge_statements.title: Obstacle Dual Newton Formulations
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Multiplier-space complementarity equation for a lower-obstacle variational inequality.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(V\) be a Hilbert space, let \(A:V\to V^*\) be bounded, coercive, and invertible, and let \(K=\{y\in V:y\geq\psi\}\). The obstacle variational inequality
\[
\langle Ay-f,v-y\rangle\geq0\qquad\text{for every }v\in K
\]
is equivalent, whenever the pointwise order and multiplier pairing are defined, to
\[
y=A^{-1}(f+\lambda),\qquad y-\psi\geq0,
\quad\lambda\geq0,
\quad\langle\lambda,y-\psi\rangle=0.
\]
Eliminating \(y\) gives the dual nonsmooth equation
\[
\min\{A^{-1}(f+\lambda)-\psi,\lambda\}=0,
\]
where the minimum is pointwise; its generalized Newton derivative selects contact and noncontact regions.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Eliminating the obstacle state produces a multiplier-space minimum equation whose generalized derivative identifies contact and noncontact regions.
assumptions_latex: \(A:V\to V^*\) is bounded, coercive, and invertible.
The obstacle cone and dual multiplier cone admit the displayed pointwise complementarity representation.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The obstacle variational inequality is equivalent to \(\min\{A^{-1}(f+\lambda)-\psi,\lambda\}=0\).

knowledge_statements.title: Obstacle Regularized-Dual Newton Methods
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Semismooth Newton iteration for a quadratically regularized obstacle multiplier equation.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(A:V\to V^*\) be an invertible elliptic operator and let \(\gamma>0\). Define the regularized dual residual
\[
F_\gamma(\lambda)=\lambda-\gamma^{-1}\bigl(\psi-A^{-1}(f+\lambda)\bigr)_+.
\]
Starting from \(\lambda^0\), set \(y^k=A^{-1}(f+\lambda^k)\), choose \(\chi_k(x)\in\partial(\cdot)_+(\psi(x)-y^k(x))\), and solve
\[
\left(I+\gamma^{-1}\chi_kA^{-1}\right)\delta\lambda^k=-F_\gamma(\lambda^k),
\qquad \lambda^{k+1}=\lambda^k+\delta\lambda^k.
\]
Stop when \(\|F_\gamma(\lambda^k)\|\) is below tolerance. The associated state is \(y^k=A^{-1}(f+\lambda^k)\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Newton steps solve a multiplier-space equation formed by the positive-part regularization of obstacle complementarity and repeated elliptic solution.
assumptions_latex: \(A\) is invertible and elliptic.
The selected generalized Newton operator is invertible near the regularized solution.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The output satisfies \(\lambda=\gamma^{-1}(\psi-A^{-1}(f+\lambda))_+\) to tolerance.

children.title: Discrete Obstacle Active Sets

knowledge_statements.title: Discrete Obstacle Active Sets
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Primal-dual active-set iteration for a discretized lower-obstacle problem.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(A_hy-f_h-\lambda=0\) be the discrete equilibrium equation, with \(y-\psi_h\geq0\), \(\lambda\geq0\), and \(\lambda_i(y_i-\psi_{h,i})=0\). Given \((y^k,\lambda^k)\) and \(c>0\), define
\[
\mathcal A_k=\{i:\lambda_i^k-c(y_i^k-\psi_{h,i})>0\},
\qquad \mathcal I_k=\{1,\ldots,n\}\setminus\mathcal A_k.
\]
Compute \((y^{k+1},\lambda^{k+1})\) from
\[
A_hy^{k+1}-f_h-\lambda^{k+1}=0,
\quad y_i^{k+1}=\psi_{h,i}\ (i\in\mathcal A_k),
\quad\lambda_i^{k+1}=0\ (i\in\mathcal I_k).
\]
Stop when the active set is unchanged and the residual tolerance is met.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The discrete method predicts contact nodes, fixes the obstacle there, sets multipliers to zero elsewhere, and solves the resulting linear system.
assumptions_latex: \(A_h\) is the discrete coercive obstacle operator.
The active-set linear systems are nonsingular.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: At termination, the iterate satisfies discrete equilibrium and obstacle complementarity to tolerance.

children.title: L1 Optimality Equations

knowledge_statements.title: L1 Optimality Equations
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Soft-thresholding equation for quadratic PDE control with an L1 control penalty.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(U=L^2(\Omega)\), let \(S:U\to Y\) be bounded and linear, and consider
\[
\min_{u\in U}\frac12\|S u-y_d\|_Y^2+\frac\alpha2\|u\|_U^2+\beta\|u\|_{L^1(\Omega)},
\qquad \alpha>0,\quad\beta>0.
\]
With \(p=S^*(S u-y_d)\), first-order optimality is
\[
0\in p+\alpha u+\beta\,\partial\|u\|_{L^1(\Omega)}.
\]
Equivalently, almost everywhere,
\[
u=\operatorname{soft}(-\alpha^{-1}p,\beta/\alpha),
\qquad
\operatorname{soft}(z,t)=\operatorname{sign}(z)\max\{|z|-t,0\}.
\]
Thus the optimality system is the semismooth equation \(F(u)=u-\operatorname{soft}(-\alpha^{-1}S^*(S u-y_d),\beta/\alpha)=0\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The L1-regularized PDE control condition is equivalent to a pointwise soft-thresholding fixed-point equation suitable for semismooth Newton iteration.
assumptions_latex: \(S:U\to Y\) is bounded and linear.
\(\alpha>0\) and \(\beta>0\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Optimality is equivalent to \(u=\operatorname{soft}(-\alpha^{-1}S^*(S u-y_d),\beta/\alpha)\).
review_flags: standard_field_rationale: subdifferential optimality for the L1 norm is equivalent to its proximal soft-thresholding equation
auto_normalized: candidate_review without source_refs downgraded to needs_source

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The subdifferential and soft-thresholding equations are standard and the representation kind fits, but no source is supplied. A finite-measure or comparable assumption on Ω is also needed for the stated L1 functional on all of L2(Ω).

children.title: L1 Thresholding Active Sets
children.top_down_role: Active-set interpretations generated by L1 thresholding structure.

knowledge_statements.title: L1 Thresholding Active Sets
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Pointwise active-set partition induced by the L1 soft-thresholding equation.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
For the optimality equation \(0\in p+\alpha u+\beta\partial|u|\), with \(\alpha,\beta>0\), define
\[
\mathcal A_+=\{x:p(x)<-\beta\},\qquad
\mathcal A_-=\{x:p(x)>\beta\},\qquad
\mathcal I=\{x:|p(x)|\leq\beta\}.
\]
Then, almost everywhere,
\[
u(x)=
\begin{cases}
-(p(x)+\beta)/\alpha,&x\in\mathcal A_+,\\
0,&x\in\mathcal I,\\
-(p(x)-\beta)/\alpha,&x\in\mathcal A_-.
\end{cases}
\]
Away from the threshold sets \(p=\pm\beta\), a generalized derivative of the soft-thresholding map equals one on \(\mathcal A_+\cup\mathcal A_-\) and zero on \(\mathcal I\), furnishing the Newton active-set mask.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Adjoint values beyond either L1 threshold determine signed nonzero controls; values inside the threshold interval identify the zero-control set.
assumptions_latex: \(0\in p+\alpha u+\beta\partial|u|\) holds almost everywhere.
\(\alpha>0\) and \(\beta>0\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The displayed partition determines \(u\) pointwise and supplies the generalized-derivative active-set mask.

knowledge_statements.title: Pointwise Bound-Constrained Flow Control
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Projection equation for pointwise box-constrained incompressible-flow control.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(U=L^2(\Omega)^d\), let \(a,b\in L^\infty(\Omega)^d\) satisfy \(a<b\) componentwise, and let \(y(u)\) be a locally differentiable incompressible-flow state. For
\[
j(u)=J(y(u))+\frac\alpha2\|u\|_U^2,
\qquad U_{ad}=\{u\in U:a\leq u\leq b\},
\]
let \(z(u)\) solve the adjoint flow equation and write the reduced gradient as \(g(u)=\alpha u+B^*z(u)\). For any \(c>0\), the variational inequality \(\langle g(u),v-u\rangle_U\geq0\) for every \(v\in U_{ad}\) is equivalent to
\[
F(u)=u-P_{[a,b]}(u-cg(u))=0.
\]
Pointwise generalized derivatives of the projection define the semismooth Newton active and free regions.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Bound-constrained flow optimality is a componentwise projection equation coupling the control with an adjoint-flow gradient and inducing Newton active sets.
assumptions_latex: The control-to-state map is locally differentiable at the considered feasible control.
The adjoint equation represents the derivative of the flow objective.
\(\alpha>0\), \(c>0\), and \(a<b\) componentwise.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: First-order bound-constrained optimality is equivalent to \(u=P_{[a,b]}(u-c(\alpha u+B^*z(u)))\).

notation.meaning: adjoint of the control action operator

children.title: Pointwise Ball-Constrained Flow Control

knowledge_statements.title: Pointwise Ball-Constrained Flow Control
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Pointwise Euclidean-ball feasibility and projection residual for distributed incompressible-flow controls.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(U=L^2(\Omega;\mathbb R^d)\), let \(r\in L^\infty(\Omega)\) satisfy \(r(x)>0\) almost everywhere, and define \(U_{\mathrm{ad}}=\{u\in U:\|u(x)\|_2\le r(x)\text{ a.e.}\}\). For a reduced gradient \(g(u)\in U\) and \(\gamma>0\), first-order stationarity is equivalently expressed by the projection residual
\[F(u)=u-\Pi_{U_{\mathrm{ad}}}(u-\gamma g(u))=0,\]
where
\[(\Pi_{U_{\mathrm{ad}}}v)(x)=\min\!\left\{1,\frac{r(x)}{\|v(x)\|_2}\right\}v(x)\]
with the multiplier interpreted as \(1\) when \(v(x)=0\). A semismooth Newton step applies a selected generalized derivative of \(F\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Ball feasibility is enforced pointwise, and stationarity becomes a zero of the control projection residual used by semismooth Newton.
assumptions_latex: \(\Omega\subset\mathbb R^d\) is measurable.
\(g:U\to U\) is defined and Newton differentiable near the iterate.
\(r\in L^\infty(\Omega)\) is positive almost everywhere.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(u\) is stationary exactly when \(F(u)=0\).

notation.meaning: Metric projection onto the admissible control set.

knowledge_statements.title: Adjoint-Based Flow Derivatives
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Reduced first derivative obtained from the compressible-flow state equation and its adjoint.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let the state \(y=S(u)\) satisfy \(E(y,u)=0\), where \(E:Y\times U\to Z\) and \(J:Y\times U\to\mathbb R\) are Fréchet differentiable. If \(E_y(y,u):Y\to Z\) is invertible, define the adjoint \(p\in Z^*\) by
\[E_y(y,u)^*p=-J_y(y,u).\]
Then the reduced functional \(j(u)=J(S(u),u)\) has derivative
\[j'(u)h=J_u(y,u)h+\langle p,E_u(y,u)h\rangle_{Z^*,Z}\]
for every \(h\in U\). Thus gradient evaluations require one state solve and one adjoint solve, independently of the number of control directions.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Solve the flow state and one adjoint equation; their residual derivatives give the reduced derivative in every control direction.
assumptions_latex: \(E\) and \(J\) are Fréchet differentiable near \((y,u)\).
\(E_y(y,u)\) is continuously invertible.
The displayed duality pairing is well defined.

knowledge_statements.title: Semismooth BFGS-Newton Family
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Hybrid generalized Newton iteration with a BFGS approximation of an unavailable smooth derivative block.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Given \(z_0\), a symmetric positive-definite matrix \(B_0\), and a residual \(F(z)=0\), choose at iteration \(k\) a generalized-Jacobian model \(G_k=A_k+B_k\), where \(A_k\) is assembled from semismooth terms. Compute \(d_k\) from
\[(A_k+B_k)d_k=-F(z_k),\qquad z_{k+1}=z_k+\alpha_kd_k,\]
with \(\alpha_k\in(0,1]\) chosen by globalization. Set \(s_k=z_{k+1}-z_k\), \(q_k=F_s(z_{k+1})-F_s(z_k)\), and, when \(s_k^\top q_k>0\), update
\[B_{k+1}=B_k-\frac{B_ks_ks_k^\top B_k}{s_k^\top B_ks_k}+\frac{q_kq_k^\top}{s_k^\top q_k}.\]
Stop when the prescribed residual tolerance is met.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Each step combines an exact semismooth derivative block with a positive-definite BFGS approximation and a globalized residual solve.
assumptions_latex: \(F=F_n+F_s\), with \(F_n\) semismooth and \(F_s\) differentiable.
\(B_0\) is symmetric positive definite.
Accepted BFGS pairs satisfy \(s_k^\top q_k>0\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The iteration returns \(z_k\) when \(\|F(z_k)\|\) meets the chosen tolerance.

knowledge_statements.title: Saddle-Point Newton Systems
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Block KKT form of equality-constrained or PDE-constrained Newton equations.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(H_k\in\mathbb R^{n\times n}\) be a symmetric primal Newton block and \(A_k\in\mathbb R^{m\times n}\) the linearized constraint operator. The Newton increments satisfy the saddle-point system
\[\begin{pmatrix}H_k&A_k^\top\\A_k&0\end{pmatrix}\begin{pmatrix}d_x\\d_\lambda\end{pmatrix}=-\begin{pmatrix}r_{d,k}\\r_{p,k}\end{pmatrix}.\]
If \(A_k\) has full row rank and \(H_k\) is positive definite on \(\ker A_k\), the block matrix is nonsingular. Hence the primal and multiplier increments are uniquely determined despite the matrix being indefinite whenever \(m>0\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: KKT linearization yields an indefinite two-by-two block system that is nonsingular under constraint qualification and reduced positive definiteness.

\(d^\top H_kd>0\) for every nonzero \(d\in\ker A_k\).
\(H_k=H_k^\top\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The saddle-point matrix is nonsingular and the Newton increment is unique.

\[F(x,\lambda)=\bigl(r_d(x,\lambda),\Phi(a(x),\lambda)\bigr),\]
where \(a:\mathbb R^n\to\mathbb R^m\) has Jacobian \(A\) and \(\Phi\) acts componentwise. Suppose a generalized Jacobian selection has the block form

children.title: Matrix-Free Newton Operators
children.top_down_role: Operator-action realizations avoiding explicit generalized Jacobian assembly.

knowledge_statements.title: Matrix-Free Newton Operators
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Generalized Newton solve using derivative actions without storing the system matrix.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Given \(z_k\), residual \(F(z_k)\), and an oracle \(\mathcal V_k(v)=V_kv\) for a fixed selection \(V_k\in\partial F(z_k)\), apply a Krylov solver to
\[\mathcal V_k(d_k)=-F(z_k)\]
using only evaluations of \(\mathcal V_k\) and, when present, a preconditioner action. Terminate the inner solve when
\[\|\mathcal V_k(d_k)+F(z_k)\|\le\eta_k\|F(z_k)\|,\qquad 0\le\eta_k<1,\]
and update \(z_{k+1}=z_k+\alpha_kd_k\). No entries of \(V_k\) need be assembled or stored.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A Krylov method accesses a fixed generalized Jacobian only through vector products and stops at a prescribed relative linear residual.
assumptions_latex: The oracle uses one fixed derivative selection throughout the inner solve.
\(V_k\) is nonsingular on the solved space.
\(0\le\eta_k<1\) is the forcing tolerance.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The returned \(d_k\) satisfies the stated inexact generalized Newton condition.
review_flags: No supplied locator directly supports matrix-free inexact generalized Newton realization.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The algorithm is mathematically coherent and fits the matrix-free operator leaf, but no source supports the fixed derivative selection, Krylov realization, or stated inexact Newton stopping condition.

children.title: Adjoint-Based Reduced Derivatives
children.top_down_role: Adjoint realizations of reduced gradients and curvature operators.

knowledge_statements.title: Adjoint-Based Reduced Derivatives
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Reduced gradient and Hessian-vector action without explicitly forming the control-to-state derivative.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(E(y,u)=0\), \(j(u)=J(y(u),u)\), and let \(p\) solve \(E_y(y,u)^*p=-J_y(y,u)\). Then
\[j'(u)=J_u(y,u)+E_u(y,u)^*p.\]
For a direction \(h\), compute the incremental state \(w\) from \(E_yw=-E_uh\), differentiate the adjoint equation to obtain an incremental adjoint \(q\), and evaluate
\[j''(u)h=D_{(y,u)}\!\left(J_u+E_u^*p\right)[w,h]+E_u^*q.\]
Thus both reduced gradients and curvature actions are realized through state, adjoint, and incremental solves rather than an explicitly assembled reduced Hessian.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: State and adjoint solves provide the reduced gradient; incremental state and adjoint solves provide Hessian-vector products.
assumptions_latex: \(E\) and \(J\) are twice Fréchet differentiable.
\(E_y(y,u)\) and \(E_y(y,u)^*\) are continuously invertible.
All displayed derivatives and duality actions are well defined.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The displayed formulas realize \(j'(u)\) and \(j''(u)h\) without forming \(S'(u)\) or the reduced Hessian matrix.

children.title: Linear Solver Families
children.top_down_role: Direct and iterative solution families for generalized Newton systems.

children.title: Direct Factorization Solves
children.top_down_role: Sparse direct solution of reduced or coupled Newton systems.

knowledge_statements.title: Direct Factorization Solves
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Sparse direct solution of an assembled generalized Newton system.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Given an assembled nonsingular Newton matrix \(V_k\) and right-hand side \(b_k=-F(z_k)\), compute a permutation \(P_k\) and a stable sparse factorization, for example
\[P_kV_kP_k^\top=L_kU_k\]
for a general matrix, or a pivoted symmetric-indefinite factorization when applicable. Solve successively with the triangular factors and undo the permutation to obtain \(d_k\). Accept the linear solve when
\[\|V_kd_k-b_k\|\le\tau_k\|b_k\|.\]
The output is the direct-factorization Newton direction, up to pivoting and floating-point error.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Permute and factor the assembled Newton matrix, use triangular solves, and verify the resulting linear residual.
assumptions_latex: \(V_k\) is assembled and nonsingular.
The factorization uses stable pivoting appropriate to the matrix class.
\(\tau_k\ge0\) is the prescribed linear-solve tolerance.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The computed \(d_k\) satisfies the Newton system to the stated residual tolerance.

children.title: Krylov Newton Solves
children.top_down_role: Iterative solution of large generalized Newton systems.

knowledge_statements.title: Krylov Newton Solves
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Preconditioned iterative solution of large generalized Newton equations.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
At outer iteration \(k\), fix a generalized Newton matrix \(V_k\), choose a nonsingular preconditioner \(M_k\), and apply an appropriate Krylov method to
\[M_k^{-1}V_kd=-M_k^{-1}F(z_k).\]
Use conjugate gradients only when the preconditioned operator is symmetric positive definite; use a nonsymmetric method such as GMRES otherwise. Stop at the first \(d_k\) satisfying
\[\|V_kd_k+F(z_k)\|\le\eta_k\|F(z_k)\|,\qquad 0\le\eta_k<1.\]
Return \(d_k\) as the inexact Newton direction for the outer update.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Apply a matrix-compatible preconditioned Krylov method until the generalized Newton residual meets the forcing tolerance.
assumptions_latex: The selected \(V_k\) remains fixed during the Krylov solve.
\(M_k\) is nonsingular.
The Krylov family matches the symmetry and definiteness of the preconditioned operator.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The returned direction satisfies the prescribed inexact Newton residual bound.

children.title: Multigrid Newton Solves
children.top_down_role: Multilevel solution families for discretized operator Newton systems.

knowledge_statements.title: Multigrid Newton Solves
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Geometric or algebraic multigrid applied to a discretized semismooth Newton correction equation.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Given a Newton matrix hierarchy \(J_0,\ldots,J_L\), transfers \(P_\ell\) and \(R_\ell\), smoothers \(S_\ell\), residual \(r_L=-F(x)\), and initial correction \(d_L^{(0)}=0\), apply multigrid cycles to \(J_Ld_L=r_L\). Each cycle performs presmoothing, restricts the residual by \(r_{\ell-1}=R_\ell(r_\ell-J_\ell d_\ell)\), solves or recursively approximates \(J_{\ell-1}e_{\ell-1}=r_{\ell-1}\), corrects by \(d_\ell\leftarrow d_\ell+P_\ell e_{\ell-1}\), and postsmooths. Stop when \(\lVert r_L-J_Ld_L\rVert\leq\eta\lVert r_L\rVert\), and output \(x^+=x+d_L\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Apply recursive smoothing, residual restriction, coarse correction, and prolongation until the Newton linear residual meets the prescribed relative tolerance.
assumptions_latex: \(J_\ell\in\mathbb R^{n_\ell\times n_\ell}\) is nonsingular for \(0\leq\ell\leq L\).
\(P_\ell\) and \(R_\ell\) have dimensions compatible with adjacent levels.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\lVert F(x)+J_Ld_L\rVert\leq\eta\lVert F(x)\rVert\) and \(x^+=x+d_L\).

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The algorithm role and multigrid cycle fit the leaf, but no source supports this particular multilevel semismooth-Newton realization or its stopping rule.

children.title: Preconditioner Reuse Mechanisms
children.top_down_role: Scalability mechanisms adapted to changing active partitions and coupled PDE structure.

children.title: Active-Set-Aware Preconditioners
children.top_down_role: Preconditioners adapted to changing active and free blocks.

knowledge_statements.title: Active-Set-Aware Preconditioners
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Block preconditioning after partitioning Newton variables into current active and free indices.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(A\) and \(F\) be the current active and free index sets, and let \(\Pi_{A,F}\) permute variables accordingly. For a Newton matrix \(J\), an active-set-aware left preconditioner has the form \[M_{A,F}^{-1}=\Pi_{A,F}^{T}\begin{pmatrix}I_A&0\\0&\widehat J_{FF}^{-1}\end{pmatrix}\Pi_{A,F},\] or a block-triangular analogue retaining selected active-free couplings. Here \(\widehat J_{FF}\) is an inexpensive nonsingular approximation to the free block \(J_{FF}\). When the partition changes, the permutation and affected blocks are updated before applying \(M_{A,F}^{-1}\) to the Newton residual.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Permute active and free variables, enforce the active block directly, and precondition the free Newton block with an inexpensive updated approximation.
assumptions_latex: \(A\cap F=\varnothing\) and \(A\cup F=\{1,\ldots,n\}\).
\(\widehat J_{FF}\) is nonsingular.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(M_{A,F}^{-1}\) respects the current active-free partition and supplies a well-defined preconditioned Newton system.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The representation fits the container, but the identity active block and claim that it enforces the active variables require a source and problem-specific justification.

children.title: Block-Schur Preconditioner Family
children.top_down_role: Block preconditioners for coupled primal-dual and PDE Newton systems.

children.title: Block Preconditioners
children.top_down_role: Preconditioners organized around the block structure of coupled Newton systems.

knowledge_statements.title: Block Preconditioners
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Diagonal and triangular preconditioners for a two-block Newton linearization.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For \(K=\begin{pmatrix}A&B\\C&D\end{pmatrix}\), let \(\widehat A\) and \(\widehat D\) be readily invertible nonsingular approximations of the diagonal blocks. Standard block preconditioners include \[P_D=\begin{pmatrix}\widehat A&0\\0&\widehat D\end{pmatrix},\qquad P_L=\begin{pmatrix}\widehat A&0\\C&\widehat D\end{pmatrix},\qquad P_U=\begin{pmatrix}\widehat A&B\\0&\widehat D\end{pmatrix}.\] Their inverses are applied by independent diagonal solves for \(P_D\), or by forward or backward block substitution for \(P_L\) and \(P_U\), respectively.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A coupled Newton matrix can be preconditioned using approximate diagonal blocks, optionally retaining one coupling block and applying block substitution.
assumptions_latex: \(K\in\mathbb R^{(n+m)\times(n+m)}\) has the displayed conforming block structure.
\(\widehat A\) and \(\widehat D\) are nonsingular.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(P_D^{-1}K\), \(P_L^{-1}K\), and \(P_U^{-1}K\) are well-defined preconditioned block systems.

children.title: Schur-Complement Preconditioners
children.top_down_role: Preconditioners organized around exact or approximate Schur complements.

knowledge_statements.title: Schur-Complement Preconditioners
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact and approximate Schur factorizations for two-block Newton systems.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: If \(A\) is nonsingular, define the Schur complement \(S=D-CA^{-1}B\). Then \[K=\begin{pmatrix}A&0\\C&S\end{pmatrix}\begin{pmatrix}I&A^{-1}B\\0&I\end{pmatrix}.\] Replacing \(A\) and \(S\) by readily invertible nonsingular approximations \(\widehat A\) and \(\widehat S\) gives the lower-triangular Schur preconditioner \[P_S=\begin{pmatrix}\widehat A&0\\C&\widehat S\end{pmatrix}.\] Applying \(P_S^{-1}\) requires one solve with \(\widehat A\), one multiplication by \(C\), and one solve with \(\widehat S\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Eliminate the first block through its Schur complement, then replace the expensive block solves by tractable approximations.
assumptions_latex: \(K=\begin{pmatrix}A&B\\C&D\end{pmatrix}\) has conforming blocks.
\(A\), \(\widehat A\), and \(\widehat S\) are nonsingular.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(P_S^{-1}K\) is well defined, and exact choices \(\widehat A=A\), \(\widehat S=S\) reproduce the block factorization.

notation.meaning: Schur complement of the block A

children.title: Coupled-System Block Structure
children.top_down_role: Primal-dual or PDE block structures guiding preconditioner design.

knowledge_statements.title: Coupled-System Block Structure
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Active-set Newton equations partitioned into two coupled groups of unknowns.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: After ordering a Newton correction as \(d=(d_1,d_2)\), the coupled linearization is represented by \[\begin{pmatrix}A&B\\C&D\end{pmatrix}\begin{pmatrix}d_1\\d_2\end{pmatrix}=-\begin{pmatrix}r_1\\r_2\end{pmatrix}.\] If \(A\) is nonsingular, eliminating \(d_1\) yields \[(D-CA^{-1}B)d_2=-r_2+CA^{-1}r_1,\qquad d_1=-A^{-1}(r_1+Bd_2).\] The blocks may correspond to state-control, primal-multiplier, or active-free variables; the algebraic representation depends only on the chosen conforming partition.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Partitioning coupled Newton variables produces a two-by-two block system whose first block can be eliminated to obtain a reduced equation.
assumptions_latex: \(d_1\in\mathbb R^n\), \(d_2\in\mathbb R^m\), and all displayed blocks are conforming.
\(A\in\mathbb R^{n\times n}\) is nonsingular.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The full block system is equivalent to the displayed reduced equation and back-substitution formula.

notation.meaning: blocks of the coupled Newton matrix

children.title: Approximate-Schur Regimes
children.top_down_role: Accuracy and scalability regimes for approximate Schur components.

knowledge_statements.title: Approximate-Schur Regimes
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Spectral-equivalence regime ensuring a uniformly effective approximate Schur block.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(S,\widehat S\in\mathbb R^{q\times q}\) be symmetric positive definite Schur operators. The approximate-Schur regime holds when constants \(0<c\leq C<\infty\), independent of discretization size and the admissible active-set partition, satisfy \[c\,v^{T}\widehat S v\leq v^{T}Sv\leq C\,v^{T}\widehat S v\qquad\text{for every }v\in\mathbb R^q.\] Equivalently, all generalized eigenvalues of \(Sv=\lambda\widehat S v\), or all eigenvalues of \(\widehat S^{-1/2}S\widehat S^{-1/2}\), lie in \([c,C]\). Consequently, \(\kappa_2(\widehat S^{-1/2}S\widehat S^{-1/2})\leq C/c\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: An approximate Schur block is uniformly effective when its quadratic form is bounded above and below by the exact Schur form with uniform constants; the symmetrically preconditioned operator then has condition number at most the ratio of those constants.
assumptions_latex: \(S\) and \(\widehat S\) are symmetric positive definite on \(\mathbb R^q\).
\(c\) and \(C\) do not depend on mesh size or admissible active-set changes.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\sigma(\widehat S^{-1/2}S\widehat S^{-1/2})\subseteq[c,C]\) and \(\kappa_2(\widehat S^{-1/2}S\widehat S^{-1/2})\leq C/c\).

children.title: Factorization-Subspace Reuse Family
children.top_down_role: Reuse across locally stable or slowly changing active partitions.

children.title: Factorization Reuse
children.top_down_role: Reuse of matrix factorizations across related Newton systems.

knowledge_statements.title: Factorization Reuse
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Reuse of a Newton-matrix factorization while its retained blocks remain unchanged.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Given successive Newton systems \(J_kd_k=-F(x_k)\), compute and store a factorization \(P J_k Q=L_kU_k\) at a refresh iteration. At iteration \(k+1\), first test whether the matrix, or the designated reusable principal block, is unchanged within a prescribed tolerance. If so, solve using the stored factors, incorporating any supported low-rank update; otherwise refactor the changed matrix or block. Accept the computed correction only when \(\lVert F(x_{k+1})+J_{k+1}d_{k+1}\rVert\leq\eta_{k+1}\lVert F(x_{k+1})\rVert\), and output \(d_{k+1}\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Reuse stored matrix factors while the relevant Newton blocks remain stable; otherwise refresh them, and accept only a correction satisfying the linear residual tolerance.
assumptions_latex: \(J_k\) is nonsingular at every accepted iteration.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Every accepted reused-factor solve satisfies the prescribed inexact Newton residual test.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The algorithm fits factorization reuse, but the tolerance-based reuse test, supported low-rank updates, and refresh policy are specialized choices requiring a source.

children.title: Subspace Reuse
children.top_down_role: Reuse of iterative-solver or spectral subspaces across Newton solves.

knowledge_statements.title: Subspace Reuse
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Recycling selected Krylov directions between consecutive Newton linear systems.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For \(J_kd_k=b_k\), retain a basis \(U_{k-1}\in\mathbb R^{n\times p}\) from the preceding linear solve. Form an initial correction \(d_k^{(0)}=U_{k-1}y_k\), where \(y_k\) minimizes \(\lVert b_k-J_kU_{k-1}y\rVert_2\). Apply a projected Krylov iteration to the remaining residual, augmenting its search space by \(\operatorname{range}(U_{k-1})\). Stop when \(\lVert b_k-J_kd_k\rVert_2\leq\eta_k\lVert b_k\rVert_2\), then select well-conditioned approximate invariant or correction directions to form \(U_k\); discard the basis if the projected problem is singular or unstable.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Project the new Newton right-hand side onto a retained Krylov space, solve the remaining residual iteratively, and retain stable useful directions.
assumptions_latex: \(J_k\in\mathbb R^{n\times n}\) is nonsingular.
\(U_{k-1}\) has full column rank.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The output \(d_k\) satisfies \(\lVert b_k-J_kd_k\rVert_2\leq\eta_k\lVert b_k\rVert_2\).

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The algorithm broadly describes augmented Krylov recycling, but the projection, retained-direction selection, and instability test depend on a specific recycling method that is neither identified nor sourced.

children.title: Stable-Partition Reuse Regimes
children.top_down_role: Reuse opportunities created by locally stable active partitions.

knowledge_statements.title: Stable-Partition Reuse Regimes
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Quantitative regime in which active-free structure and Newton blocks change mildly.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(A_k\) and \(F_k\) be the active and free sets, and let \(J_k\) be the correspondingly ordered Newton matrix. A stable-partition reuse regime over iterations \(k\in I\) is characterized by \[A_{k+1}=A_k,\qquad F_{k+1}=F_k,\qquad \lVert M_k^{-1}(J_{k+1}-J_k)\rVert\leq\delta<1,\] where \(M_k\) is the reused nonsingular preconditioner or factored approximation. The last inequality implies that \(M_k^{-1}J_{k+1}\) differs from \(M_k^{-1}J_k\) by an operator of norm at most \(\delta\), providing an explicit admissibility test for reuse.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Reuse is admissible while the active-free partition is unchanged and the preconditioned Newton-matrix perturbation stays below a fixed threshold.
assumptions_latex: \(M_k\) is nonsingular for every \(k\in I\).
\(\lVert\cdot\rVert\) is a subordinate matrix norm.
\(0\leq\delta<1\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\lVert M_k^{-1}J_{k+1}-M_k^{-1}J_k\rVert\leq\delta\) throughout the reuse regime.

notation.meaning: active and free sets at iteration k

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The displayed perturbation identity is valid, but the threshold \(\delta<1\) alone does not establish effective or safe reuse relative to an arbitrary prior preconditioned system. The proposed admissibility regime needs additional hypotheses and a source.

children.title: Reuse-Invalidation Boundaries
children.top_down_role: Structural changes that make previously retained solver information unreliable.

knowledge_statements.title: Reuse-Invalidation Boundaries
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Events requiring refresh of reused factors, preconditioners, or recycled subspaces.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A reused solver object \(M_k\) is invalidated for the next Newton system whenever at least one monitored condition holds: \[A_{k+1}\neq A_k,\qquad M_k\text{ is singular},\qquad \lVert M_k^{-1}(J_{k+1}-J_k)\rVert>\delta,\qquad \lVert b_{k+1}-J_{k+1}d\rVert>\eta\lVert b_{k+1}\rVert\] after the permitted reused-solver work. At such a boundary, unchanged reuse supplies no admissibility certificate; the affected factorization, preconditioner blocks, or recycled subspace must be refreshed before the correction is accepted.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Partition changes, singularity, excessive matrix perturbation, or failure of the residual test invalidate unchanged reuse and require refresh.
assumptions_latex: \(J_{k+1}d=b_{k+1}\) is the new Newton system.
\(\delta\geq0\) and \(0\leq\eta<1\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Any displayed event rejects unchanged reuse of \(M_k\) for accepting the new correction.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The statement incorrectly treats factors, preconditioners, and recycled subspaces as one invertible matrix object and declares every active-set change a universal invalidation event. These solver objects have different validity boundaries, and a partition change need not invalidate a useful recycled subspace or preconditioner.

children.title: Computational Convergence Certificate System
children.top_down_role: Computable certificate families for equations, complementarity, active sets, and inexact solves.

children.title: Equation-Residual Certificates
children.top_down_role: Residual-based assessment for nonsmooth equation systems.

knowledge_statements.title: Equation-Residual Certificates
knowledge_statements.scope_note: A normwise, directly computable certificate for a nonsmooth equation.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(F:\mathbb R^n\to\mathbb R^m\) define the target equation \(F(x)=0\). For a computed point \(\widehat x\), the quantity \(\rho_F(\widehat x)=\lVert F(\widehat x)\rVert\) is an equation-residual certificate. Given absolute and relative tolerances \(\varepsilon_{\mathrm{abs}},\varepsilon_{\mathrm{rel}}\geq0\) and a fixed reference residual \(\rho_{\mathrm{ref}}>0\), the certificate passes when \[\rho_F(\widehat x)\leq\varepsilon_{\mathrm{abs}}+\varepsilon_{\mathrm{rel}}\rho_{\mathrm{ref}}.\] Exact vanishing, \(\rho_F(\widehat x)=0\), is equivalent to satisfaction of the equation.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Evaluate the nonsmooth equation at the computed point and compare its norm with combined absolute and relative tolerances.
assumptions_latex: \(F:\mathbb R^n\to\mathbb R^m\) is evaluable at \(\widehat x\).
\(\lVert\cdot\rVert\) is a norm on \(\mathbb R^m\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\rho_F(\widehat x)=0\iff F(\widehat x)=0\), and the displayed inequality certifies tolerance-level satisfaction.

children.title: Complementarity Certificates
children.top_down_role: Combined feasibility and complementarity assessment.

knowledge_statements.title: Complementarity Certificates
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Componentwise feasibility and complementarity residual for nonlinear complementarity systems.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For the nonlinear complementarity problem \(x\geq0\), \(G(x)\geq0\), and \(x_iG_i(x)=0\) for every \(i\), define \[\rho_{\mathrm{NCP}}(x)=\max\left\{\lVert(-x)_+\rVert_\infty,\ \lVert(-G(x))_+\rVert_\infty,\ \lVert x\odot G(x)\rVert_\infty\right\}.\] This quantity is directly computable. It vanishes exactly when primal nonnegativity, image nonnegativity, and componentwise complementarity all hold. Thus \(\rho_{\mathrm{NCP}}(x)\leq\varepsilon\) certifies simultaneous feasibility and complementarity to tolerance \(\varepsilon\geq0\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The maximum of primal infeasibility, image infeasibility, and complementarity-product residuals certifies an approximate nonlinear complementarity solution.
assumptions_latex: \(G:\mathbb R^n\to\mathbb R^n\) is evaluable at \(x\).
\(\varepsilon\geq0\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\rho_{\mathrm{NCP}}(x)=0\) if and only if \(x\geq0\), \(G(x)\geq0\), and \(x\odot G(x)=0\).

children.title: Active-Set Consistency Certificates
children.top_down_role: Assessment of stability and consistency of an identified activity pattern.

knowledge_statements.title: Active-Set Consistency Certificates
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Strict-separation certificate for a primal-dual complementarity active set.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Given \(0\leq\varepsilon_{\mathrm{act}}<\delta\), a partition \((A_k,I_k)\) is branch-consistent at \((x_k,\lambda_k)\) when \(x_{k,i}\leq\varepsilon_{\mathrm{act}}\) and \(\lambda_{k,i}\geq\delta\) for every \(i\in A_k\), while \(\lambda_{k,i}\leq\varepsilon_{\mathrm{act}}\) and \(x_{k,i}\geq\delta\) for every \(i\in I_k\). Define an index as active when \(x_i<\lambda_i\) and inactive when \(\lambda_i<x_i\). Then every perturbation satisfying \(\|\Delta x\|_\infty< (\delta-\varepsilon_{\mathrm{act}})/2\) and \(\|\Delta\lambda\|_\infty< (\delta-\varepsilon_{\mathrm{act}})/2\) preserves this branch classification.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Small designated components and a positive separation from their complementary components certify that the active/inactive ordering survives sufficiently small perturbations.
assumptions_latex: The iterate is a primal-dual pair \((x_k,\lambda_k)\in\mathbb{R}^n_+\times\mathbb{R}^n_+\).
The sets \(A_k\) and \(I_k\) form a disjoint partition of \(\{1,\ldots,n\}\).
The tolerances satisfy \(0\leq\varepsilon_{\mathrm{act}}<\delta\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The inequalities certify strict branch separation and robustness of the stated ordering-based classification.

notation.meaning: candidate active and inactive index sets

children.title: Inexact-Solve Certificates
children.top_down_role: Assessment of compatibility between approximate linear solves and the selected forcing regime.

assumptions_latex: The residual mapping is \(F:\mathbb{R}^n\to\mathbb{R}^n\), and \(V_k\) is the selected Newton derivative at \(x_k\).
The computed step \(s_k\) and linear residual \(r_k\) satisfy \(V_ks_k=-F(x_k)+r_k\).
The prescribed forcing number satisfies \(0\leq\eta_k<1\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The displayed residual inequality certifies that the approximate solve meets the selected forcing regime.

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For a computed step \(s_k\), form the independently evaluated residual \(r_k:=V_ks_k+F(x_k)\). If \(F(x_k)\neq0\), the inexact-solve certificate is \[\widehat\eta_k:=\frac{\|r_k\|}{\|F(x_k)\|}\leq\eta_k.\] If \(F(x_k)=0\), the nonlinear equation is already satisfied and no linear solve is required. The certificate is compatible with a constant forcing regime when \(\eta_k\leq\bar\eta<1\), with a superlinear regime when \(\eta_k\to0\), and with an order-preserving regime when \(\eta_k=O(\|F(x_k)\|^\alpha)\) for the relevant semismoothness order \(\alpha\in(0,1]\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: An approximate Newton step is certified when its independently recomputed linear residual does not exceed the prescribed fraction of the current nonlinear residual.

children.title: Convergence-Rate Diagnostics
children.top_down_role: Computable evidence concerning observed local or global convergence behavior.

knowledge_statements.title: Convergence-Rate Diagnostics
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Residual-based empirical diagnostics; these are observations, not standalone convergence proofs.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Define \(R_k:=\|F(x_k)\|\) and \(q_k:=R_{k+1}/R_k\) whenever \(R_k>0\). When \(R_{k-1},R_k,R_{k+1}>0\) and \(R_k\neq R_{k-1}\), define \[p_k:=\frac{\log(R_{k+1}/R_k)}{\log(R_k/R_{k-1})}.\] In an asymptotic regime, \(q_k\to q\in(0,1)\) diagnoses linear residual convergence with factor \(q\), while \(q_k\to0\) diagnoses superlinear residual convergence. If \(R_{k+1}=C R_k^p(1+o(1))\), \(R_k\to0\), and \(p>1\), then \(p_k\to p\) whenever the quotient is defined. Values near the rounding-error floor or spanning globalization transitions are excluded from the diagnostic window.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Successive positive-residual ratios diagnose linear versus superlinear behavior, while a well-defined three-residual logarithmic quotient estimates the local convergence order.
assumptions_latex: The residual mapping is \(F:\mathbb{R}^n\to\mathbb{R}^n\), and the sampled iterates are \(x_k\in\mathbb{R}^n\).
The residual values used in a quotient are positive.
At least three consecutive residual values are available for an order estimate.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The sequences \(q_k\) and \(p_k\), on their stated domains, diagnose observed linear, superlinear, and order-\(p\) residual convergence.

children.title: Termination-Decision Criteria
children.top_down_role: Cross-cutting criteria used to decide when nonlinear iteration may stop.

assumptions_latex: The implementation supplies tolerances \(\varepsilon_F,\varepsilon_C,\varepsilon_A,\varepsilon_L\geq0\).
The quantities \(R_F,R_C,R_A,R_L\) are independently evaluated nonlinear, complementarity, activity-consistency, and linear-solve residuals.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Termination is accepted exactly when all required residual and consistency tests meet their declared tolerances.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Composite stopping condition for a complementarity-oriented active-set Newton implementation.

source_refs.source_title: Finite-Dimensional Variational Inequalities and Complementarity Problems, Vol. II

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(R_F:=\|F(x_k)\|/s_F\), \(R_C:=\|\min(x_k,\lambda_k)\|_\infty/s_C\), let \(R_A\) be the maximum normalized active-set classification violation, and let \(R_L:=\|V_ks_k+F(x_k)\|/\max\{\|F(x_k)\|,s_L\}\), where \(s_F,s_C,s_L>0\) are fixed scaling quantities. Declare successful termination only if \[R_F\leq\varepsilon_F,\qquad R_C\leq\varepsilon_C,\qquad R_A\leq\varepsilon_A,\qquad R_L\leq\varepsilon_L.\] A separate failure exit is required when the iteration limit, nonfinite arithmetic, or an unrecoverable linear-solver failure occurs; such an exit is not a convergence certificate.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Successful termination requires simultaneous nonlinear, complementarity, active-set, and linear-solve tests; resource or arithmetic failures must be reported separately.

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Suppose \(\sigma_{\min}(V_k)\downarrow0\), equivalently \(\|V_k^{-1}\|_2\to\infty\) when \(\|V_k\|_2\) remains bounded. For the perturbed Newton equations \(V_ks_k=-F(x_k)+r_k\) and \(V_k\widetilde s_k=-F(x_k)+\widetilde r_k\), \[\|\widetilde s_k-s_k\|_2\leq\|V_k^{-1}\|_2\,\|\widetilde r_k-r_k\|_2.\] Moreover, perturbations aligned with a left singular vector for \(\sigma_{\min}(V_k)\) attain amplification \(1/\sigma_{\min}(V_k)\). Thus nonsingularity at every iteration alone does not provide a uniform numerical-stability or convergence boundary.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Even nonsingular Newton systems become unstable when their smallest singular values approach zero, because residual and rounding errors receive unbounded amplification.

children.title: Unstable Active-Set Reductions
children.top_down_role: Reduced systems destabilized by weakly determined activity patterns.

knowledge_statements.title: Unstable Active-Set Reductions
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Failure of stable reduction at weakly complementary indices under ordering-based branch selection.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: At a weakly complementary index \(j\), suppose the reduction selects the active branch when \(x_j<\lambda_j\) and the inactive branch when \(\lambda_j<x_j\), with either choice allowed at a tie. At \((x_j^*,\lambda_j^*)=(0,0)\), every neighborhood contains \((\epsilon,0)\) and \((0,\epsilon)\) for some \(\epsilon>0\), and these points select opposite branches. Thus no tie choice makes this discrete branch map locally constant at the solution. If the two branches induce different reduced Newton matrices, arbitrarily small iterate or rounding perturbations can switch the realized reduced system, so conditioning of either fixed reduction alone does not guarantee stability of the realized sequence.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: At a weakly complementary solution, an ordering-based branch rule can switch under arbitrarily small perturbations; if the branches produce different matrices, the realized reduced systems need not be stable.
assumptions_latex: The active-set reduction classifies each complementary pair by comparing \(x_i\) and \(\lambda_i\).
A limiting solution has an index \(j\) with \(x_j^*=\lambda_j^*=0\).
The two classifications at index \(j\) may induce different reduced Newton matrices.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Without a positive branch-separation margin, the classification is not locally stable and the realized reduced system may switch under arbitrarily small perturbations.

children.title: Inexact-Solve Compatibility
children.top_down_role: Approximate-solve regimes consistent with the intended nonlinear behavior.

knowledge_statements.title: Inexact-Solve Compatibility
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Local compatibility condition between linear residuals and nonlinear convergence.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(F:\mathbb{R}^n\to\mathbb{R}^n\) satisfy \(F(x^*)=0\), and let \(V_k\) be a selected generalized Newton matrix at \(x_k\). An approximate solve \(V_ks_k=-F(x_k)+r_k\) is locally forcing-compatible when \[\|r_k\|\leq\eta_k\|F(x_k)\|,\qquad 0\leq\eta_k\leq\bar\eta,\] where \(\bar\eta\) is below the contraction threshold determined by the local inverse and linearization bounds. Under local residual-error equivalence, a fixed admissible \(\bar\eta\) contributes a linear error term, while superlinear compatibility requires \(\eta_k\to0\). If the semismooth remainder has order \(1+\alpha\), preservation of that order requires \(\eta_k=O(\|F(x_k)\|^\alpha)\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The linear residual must remain below the local contraction threshold relative to the nonlinear residual; vanishing or order-matched forcing is required to preserve faster local convergence.
assumptions_latex: The mapping is \(F:\mathbb{R}^n\to\mathbb{R}^n\), with \(F(x^*)=0\), and is semismooth of order \(\alpha\in(0,1]\) near \(x^*\).
The matrices \(V_k\) are admissible generalized Newton matrices and are uniformly invertible near \(x^*\).
The nonlinear residual and iteration error are locally equivalent near \(x^*\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The residual bound is compatible with local contraction when \(\bar\eta\) is below the local threshold; superlinear and order-\(1+\alpha\) compatibility require the stated decay of \(\eta_k\).

children.title: Preconditioner Compatibility
children.top_down_role: Preconditioning regimes aligned with active Newton models and residual measures.

knowledge_statements.title: Preconditioner Compatibility
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Uniform norm-equivalence condition for left-preconditioned forcing tests.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(P_k\in\mathbb{R}^{n\times n}\) be nonsingular, \(r_k:=V_ks_k+F(x_k)\), and \(\rho_k:=P_k^{-1}r_k\). The left preconditioners are forcing-compatible when constants \(0<m\leq M<\infty\), independent of \(k\), satisfy \[m\|v\|_2\leq\|P_k^{-1}v\|_2\leq M\|v\|_2\qquad\text{for every }v\in\mathbb{R}^n.\] Then \(\|r_k\|_2\leq m^{-1}\|\rho_k\|_2\) and \(\|P_k^{-1}F(x_k)\|_2\leq M\|F(x_k)\|_2\). Consequently, a preconditioned relative-residual test implies an original-norm forcing test with factor at most \(M/m\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A left preconditioner is forcing-compatible when its residual norm is uniformly equivalent to the original norm, giving an iteration-independent conversion between their forcing tests.
assumptions_latex: Each left preconditioner \(P_k\in\mathbb{R}^{n\times n}\) is nonsingular.
Residuals are measured in the Euclidean norm.
The Newton equation is left-preconditioned as \(P_k^{-1}V_ks=-P_k^{-1}F(x_k)\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Uniform norm equivalence makes the preconditioned and original forcing tests quantitatively interchangeable with factor \(M/m\).

children.title: Forcing-Quality Distortion
children.top_down_role: Distortion of effective solve quality caused by incompatible scaling or preconditioning.

knowledge_statements.title: Forcing-Quality Distortion
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Worst-case distortion of a left-preconditioned relative residual test.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(P_k\in\mathbb{R}^{n\times n}\) be nonsingular, let \(F(x_k)\neq0\), and define \(r_k:=V_ks_k+F(x_k)\) and \(\rho_k:=P_k^{-1}r_k\). If the inner solver enforces \(\|\rho_k\|_2\leq\widehat\eta_k\|P_k^{-1}F(x_k)\|_2\), then \[\eta_k^{\mathrm{eff}}:=\frac{\|r_k\|_2}{\|F(x_k)\|_2}\leq\|P_k\|_2\|P_k^{-1}\|_2\widehat\eta_k=\kappa_2(P_k)\widehat\eta_k.\] Thus a small \(\widehat\eta_k\) need not imply a small original residual when \(\kappa_2(P_k)\) is large. In particular, \(\widehat\eta_k\to0\) does not by itself imply \(\eta_k^{\mathrm{eff}}\to0\); the sufficient bound additionally requires \(\kappa_2(P_k)\widehat\eta_k\to0\), unless a sharper residual-space estimate is available.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: An ill-conditioned left preconditioner can inflate the effective original-norm forcing number, so a vanishing preconditioned tolerance alone need not certify a vanishing original residual.
assumptions_latex: Each \(P_k\in\mathbb{R}^{n\times n}\) is nonsingular.
The nonlinear residual satisfies \(F(x_k)\neq0\) whenever the relative forcing number is evaluated.
The inner solver enforces \(\|P_k^{-1}r_k\|_2\leq\widehat\eta_k\|P_k^{-1}F(x_k)\|_2\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The effective original-norm forcing number is bounded by \(\kappa_2(P_k)\widehat\eta_k\), so poor preconditioner conditioning can distort the reported solve quality.

notation.meaning: effective forcing number in the original norm

children.title: Nonlinear-Convergence Degradation
children.top_down_role: Loss of expected nonlinear progress under incompatible approximate solves.

knowledge_statements.title: Nonlinear-Convergence Degradation
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Local error-recursion boundary for inexact semismooth Newton steps.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(e_k:=x_k-x^*\), let \(x_{k+1}=x_k+s_k\), and suppose \(V_ks_k=-F(x_k)+r_k\) with \(\|r_k\|\leq\eta_k\|F(x_k)\|\). Under the stated semismoothness, uniform-invertibility, and local residual-error assumptions, constants \(C_1,C_2>0\) exist such that, for all sufficiently large \(k\), \[\|e_{k+1}\|\leq C_1\|e_k\|^{1+\alpha}+C_2\eta_k\|e_k\|.\] A fixed admissible forcing bound generally leaves a linear term. If \(\eta_k\to0\), the forcing contribution is superlinear; if \(\eta_k=O(\|e_k\|^\alpha)\), order \(1+\alpha\) is retained. If \(C_2\eta_k\geq1\) along a subsequence, this bound no longer certifies contraction along that subsequence.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The local error recursion shows that fixed forcing generally limits the guaranteed rate to linear, vanishing forcing permits superlinear behavior, order-matched forcing retains the semismooth order, and excessive forcing removes the contraction guarantee.
assumptions_latex: The mapping is \(F:\mathbb{R}^n\to\mathbb{R}^n\), satisfies \(F(x^*)=0\), and is semismooth of order \(\alpha\in(0,1]\) near \(x^*\).
Each \(V_k\) is an admissible generalized Newton matrix for \(F\) at \(x_k\), and the selected matrices are uniformly invertible near \(x^*\).
The nonlinear residual obeys a local bound \(\|F(x_k)\|\leq L\|x_k-x^*\|\) for some \(L>0\).
The iteration uses \(x_{k+1}=x_k+s_k\) and \(V_ks_k=-F(x_k)+r_k\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Nonvanishing or distorted forcing terms reduce the locally guaranteed convergence order and remove the contraction guarantee when their coefficient is too large.
